undetected_forms.text: a context that cannot hold a line break, written after the = of a line or in the body of name<<DELIM: a SHA, a number, a date, the name of an account, a repository or a branch, the description of a fork (github.event.forkee.description), a URL (before the =, any value an attacker controls is reported)

examples.name: no-line-break.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on pull_request_target, workflow_run, merge_group, fork, and
#   issues and discussion transferred, runs write branches' names, a number
#   and a SHA after the = of lines of $GITHUB_ENV. issues and discussion run only
#   when transferred: changes.new_repository is in the payload of that
#   action alone.
# reason: no added gain: a branch's name cannot hold a line break: "They
#   cannot have ASCII control characters (i.e. bytes whose values are lower
#   than \040, or \177 DEL)" (git-check-ref-format, git v2.51.0). The second
#   step is the form of GHSL-2025-105 (vets-api,
#   https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-105_vets-api/),
#   which the advisory reports as code injection: code-injection reports it.
# cause: the rule's table of contexts reads the branches' names as
#   structured (an attacker shapes them within a form without line breaks)
#   and the number and the SHA as fixed. A fixed value is not taken as an
#   attacker's, and a structured one not as written with line breaks; after
#   the =, the rule reports only a value written with line breaks.
# attack-value: github.event.workflow_run.head_branch = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: were a branch so named, the second step's script
#   would become echo "pr_branch=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> $GITHUB_ENV, which
#   appends pr_branch=x and PWNED=1, and the runner would set PWNED to 1.
#   git and GitHub refuse a branch whose name has a line break, so
#   head_branch never holds this value.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-105_vets-api/
on:
  pull_request_target:
  workflow_run:
  merge_group:
  fork:
  issues:
    types: [transferred]
  discussion:
    types: [transferred]
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "h=${{ github.head_ref }} n=${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} s=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - run: echo "pr_branch=${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - run: |
          echo "a=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "b=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.label }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "c=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "d=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.label }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "e=${{ github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].head.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "f=${{ github.event.workflow_run.pull_requests[0].base.ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "g=${{ github.event.workflow_run.referenced_workflows[0].ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "h=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "i=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.repo.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "j=${{ github.event.forkee.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "k=${{ github.event.changes.new_repository.default_branch }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "m=${{ github.event.merge_group.head_ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "n=${{ github.event.merge_group.base_ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on pull_request_target, workflow_run, merge_group, fork, and issues and discussion transferred, runs write branches' names, a number and a SHA after the = of lines of $GITHUB_ENV. issues and discussion run only when transferred: changes.new_repository is in the payload of that action alone.
notes.reason: no added gain: a branch's name cannot hold a line break: "They cannot have ASCII control characters (i.e. bytes whose values are lower than \040, or \177 DEL)" (git-check-ref-format, git v2.51.0). The second step is the form of GHSL-2025-105 (vets-api, https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-105_vets-api/), which the advisory reports as code injection: code-injection reports it.
notes.cause: the rule's table of contexts reads the branches' names as structured (an attacker shapes them within a form without line breaks) and the number and the SHA as fixed. A fixed value is not taken as an attacker's, and a structured one not as written with line breaks; after the =, the rule reports only a value written with line breaks.
notes.attack_run_behavior: were a branch so named, the second step's script would become echo "pr_branch=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> $GITHUB_ENV, which appends pr_branch=x and PWNED=1, and the runner would set PWNED to 1. git and GitHub refuse a branch whose name has a line break, so head_branch never holds this value.

undetected_forms.text: a value written through $( ) whose pipeline starts with echo or printf '%s' of it and ends with tr -d with \n in the set, or tr turning \n into another byte

examples.name: line-free.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV through
#   $( ) whose pipeline ends with tr -d '\n'.
# reason: no added gain: the line breaks are taken out, so the value is one
#   line.
# cause: the rule reads such a pipeline as taking the line breaks out.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: echo "$B" | tr -d '\n' prints xPWNED=1, so echo
#   appends the one line b=xPWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets b to
#   xPWNED=1, and no variable PWNED, with any body.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "b=$(echo "$B" | tr -d '\n')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV through $( ) whose pipeline ends with tr -d '\n'.
notes.reason: no added gain: the line breaks are taken out, so the value is one line.
notes.cause: the rule reads such a pipeline as taking the line breaks out.
notes.attack_run_behavior: echo "$B" | tr -d '\n' prints xPWNED=1, so echo appends the one line b=xPWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets b to xPWNED=1, and no variable PWNED, with any body.

undetected_forms.text: the body of name<<DELIM whose delimiter is $GHA_DELIM, set before it to ghadelimiter_ and 16 random bytes in hex as the fix writes it

examples.name: random-delimiter.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV in
#   b<<DELIM, whose delimiter is ghadelimiter_ and 16 random bytes in hex.
# reason: no added gain: the attacker cannot write the delimiter.
# cause: the rule reads the delimiter of its own fix's form as random.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nghadelimiter_00000000000000000000000000000000\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the body guesses the delimiter as ghadelimiter_ and
#   32 zeros; GHA_DELIM is ghadelimiter_ and 32 hex digits from
#   /dev/urandom, so the guess is not the delimiter (but by a chance of 1 in
#   2^128), and the runner reads the body's three lines as the value of b,
#   up to the line GHA_DELIM, and sets no variable PWNED.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          GHA_DELIM="ghadelimiter_$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"; { echo "b<<${GHA_DELIM}"; echo "$B"; echo "${GHA_DELIM}"; } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV in b<<DELIM, whose delimiter is ghadelimiter_ and 16 random bytes in hex.
notes.reason: no added gain: the attacker cannot write the delimiter.
notes.cause: the rule reads the delimiter of its own fix's form as random.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the body guesses the delimiter as ghadelimiter_ and 32 zeros; GHA_DELIM is ghadelimiter_ and 32 hex digits from /dev/urandom, so the guess is not the delimiter (but by a chance of 1 in 2^128), and the runner reads the body's three lines as the value of b, up to the line GHA_DELIM, and sets no variable PWNED.

undetected_forms.text: a shell variable no env of the workflow sets: one the script sets (from a file, an artifact, an API), a positional parameter of a function the script calls with the value, or the runner

examples.name: script-var.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on workflow_run, a run writes to $GITHUB_ENV a value from a
#   file of an artifact through a variable the script sets, the form of
#   Feign's comment-pr.yml (GHSL-2024-173,
#   https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-173_Feign/); another
#   writes a commit message through a positional parameter of a function and
#   an indirection the script sets.
# reason: a todo (the same file): following the variables of the script
#   would find it.
# cause: the value goes through a variable the script sets, which the rule
#   does not follow.
# attack-value: the file pr_number.txt of the artifact pr_number = "111\nLD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/feign/feign/inject.so\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value is that of GHSL-2024-173's PoC, with the
#   line PWNED=1 added. PR_NUMBER=$(cat pr_number.txt) holds its three
#   lines, and echo appends PR_NUMBER=111,
#   LD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/feign/feign/inject.so and PWNED=1 to
#   $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets the three, and a program a later step
#   starts, such as node, loads inject.so from the artifact.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-173_Feign/
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["receive-pr"]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pr_number
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
      - run: |
          PR_NUMBER=$(cat pr_number.txt)
          echo "PR_NUMBER=$PR_NUMBER" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      # a positional parameter of a function the script calls with the value
      - env:
          T: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          f() { echo "a=$1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"; }
          f "$T"
          # the indirection names T through X, which the script sets
          X=T
          echo "a=${!X}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on workflow_run, a run writes to $GITHUB_ENV a value from a file of an artifact through a variable the script sets, the form of Feign's comment-pr.yml (GHSL-2024-173, https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2024-173_Feign/); another writes a commit message through a positional parameter of a function and an indirection the script sets.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): following the variables of the script would find it.
notes.cause: the value goes through a variable the script sets, which the rule does not follow.

attack_value.carrier: the file pr_number.txt of the artifact pr_number

notes.attack_run_behavior: the value is that of GHSL-2024-173's PoC, with the line PWNED=1 added. PR_NUMBER=$(cat pr_number.txt) holds its three lines, and echo appends PR_NUMBER=111, LD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/feign/feign/inject.so and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets the three, and a program a later step starts, such as node, loads inject.so from the artifact.

undetected_forms.text: what another shell or program the script starts writes to the environment file, from its code (eval; bash -c and sh -c whose code is not one word in single quotes, or whose code reads the arguments after it as $1 and the like, or whose -c comes after an option of the shell the rule does not read, or whose code reads a variable the script assigns before the command (T="pre-$T"; bash -c '...'): one word in single quotes is read as a script of its own) or from the environment it reads itself (python -c and the like)

examples.name: nested-shell.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_ENV
#   through eval, bash -c and python -c.
# reason: a todo (the same file): reading what another shell or program
#   writes to the environment file would find it.
# cause: the tree does not read the code of eval, nor that of bash -c
#   written as two words in single quotes, and python reads the value from
#   its environment itself.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: eval runs echo "a=$T", bash -c runs it with T from
#   its environment, and python prints a= and T, each appending a=x and
#   PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets a to x and PWNED to 1 (three
#   times).
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          T: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          eval 'echo "a=$T" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"'
          bash -c 'echo "a=$T"'' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"'
          python3 -c 'import os; print("a=" + os.environ["T"])' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_ENV through eval, bash -c and python -c.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): reading what another shell or program writes to the environment file would find it.
notes.cause: the tree does not read the code of eval, nor that of bash -c written as two words in single quotes, and python reads the value from its environment itself.
notes.attack_run_behavior: eval runs echo "a=$T", bash -c runs it with T from its environment, and python prints a= and T, each appending a=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets a to x and PWNED to 1 (three times).

undetected_forms.text: an assignment or an exec in the last command of a pipeline after a shopt -s lastpipe whose option name the script does not write as a literal word (shopt -s "$o"): bash runs the last command of the pipeline in the shell that runs the pipeline, so the assignment or the exec stays after the pipeline, and the rule reads the last command as a command in a subshell

examples.name: lastpipe-not-literal.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step turns lastpipe on with shopt -s and
#   the option name in a variable, sets out to $GITHUB_ENV in the last command
#   of a pipeline, and writes V=$V to "$out".
# reason: a todo (the same file): with lastpipe, bash runs the last command
#   of the pipeline in the shell itself, so out stays $GITHUB_ENV after the
#   pipeline and the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
# cause: the rule follows lastpipe only after shopt -s lastpipe written as
#   literal words, and reads the last command as a command in a subshell.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          o=lastpipe
          shopt -s "$o"
          true | out=$GITHUB_ENV
          echo "V=$V" >> "$out"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step turns lastpipe on with shopt -s and the option name in a variable, sets out to $GITHUB_ENV in the last command of a pipeline, and writes V=$V to "$out".
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): with lastpipe, bash runs the last command of the pipeline in the shell itself, so out stays $GITHUB_ENV after the pipeline and the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.cause: the rule follows lastpipe only after shopt -s lastpipe written as literal words, and reads the last command as a command in a subshell.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.

undetected_forms.text: an assignment whose variable name the script does not write as a literal word (n=key; declare "$n=$X"; or read -r "$n"): bash assigns the word after = (with declare) or the line that read reads (with read) to the variable whose name is the value of n, and the rule does not read the assignment

examples.name: name-not-literal.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step sets n to the name out, assigns
#   $GITHUB_ENV to the variable that n names with declare, and writes
#   V=$V to "$out".
# reason: a todo (the same file): bash assigns $GITHUB_ENV to out, so
#   the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
# cause: the variable name of the assignment is not a literal word, so the
#   rule does not read the assignment.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          n=out
          declare "$n=$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "V=$V" >> "$out"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step sets n to the name out, assigns $GITHUB_ENV to the variable that n names with declare, and writes V=$V to "$out".
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): bash assigns $GITHUB_ENV to out, so the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.cause: the variable name of the assignment is not a literal word, so the rule does not read the assignment.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.

undetected_forms.text: a variable that a shell function unsets inside a recursive call of a function, where a function between the two calls made the variable local (f() { if [ -z "$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }; h() { s=x; local s=y; f; }; g() { unset s; }): bash takes away the local of the nearest calling function that made the variable local, and the variable then holds the value from before the nearest calling function made the variable local; the rule reads the recursive call where the first call of the function runs, without the calls in between, and does not read the value that the unset reveals

examples.name: recursive-unset-local.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step defines f, which calls h on the first
#   call of f and calls g on the second call of f; h sets out to $GITHUB_ENV,
#   makes out local with /dev/null, and calls f. g unsets out and writes V=
#   and "$V" to the file in "$out".
# reason: a todo (the same file): in the second call of f, the unset in g
#   takes away the local that h made, and out holds the value that h set
#   before h made out local: $GITHUB_ENV, which gets the issue's body.
# cause: the rule reads the second call of f, which f makes through h, where
#   the first call of f runs, without the call of h, so the rule does not read
#   the value that the unset reveals.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the runner sets PWNED for the steps after the step.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          f() { if [ -z "$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }
          g() { unset out; echo "V=$V" >> "$out"; }
          h() { out="$GITHUB_ENV"; local out=/dev/null; f; }
          f

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step defines f, which calls h on the first call of f and calls g on the second call of f; h sets out to $GITHUB_ENV, makes out local with /dev/null, and calls f. g unsets out and writes V= and "$V" to the file in "$out".
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): in the second call of f, the unset in g takes away the local that h made, and out holds the value that h set before h made out local: $GITHUB_ENV, which gets the issue's body.
notes.cause: the rule reads the second call of f, which f makes through h, where the first call of f runs, without the call of h, so the rule does not read the value that the unset reveals.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the runner sets PWNED for the steps after the step.

undetected_forms.text: a variable that a shell function unsets after a calling function made the variable local, when an assignment to the variable or a second unset of the variable follows the unset (s=x; reset() { unset s; }; point() { local s=y; reset; s=z; }; point): bash takes away the local of the calling function, so that the assignment after the unset sets the variable outside the calling function, and a second unset takes away the local of the next calling function or unsets the variable outside the functions; the rule keeps the local of the calling function after the unset, gives the variable back the value from before the calling function made the variable local when the calling function returns, and reads the second unset as the first unset

examples.name: unset-caller-local.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to /dev/null and defines reset,
#   which unsets out; point makes out local with /dev/null, calls reset, and
#   sets out to $GITHUB_ENV. The step calls point and then writes V= and "$V"
#   to the file in "$out".
# reason: a todo (the same file): the unset in reset takes away the local that
#   point made, so the assignment in point after reset sets the out of the
#   step: $GITHUB_ENV, which gets the issue's body.
# cause: the rule keeps the local of point after the unset in reset, and gives
#   out back /dev/null when point returns, so the rule does not read the value
#   that point set after reset.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the runner sets PWNED for the steps after the step.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          out=/dev/null
          reset() { unset out; }
          point() { local out=/dev/null; reset; out="$GITHUB_ENV"; }
          point
          echo "V=$V" >> "$out"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to /dev/null and defines reset, which unsets out; point makes out local with /dev/null, calls reset, and sets out to $GITHUB_ENV. The step calls point and then writes V= and "$V" to the file in "$out".
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): the unset in reset takes away the local that point made, so the assignment in point after reset sets the out of the step: $GITHUB_ENV, which gets the issue's body.
notes.cause: the rule keeps the local of point after the unset in reset, and gives out back /dev/null when point returns, so the rule does not read the value that point set after reset.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the runner sets PWNED for the steps after the step.

undetected_forms.text: tee run through another command or by its path (sudo tee, command tee, /usr/bin/tee): the rule reads tee by its name alone

examples.name: wrapped-tee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_ENV by
#   sudo tee, command tee and /usr/bin/tee.
# reason: a todo (the same file): reading tee through another command or by
#   its path would find it.
# cause: the rule reads tee by its name alone.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: each echo prints a=x and PWNED=1, and sudo tee,
#   command tee and /usr/bin/tee each append them to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner
#   sets a to x and PWNED to 1.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          T: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          echo "a=$T" | sudo tee -a "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "a=$T" | command tee -a "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "a=$T" | /usr/bin/tee -a "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_ENV by sudo tee, command tee and /usr/bin/tee.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): reading tee through another command or by its path would find it.
notes.cause: the rule reads tee by its name alone.
notes.attack_run_behavior: each echo prints a=x and PWNED=1, and sudo tee, command tee and /usr/bin/tee each append them to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets a to x and PWNED to 1.

undetected_forms.text: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('[...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, _, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space. The if of the job limits the value in every step of the job, and the if of a step with a run: script limits the value in that step only. In those steps the value equals one of the strings when the case of the letters is ignored, so the rule does not report the value. The attacker still chooses the case of each letter of the value. GitHub's server, which evaluates the if of a job, also takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k and the long s as equal to the letter s; the runner, which evaluates the if of a step, takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k. Where the case of a letter changes what the value names, such as a command, a variable, a file on a file system that tells names apart by their case (the default file system of a Linux runner), a host or a tool, the choice of the case can cause harm

examples.name: if-compared.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
#   bash_env, and a step writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the name
#   of the variable, the part of a line of $GITHUB_ENV before the =.
# reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string bash_env, ignoring
#   the case of its letters, so the body has no line break; the attacker
#   still chooses the case, and BASH_ENV is the variable whose file bash
#   reads before each later script.
# cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares
#   with such a string as written by the attacker.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "BASH_ENV"
# attack-run-behavior: the if passes, and the step writes the line
#   BASH_ENV=./setup.sh to $GITHUB_ENV.
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
jobs:
  j:
    if: github.event.comment.body == 'bash_env'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}=./setup.sh" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is bash_env, and a step writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the name of the variable, the part of a line of $GITHUB_ENV before the =.
notes.reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string bash_env, ignoring the case of its letters, so the body has no line break; the attacker still chooses the case, and BASH_ENV is the variable whose file bash reads before each later script.
notes.cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares with such a string as written by the attacker.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the if passes, and the step writes the line BASH_ENV=./setup.sh to $GITHUB_ENV.

undetected_forms.text: a run of pwsh, cmd or python, and a run whose shell the rule cannot determine to be bash or sh: a shell: value whose command is not bash or sh, such as pwsh -File {0}; a shell: value of bash or sh with an option that the rule does not read, such as bash -c 'make' {0}, bash -v {0} or bash -O extglob {0}; a shell: value that names bash or sh by a path, such as /usr/bin/bash -e {0}, on a runner where the rule does not know that the path exists (any runner other than one whose runs-on is a single label that starts with ubuntu-, or with macos- for /bin/bash and /bin/sh) or in a step of a composite action; a shell: that is an expression; or a step without shell: whose job and workflow have no defaults.run.shell and whose job has a runs-on that is not a single label that starts with ubuntu-, macos- or windows-, such as self-hosted or an expression: the rule reads the runs of bash and sh only

examples.name: other-shell.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run of pwsh writes the issue's body to
#   $GITHUB_ENV.
# reason: a todo (the same file): reading pwsh would find it.
# cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: pwsh's echo writes b=x, a line break and PWNED=1 to
#   $GITHUB_ENV, appending the lines b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x
#   and PWNED to 1.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: pwsh
        env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "b=$env:B" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV

notes.situation: on issues, a run of pwsh writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): reading pwsh would find it.
notes.cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
notes.attack_run_behavior: pwsh's echo writes b=x, a line break and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, appending the lines b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x and PWNED to 1.

examples.name: other-shell.pwsh-expression.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run of pwsh writes the issue's body to
#   $GITHUB_ENV with a ${{ }} in the script.
# reason: reading pwsh would find the write to $GITHUB_ENV. code-injection
#   reports the ${{ }}, and the fix of the step reads $env:ISSUE_BODY in
#   place of the ${{ }}. The fix of the step does not take the line breaks
#   out of the issue's body, because no rule reports the write to
#   $GITHUB_ENV in a run of pwsh, so the run after the fix still writes the
#   line breaks of the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV.
# cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: pwsh's echo writes b=x, a line break and PWNED=1 to
#   $GITHUB_ENV, appending the lines b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x
#   and PWNED to 1.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: pwsh
        run: echo "b=${{ github.event.issue.body }}" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV

notes.situation: on issues, a run of pwsh writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV with a ${{ }} in the script.
notes.reason: reading pwsh would find the write to $GITHUB_ENV. code-injection reports the ${{ }}, and the fix of the step reads $env:ISSUE_BODY in place of the ${{ }}. The fix of the step does not take the line breaks out of the issue's body, because no rule reports the write to $GITHUB_ENV in a run of pwsh, so the run after the fix still writes the line breaks of the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.cause: the rule reads runs of bash and sh only.
notes.attack_run_behavior: pwsh's echo writes b=x, a line break and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, appending the lines b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x and PWNED to 1.

undetected_forms.text: core.exportVariable and core.setOutput of actions/github-script: @actions/core writes a random delimiter, and refuses a value that has it

examples.name: github-script.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, actions/github-script calls core.exportVariable with
#   the issue's body.
# reason: no added gain: @actions/core writes a random delimiter, and
#   refuses a value that has it.
# cause: the rule does not read JavaScript.
# attack-value: the issue's body, which the script reads as context.payload.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: core.exportVariable appends B<<ghadelimiter_<a random
#   UUID>, x, PWNED=1 and the delimiter to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets
#   B to x, a line break and PWNED=1, and no variable PWNED; a body with the
#   delimiter's line in it makes exportVariable throw instead.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: core.exportVariable('B', context.payload.issue.body)

notes.situation: on issues, actions/github-script calls core.exportVariable with the issue's body.
notes.reason: no added gain: @actions/core writes a random delimiter, and refuses a value that has it.
notes.cause: the rule does not read JavaScript.

attack_value.carrier: the issue's body, which the script reads as context.payload.issue.body

notes.attack_run_behavior: core.exportVariable appends B<<ghadelimiter_<a random UUID>, x, PWNED=1 and the delimiter to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets B to x, a line break and PWNED=1, and no variable PWNED; a body with the delimiter's line in it makes exportVariable throw instead.

undetected_forms.text: a value written to the file $GITHUB_STATE, which the post step of a JavaScript action reads

examples.name: other-file.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_STATE.
# reason: no added gain: $GITHUB_STATE is a file that the
#   post step of a JavaScript action reads.
# cause: the rule reads writes to $GITHUB_ENV only.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: echo appends b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_STATE, and
#   the runner keeps them as the state b and PWNED, which the post steps of
#   the job's actions get as STATE_b and STATE_PWNED; nothing is written to
#   $GITHUB_ENV, and no variable PWNED is set.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "b=$B" >> "$GITHUB_STATE"

notes.situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_STATE.
notes.reason: no added gain: $GITHUB_STATE is a file that the post step of a JavaScript action reads.
notes.cause: the rule reads writes to $GITHUB_ENV only.
notes.attack_run_behavior: echo appends b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_STATE, and the runner keeps them as the state b and PWNED, which the post steps of the job's actions get as STATE_b and STATE_PWNED; nothing is written to $GITHUB_ENV, and no variable PWNED is set.

undetected_forms.text: a write to the environment file, or an exec (the builtin of the shell) that opens the environment file, inside an arm of a case statement of the shell: the rule finds the case statement and does not read the commands in the arms of the case statement

examples.name: case-arm.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step writes BODY= and the issue's body to
#   $GITHUB_ENV inside an arm of a case that skips an empty value.
# reason: a todo (the same file): the arm runs, and each later line of the
#   body such as NAME=value sets an environment variable of the steps after
#   it.
# cause: the shell parser does not read the commands of a case.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value is not empty, so the case takes its
#   second arm, and echo writes the lines BODY=x and PWNED=1 to
#   $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets BODY and PWNED for the steps after it.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          case "$V" in
            "") ;;
            *) echo "BODY=$V" >> "$GITHUB_ENV" ;;
          esac

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step writes BODY= and the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV inside an arm of a case that skips an empty value.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): the arm runs, and each later line of the body such as NAME=value sets an environment variable of the steps after it.
notes.cause: the shell parser does not read the commands of a case.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value is not empty, so the case takes its second arm, and echo writes the lines BODY=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets BODY and PWNED for the steps after it.

undetected_forms.text: the content of a file that a command of the script writes into $GITHUB_ENV by printing the file, not through a shell variable (cat values.txt >> $GITHUB_ENV, tee -a $GITHUB_ENV < values.txt, or the content passed through sed or tr between the file and $GITHUB_ENV), such as a file of an artifact that was uploaded by a run that an attacker started: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where the file comes from (the step that downloads the file)

examples.name: file-content.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on workflow_run, the script of a step copies into $GITHUB_ENV, with
#   cat, the content of a file of an artifact that was uploaded by the run
#   that triggered the workflow, by printing the file, not through a shell
#   variable.
# reason: a todo (the same file): reading, in the workflow, the command that
#   copies the file and the step that downloads the file would find it.
#   artifact-poisoning reports the download of the artifact, and this rule
#   reports nothing.
# cause: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where
#   the file comes from (the step that downloads the file).
# attack-value: the file values.txt of the artifact values = "A=1\nLD_PRELOAD=/home/runner/work/r/r/inject.so\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: download-artifact puts values.txt in the workspace, and cat appends
#   the three lines of values.txt to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets A,
#   LD_PRELOAD and PWNED for the steps after the step of cat; the artifact
#   also holds inject.so, which download-artifact puts in the workspace too,
#   and a program that a later step starts loads that inject.so.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["receive-pr"]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: values
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
      - run: cat values.txt >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on workflow_run, the script of a step copies into $GITHUB_ENV, with cat, the content of a file of an artifact that was uploaded by the run that triggered the workflow, by printing the file, not through a shell variable.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): reading, in the workflow, the command that copies the file and the step that downloads the file would find it. artifact-poisoning reports the download of the artifact, and this rule reports nothing.
notes.cause: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where the file comes from (the step that downloads the file).

attack_value.carrier: the file values.txt of the artifact values

notes.attack_run_behavior: download-artifact puts values.txt in the workspace, and cat appends the three lines of values.txt to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets A, LD_PRELOAD and PWNED for the steps after the step of cat; the artifact also holds inject.so, which download-artifact puts in the workspace too, and a program that a later step starts loads that inject.so.

undetected_forms.text: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/<n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request

examples.name: fork-review.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body to
#   $GITHUB_ENV, in a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
#   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
#   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
#   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
#   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
# cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
#   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
#   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "x\nNODE_OPTIONS=--require=/tmp/PWNED.js"
# attack-run-behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull
#   request of another person from a fork starts the job a; the line after
#   the line break sets NODE_OPTIONS for the later steps of the job.
on: pull_request_review_comment
jobs:
  a:
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: echo "body=$B" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body to $GITHUB_ENV, in a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
notes.cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull request of another person from a fork starts the job a; the line after the line break sets NODE_OPTIONS for the later steps of the job.

undetected_forms.text: a write by a function that the script defines before an exec that points the standard output to $GITHUB_ENV, and that the script calls after the exec (f() { echo "V=$V"; }; exec >>"$GITHUB_ENV"; f): bash writes what the body of the function prints to $GITHUB_ENV; the rule reads the commands that run after the exec by the place of each command in the text of the script, and does not read the body of the function, which comes before the exec in the text, as a command that runs after the exec

examples.name: call-after-exec.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step defines a function f that writes V=
#   and the issue's body to its standard output, points the standard output
#   of the script to $GITHUB_ENV with exec, and calls f.
# reason: a todo (the same file): f runs after the exec, so the body goes
#   to $GITHUB_ENV.
# cause: the rule reads the commands that run after the exec by their place
#   in the text of the script, and the body of f comes before the exec.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          f() { echo "V=$V"; }
          exec >>"$GITHUB_ENV"
          f

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step defines a function f that writes V= and the issue's body to its standard output, points the standard output of the script to $GITHUB_ENV with exec, and calls f.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): f runs after the exec, so the body goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.cause: the rule reads the commands that run after the exec by their place in the text of the script, and the body of f comes before the exec.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.

undetected_forms.text: a print inside a $( ) with a redirect that duplicates file descriptor 0 or file descriptor 2, where the script closed that file descriptor before the $( ) and bash places an end of the pipe of the $( ) on that file descriptor (exec 2>&-; echo "$( echo "V=$V" >>"$GITHUB_ENV" 3>&2 )"): bash opens the pipe of the $( ) on the lowest closed file descriptors and does not close an end of the pipe that is file descriptor 0, 1 or 2 inside the $( ), so the redirect that duplicates the file descriptor does not fail and bash runs the print; the rule reads file descriptor 0 or file descriptor 2 inside the $( ) as closed, and reads the print as a command that bash does not run because the redirect that duplicates the file descriptor fails

examples.name: substitution-pipe-end.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step closes the standard error, and inside
#   a $( ) appends V= and the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV with a redirect
#   that duplicates descriptor 2 to descriptor 3.
# reason: a todo (the same file): bash opens the pipe of the $( ) on the
#   lowest closed descriptors, so descriptor 2 inside the $( ) is the end of
#   the pipe that reads; the duplicate does not fail, and the body goes to
#   $GITHUB_ENV.
# cause: the rule reads descriptor 2 inside the $( ) as closed, and reads
#   the echo as a command that bash does not run.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          exec 2>&-
          echo "$( echo "V=$V" >>"$GITHUB_ENV" 3>&2 )"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step closes the standard error, and inside a $( ) appends V= and the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV with a redirect that duplicates descriptor 2 to descriptor 3.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): bash opens the pipe of the $( ) on the lowest closed descriptors, so descriptor 2 inside the $( ) is the end of the pipe that reads; the duplicate does not fail, and the body goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.cause: the rule reads descriptor 2 inside the $( ) as closed, and reads the echo as a command that bash does not run.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.

undetected_forms.text: an if that lets in MEMBER or COLLABORATOR by the author_association of the issue, the pull request or the discussion the run is of, which the following pass: a member or a collaborator whose repository role is Read only, who gets, in the run, a token that writes and the secrets, more than what the Read role gives; the account of such a member or collaborator, taken over; and an outsider who becomes a MEMBER with the Read role, in an organization that lets anyone become a member (a bot that invites whoever asks). A member or a collaborator whose role is Triage or above holds a credential that can add a label or write to the repository, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds. Who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow

examples.name: insider-association.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose
#   author_association is MEMBER writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV.
# reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
#   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a
#   member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such
#   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
#   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
# cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
#   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it
#   is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: on an issue a member opens, the job runs and echo
#   appends body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets body to x and
#   PWNED to 1. On an issue whose author_association is NONE, FIRST_TIMER,
#   FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR, the if skips the job.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    if: github.event.issue.author_association == 'MEMBER'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "body=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose author_association is MEMBER writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
notes.cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
notes.attack_run_behavior: on an issue a member opens, the job runs and echo appends body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets body to x and PWNED to 1. On an issue whose author_association is NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR, the if skips the job.

undetected_forms.text: a variable named by the part of a key of env before the first =, such as A for the key A=B, which the runner sets to the rest of the key, =, and the value (in a step in a job's container, to the rest of the key alone): the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to the name of the variable

examples.name: split-env-name.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step has the env key T=X with the issue's
#   title, and writes $T to $GITHUB_ENV.
# reason: a todo (the same file): the runner sets the variable T to X= and
#   the title, and a title with a line break writes a line of its own to
#   $GITHUB_ENV.
# cause: the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to its name, and
#   no key is T.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: T is X=x, a line break and the rest of the title, and
#   echo writes the lines TITLE=X=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets
#   PWNED for the steps after it.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          T=X: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: echo "TITLE=$T" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - run: make

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step has the env key T=X with the issue's title, and writes $T to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): the runner sets the variable T to X= and the title, and a title with a line break writes a line of its own to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.cause: the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to its name, and no key is T.
notes.attack_run_behavior: T is X=x, a line break and the rest of the title, and echo writes the lines TITLE=X=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets PWNED for the steps after it.

undetected_forms.text: the summary of a wiki page (github.event.pages[*].summary) in a job that runs on gollum: the rule reads the summary as a value that nobody writes. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time: for pages made and edited on the web interface of GitHub and pushed by git, an edit message on the web interface and a commit message of git did not go into the summary. The authors saw only pages that the owner of a public repository made and edited, and did not try an edit by an account with no role in the repository

examples.name: wiki-summary.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on gollum, a step writes the summary of the wiki page to
#   $GITHUB_ENV.
# reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page
#   when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the
#   linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on
#   the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role
#   in the repository was not tried.
# cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody
#   writes.
# attack-value: github.event.pages[0].summary = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the
#   wiki writes in the payload, a line break in the summary would set
#   another environment variable of the steps after the step.
on: gollum
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          SUMMARY: ${{ github.event.pages[0].summary }}
        run: echo "summary=$SUMMARY" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: on gollum, a step writes the summary of the wiki page to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role in the repository was not tried.
notes.cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody writes.
notes.attack_run_behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the wiki writes in the payload, a line break in the summary would set another environment variable of the steps after the step.

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.name: remote-callee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/envvar-injection-unanswered, whose content is
#   the workflow of the true positive controlled
#   (controlled.custom-shell.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in
#   place of the on of controlled.custom-shell.yml. The linter has no answer
#   of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
#   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
#   the reusable workflow.
# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
#   the answer of workflow.definition.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: BODY holds x, a line break and PWNED=1, so echo
#   appends the two lines body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner
#   reads each line as NAME=value and sets body to x and PWNED to 1 for the
#   later steps.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/envvar-injection-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

notes.situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of the repository example-org/envvar-injection-unanswered, whose content is the workflow of the true positive controlled (controlled.custom-shell.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of controlled.custom-shell.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read the reusable workflow.
notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.
notes.attack_run_behavior: BODY holds x, a line break and PWNED=1, so echo appends the two lines body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner reads each line as NAME=value and sets body to x and PWNED to 1 for the later steps.

inconclusive_kinds.text: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.<id>.outputs), which the script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT

examples.name: step-output-run.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the next step writes steps.s.outputs.o to
#   $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}.
# reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an
#   attacker controls it is not known.
# cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: here s writes o=x, so o is x and the step appends the
#   one line v=x. Were o this value (a script of s that writes an attacker's
#   text as o), the script would become echo "v=x<line break>PWNED=1" >>
#   "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends v=x and PWNED=1, and the runner would set
#   PWNED to 1.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: echo "v=${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the next step writes steps.s.outputs.o to $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}.
notes.reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an attacker controls it is not known.
notes.cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.attack_run_behavior: here s writes o=x, so o is x and the step appends the one line v=x. Were o this value (a script of s that writes an attacker's text as o), the script would become echo "v=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends v=x and PWNED=1, and the runner would set PWNED to 1.

examples.name: step-output-local-action.yml

# situation: the job a sets its output o from the output of its step s,

inconclusive_kinds.text: an input of workflow_dispatch (inputs, github.event.inputs): whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input. A credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible attacker; the linter does not know whether such a credential exists or who holds it. The rule reports the value in a job with an environment that has required reviewers too, where a required reviewer of the environment can stop the run

examples.name: input-dispatch.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the workflow runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and a
#   step writes inputs.x and github.event.inputs.x to $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}.
# reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value, and the
#   workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls it
#   is not known; nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.
# attack-value: inputs.x = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow is an
#   attacker and gives x this value, both ${{ }} hold it, so echo appends
#   v=x, PWNED=1 x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets v to x and
#   PWNED to 1 x and then to 1.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      x: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=${{ inputs.x }} ${{ github.event.inputs.x }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: the workflow runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and a step writes inputs.x and github.event.inputs.x to $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}.
notes.reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value, and the workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls it is not known; nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when the one who dispatches the workflow is an attacker and gives x this value, both ${{ }} hold it, so echo appends v=x, PWNED=1 x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV; the runner sets v to x and PWNED to 1 x and then to 1.

examples.name: input-call.yml

#   here calls this workflow, so whether an attacker controls it is not

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=${{ inputs.x }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.attack_run_behavior: when a caller gives x an attacker's text such as this value (a caller on issues passing the issue's body), the script becomes echo "v=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends v=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets v to x and PWNED to 1.

notes.attack_run_behavior: when vars.V holds an attacker's text such as this value, the script becomes echo "v=x<line break>PWNED=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV", which appends v=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets v to x and PWNED to 1.

inconclusive_kinds.text: an env the workflow does not set, which a step before may set at run time ($GITHUB_ENV)

examples.name: env-unset.yml

notes.reason: which names that env sets, and their values, are known only at run time, so whether an attacker controls env.X is not known.

examples.name: env-whole.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step writes toJSON(env) to $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}, the whole

# reason: the whole env has what steps set at run time, so whether an

# attack-run-behavior: the value is toJSON(env) when a step before set B to
#   x, a line break and PWNED=1. toJSON writes the line break in a string as
#   the two characters \n, so the lines appended to $GITHUB_ENV are v={,
#   then "B": "x\nPWNED=1" after two spaces, and }; the runner sets v to {,
#   then a variable whose name is the second line up to its first =, two
#   spaces and "B": "x\nPWNED, and fails the step at the line }, which has
#   neither = nor <<. No variable PWNED is set: no text of a value starts a

on: issues

notes.situation: a step writes toJSON(env) to $GITHUB_ENV by ${{ }}, the whole env.
notes.reason: the whole env has what steps set at run time, so whether an attacker controls a part of it is not known.
notes.attack_run_behavior:
the value is toJSON(env) when a step before set B to x, a line break and PWNED=1. toJSON writes the line break in a string as the two characters 
, so the lines appended to $GITHUB_ENV are v={, then "B": "x
PWNED=1" after two spaces, and }; the runner sets v to {, then a variable whose name is the second line up to its first =, two spaces and "B": "x
PWNED, and fails the step at the line }, which has neither = nor <<. No variable PWNED is set: no text of a value starts a line of its own.

inconclusive_kinds.text: what a command other than echo, printf and cat writes to the environment file, with what an attacker may control in the arguments of the command or in what a pipe gives the command; and also what the echo of dash writes of a value, what printf writes of a value split into more arguments, a write inside a case statement of the shell, and a write to the environment file that the script names in a way the rule does not read

examples.name: writer-unknown.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, and jq writes
#   what it reads from "$B" to $GITHUB_ENV.
# reason: the rule reads what echo, printf and cat write to the file; what
#   another command such as jq writes from a value an attacker may control
#   is not analyzed.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "\"v=x\\nPWNED=1\""
# attack-run-behavior: the body is the JSON string "v=x\nPWNED=1"; jq reads
#   it, turns its \n into a line break, and -r prints it without quotes, so
#   the lines v=x and PWNED=1 are appended to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner
#   sets v to x and PWNED to 1. A body that is not JSON makes jq fail and
#   write nothing.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: jq -r . <<< "$B" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, and jq writes what it reads from "$B" to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.reason: the rule reads what echo, printf and cat write to the file; what another command such as jq writes from a value an attacker may control is not analyzed.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the body is the JSON string "v=x\nPWNED=1"; jq reads it, turns its \n into a line break, and -r prints it without quotes, so the lines v=x and PWNED=1 are appended to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets v to x and PWNED to 1. A body that is not JSON makes jq fail and write nothing.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a $( ), ` ` or $(( )), or ${ } with an operator, written to the environment file with what an attacker may control in it, whose line breaks are not known to be taken out

examples.name: subst-value.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B and writes
#   "b=$(echo "$B" | sed 's/^ *//')" to $GITHUB_ENV.
# reason: the value written is the output of a $( ) with what an attacker
#   may control in it, and whether its line breaks are taken out is not
#   known to the rule.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when the command in $( ) keeps line breaks, as sed
#   here does, echo writes b=x and then the line PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, and
#   the runner sets b to x and a variable PWNED to 1; a command that keeps the
#   first line only (head -1) would write the one line b=x.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "b=$(echo "$B" | sed 's/^ *//')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B and writes "b=$(echo "$B" | sed 's/^ *//')" to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.reason: the value written is the output of a $( ) with what an attacker may control in it, and whether its line breaks are taken out is not known to the rule.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when the command in $( ) keeps line breaks, as sed here does, echo writes b=x and then the line PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets b to x and a variable PWNED to 1; a command that keeps the first line only (head -1) would write the one line b=x.

inconclusive_kinds.text: what the script writes after exec sends its output to the environment file

examples.name: exec-redirect.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, sends the
#   output of its script to $GITHUB_ENV by exec, and then runs echo "b=$B".
# reason: after exec, what each later command writes goes to the file; the
#   rule does not analyze what the script writes after the exec.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: after exec, echo "b=$B" writes to $GITHUB_ENV,
#   appending b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x and PWNED to 1.
#   Nothing unknown decides this: the rule does not read the writes after
#   the exec.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          exec >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "b=$B"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, sends the output of its script to $GITHUB_ENV by exec, and then runs echo "b=$B".
notes.reason: after exec, what each later command writes goes to the file; the rule does not analyze what the script writes after the exec.
notes.attack_run_behavior: after exec, echo "b=$B" writes to $GITHUB_ENV, appending b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x and PWNED to 1. Nothing unknown decides this: the rule does not read the writes after the exec.

examples.name: exec-redirect.loop.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B and, in a for
#   loop of two rounds, runs echo "b=$B" and then sends the output of its
#   script to $GITHUB_ENV by exec.
# reason: in the second round, echo "b=$B" runs after the exec, so it
#   writes to the file; the rule does not analyze what the script writes
#   after the exec.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: in the second round, echo "b=$B" writes to
#   $GITHUB_ENV, appending b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x and
#   PWNED to 1. Nothing unknown decides this: the rule does not read the
#   writes after the exec.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          for i in 1 2; do
            echo "b=$B"
            exec >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          done

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B and, in a for loop of two rounds, runs echo "b=$B" and then sends the output of its script to $GITHUB_ENV by exec.
notes.reason: in the second round, echo "b=$B" runs after the exec, so it writes to the file; the rule does not analyze what the script writes after the exec.
notes.attack_run_behavior: in the second round, echo "b=$B" writes to $GITHUB_ENV, appending b=x and PWNED=1; the runner sets b to x and PWNED to 1. Nothing unknown decides this: the rule does not read the writes after the exec.

inconclusive_kinds.text: what the script writes to the environment file after the point where the rule stops following the script

examples.name: after-stop.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B; its script
#   first runs an echo with a case inside $( ), and then writes "b=$B" to
#   $GITHUB_ENV.
# reason: the rule stops following the script where it cannot read it (the
#   case), so what the script writes to the file after that is not analyzed.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the first echo prints a= (the case matches nothing);
#   the second appends b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets b
#   to x and PWNED to 1. Nothing unknown decides this: what the rule cannot
#   read, the case, does not change what the second echo writes.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          echo "a=$(case x in a) b;; esac)"
          echo "b=$B" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B; its script first runs an echo with a case inside $( ), and then writes "b=$B" to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.reason: the rule stops following the script where it cannot read it (the case), so what the script writes to the file after that is not analyzed.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the first echo prints a= (the case matches nothing); the second appends b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_ENV, and the runner sets b to x and PWNED to 1. Nothing unknown decides this: what the rule cannot read, the case, does not change what the second echo writes.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a call of a function after the rule has read the bodies of the functions at 4,096 calls in the script, such as a call after a chain of functions in which each function calls the next function twice (f1() { f0; f0; }; ... f13() { f12; f12; }; f13; w): the rule does not read the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls, so the rule does not decide the assignments, the writes, the prints and the requests in the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls

examples.name: call-body-unknown.yml

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step defines a function w that sets out to $GITHUB_ENV, runs a chain of functions f0 to f13 in which each function calls the function before it twice (16,383 calls), calls w, and writes V=$V to "$out".
notes.reason: the call of w comes after the 4,096 calls of functions that the rule follows, so the rule does not read the body of w, and does not decide whether V=$V goes to $GITHUB_ENV.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_ENV.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow

examples.name: remote-callee-unknown.yml
examples.text:

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/envvar-injection-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
