undetected_forms.text: a variable that a shell function unsets inside a recursive call of a function, where a function between the two calls made the variable local (f() { if [ -z "$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }; h() { s=x; local s=y; f; }; g() { unset s; }): bash takes away the local of the nearest calling function that made the variable local, and the variable then holds the value from before the nearest calling function made the variable local; the rule reads the recursive call where the first call of the function runs, without the calls in between, and does not read the value that the unset reveals

examples.name: recursive-unset-local.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step defines f, which calls h on the first
#   call of f and calls g on the second call of f; h sets out to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, makes out local with /dev/null, and calls f. g unsets out
#   and writes v= and "$V" to the file in "$out".
# reason: a todo (the same file): in the second call of f, the unset in g
#   takes away the local that h made, and out holds the value that h set
#   before h made out local: $GITHUB_OUTPUT, which gets the issue's body.
# cause: the rule reads the second call of f, which f makes through h, where
#   the first call of f runs, without the call of h, so the rule does not read
#   the value that the unset reveals.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\napproved=true"
# attack-run-behavior: the step s has the output approved.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          f() { if [ -z "$inner" ]; then inner=1; h; else g; fi; }
          g() { unset out; echo "v=$V" >> "$out"; }
          h() { out="$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; local out=/dev/null; f; }
          f
      - env:
          W: ${{ steps.s.outputs.v }}
        run: echo "$W"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step defines f, which calls h on the first call of f and calls g on the second call of f; h sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, makes out local with /dev/null, and calls f. g unsets out and writes v= and "$V" to the file in "$out".
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): in the second call of f, the unset in g takes away the local that h made, and out holds the value that h set before h made out local: $GITHUB_OUTPUT, which gets the issue's body.
notes.cause: the rule reads the second call of f, which f makes through h, where the first call of f runs, without the call of h, so the rule does not read the value that the unset reveals.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the step s has the output approved.

undetected_forms.text: a variable that a shell function unsets after a calling function made the variable local, when an assignment to the variable or a second unset of the variable follows the unset (s=x; reset() { unset s; }; point() { local s=y; reset; s=z; }; point): bash takes away the local of the calling function, so that the assignment after the unset sets the variable outside the calling function, and a second unset takes away the local of the next calling function or unsets the variable outside the functions; the rule keeps the local of the calling function after the unset, gives the variable back the value from before the calling function made the variable local when the calling function returns, and reads the second unset as the first unset

examples.name: unset-caller-local.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to /dev/null and defines reset,
#   which unsets out; point makes out local with /dev/null, calls reset, and
#   sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The step calls point and then writes v= and
#   "$V" to the file in "$out".
# reason: a todo (the same file): the unset in reset takes away the local that
#   point made, so the assignment in point after reset sets the out of the
#   step: $GITHUB_OUTPUT, which gets the issue's body.
# cause: the rule keeps the local of point after the unset in reset, and gives
#   out back /dev/null when point returns, so the rule does not read the value
#   that point set after reset.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\napproved=true"
# attack-run-behavior: the step s has the output approved.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          out=/dev/null
          reset() { unset out; }
          point() { local out=/dev/null; reset; out="$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; }
          point
          echo "v=$V" >> "$out"
      - env:
          W: ${{ steps.s.outputs.v }}
        run: echo "$W"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step sets out to /dev/null and defines reset, which unsets out; point makes out local with /dev/null, calls reset, and sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The step calls point and then writes v= and "$V" to the file in "$out".
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): the unset in reset takes away the local that point made, so the assignment in point after reset sets the out of the step: $GITHUB_OUTPUT, which gets the issue's body.
notes.cause: the rule keeps the local of point after the unset in reset, and gives out back /dev/null when point returns, so the rule does not read the value that point set after reset.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the step s has the output approved.

undetected_forms.text: tee run through another command or by its path (sudo tee, command tee, /usr/bin/tee): the rule reads tee by its name alone

examples.name: wrapped-tee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by
#   sudo tee, command tee and /usr/bin/tee.
# reason: a todo (the same file): reading tee through another command or by
#   its path would find it.
# cause: the rule reads tee by its name alone.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: echo prints the lines a=x and PWNED=1, and each tee
#   (run by sudo, by command, and by its path) appends them to $GITHUB_OUTPUT,
#   so the runner sets the outputs a and PWNED.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          T: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          echo "a=$T" | sudo tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "a=$T" | command tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "a=$T" | /usr/bin/tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on issues, a run writes the issue's title to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by sudo tee, command tee and /usr/bin/tee.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): reading tee through another command or by its path would find it.
notes.cause: the rule reads tee by its name alone.
notes.attack_run_behavior: echo prints the lines a=x and PWNED=1, and each tee (run by sudo, by command, and by its path) appends them to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, so the runner sets the outputs a and PWNED.

undetected_forms.text: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('[...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, _, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space. The if of the job limits the value in every step of the job, and the if of a step with a run: script limits the value in that step only. In those steps the value equals one of the strings when the case of the letters is ignored, so the rule does not report the value. The attacker still chooses the case of each letter of the value. GitHub's server, which evaluates the if of a job, also takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k and the long s as equal to the letter s; the runner, which evaluates the if of a step, takes the Kelvin sign as equal to the letter k. Where the case of a letter changes what the value names, such as a command, a variable, a file on a file system that tells names apart by their case (the default file system of a Linux runner), a host or a tool, the choice of the case can cause harm

examples.name: if-compared.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is
#   result, and a step writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the name
#   of the output, the part of a line of $GITHUB_OUTPUT before the =; the
#   step has an id, so the runner keeps the outputs of the step.
# reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string result, ignoring the
#   case of its letters, so the body has no line break; the attacker still
#   chooses the case of the name of the output, and the author of this example has not checked
#   whether the case of the name of an output changes which output a later
#   step reads.
# cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares
#   with such a string as written by the attacker.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "RESULT"
# attack-run-behavior: the if passes, and the step writes the line RESULT=ok
#   to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
jobs:
  j:
    if: github.event.comment.body == 'result'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        run: echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}=ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on issue_comment, a job runs only when the comment's body is result, and a step writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the name of the output, the part of a line of $GITHUB_OUTPUT before the =; the step has an id, so the runner keeps the outputs of the step.
notes.reason: the job's if lets the body be only the string result, ignoring the case of its letters, so the body has no line break; the attacker still chooses the case of the name of the output, and the author of this example has not checked whether the case of the name of an output changes which output a later step reads.
notes.cause: the rule does not treat a value that the if of the job compares with such a string as written by the attacker.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the if passes, and the step writes the line RESULT=ok to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

notes.reason: a todo (the same file): reading pwsh would find it.

examples.name: github-script.yml

# situation: on issues, actions/github-script calls core.setOutput with the
#   issue's body.
# reason: no added gain: @actions/core writes a random delimiter, and

undetected_forms.text: a write to the environment file, or an exec (the builtin of the shell) that opens the environment file, inside an arm of a case statement of the shell: the rule finds the case statement and does not read the commands in the arms of the case statement

examples.name: case-arm.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step writes body= and the issue's body to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT inside an arm of a case that skips an empty value.
# reason: a todo (the same file): the arm runs, and each later line of the
#   body such as x=y is read as an output of its own beside body.
# cause: the shell parser does not read the commands of a case.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value is not empty, so the case takes its
#   second arm, and echo writes the lines body=x and PWNED=1 to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the runner sets the outputs body (x) and PWNED (1).
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          case "$BODY" in
            "") ;;
            *) echo "body=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
          esac

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step writes body= and the issue's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT inside an arm of a case that skips an empty value.

undetected_forms.text: the content of a file that a command of the script writes into $GITHUB_OUTPUT by printing the file, not through a shell variable (cat values.txt >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT, tee -a $GITHUB_OUTPUT < values.txt, or the content passed through sed or tr between the file and $GITHUB_OUTPUT), such as a file of an artifact that was uploaded by a run that an attacker started: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where the file comes from (the step that downloads the file)

examples.name: file-content.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on workflow_run, the script of a step copies into $GITHUB_OUTPUT, with
#   cat, the content of a file of an artifact that was uploaded by the run
#   that triggered the workflow, by printing the file, not through a shell
#   variable.
# reason: a todo (the same file): reading, in the workflow, the command that
#   copies the file and the step that downloads the file would find it.
#   artifact-poisoning reports the download of the artifact, and this rule
#   reports nothing.
# cause: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where
#   the file comes from (the step that downloads the file).
# attack-value: the file values.txt of the artifact values = "version=1.2.3\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: download-artifact puts values.txt in the workspace, and cat appends
#   the two lines of values.txt to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the runner sets the
#   outputs version and PWNED of the step publish.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["receive-pr"]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: values
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
      - id: publish
        run: cat values.txt >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on workflow_run, the script of a step copies into $GITHUB_OUTPUT, with cat, the content of a file of an artifact that was uploaded by the run that triggered the workflow, by printing the file, not through a shell variable.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): reading, in the workflow, the command that copies the file and the step that downloads the file would find it. artifact-poisoning reports the download of the artifact, and this rule reports nothing.
notes.cause: the rule reads the text of the script, and does not follow where the file comes from (the step that downloads the file).

attack_value.carrier: the file values.txt of the artifact values

notes.attack_run_behavior: download-artifact puts values.txt in the workspace, and cat appends the two lines of values.txt to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the runner sets the outputs version and PWNED of the step publish.

undetected_forms.text: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment that runs only for a pull request from a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository: the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (repo.fork-pr-secrets, repo.fork-pr-write-tokens). The rule does not read the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens for the runs of a review, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker. When the attacker opened the pull request from a fork, a review of that pull request gives the attacker nothing more than the pull request itself gives: the run takes the workflow of the merge commit of the pull request (GitHub's documentation gives refs/pull/<n>/merge as the ref of the run of a review), and the attacker can change that workflow in the pull request

examples.name: fork-review.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, in a job that runs only for a pull request from a
#   fork.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a
#   fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes
#   to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the
#   attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has
#   those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
# cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for
#   the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a
#   review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "x\nversion=PWNED"
# attack-run-behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull
#   request of another person from a fork starts the job a; the line after
#   the line break sets the output version of the step.

jobs:

    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:

          B: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: echo "body=$B" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, in a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the job runs only for a pull request from a fork. Where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks, the run of a review that the attacker writes on the pull request of another person from a fork has those secrets or that token, and the job runs for the attacker.
notes.cause: the rule does not read the settings of a private repository for the runs of pull requests from forks, and does not count the run of a review of a pull request from a fork as a run of the attacker.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the comment of the attacker on the diff of the pull request of another person from a fork starts the job a; the line after the line break sets the output version of the step.

examples.name: insider-association.yml
examples.text:

#   author_association is MEMBER writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read
#   access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a

#   a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role
#   gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
# cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association
#   (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it

        run: echo "body=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a job whose if lets in an issue whose author_association is MEMBER writes the issue's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): a member of the organization, who may have read access only, passes this if (in an organization that lets anyone become a member, such as by a bot that invites whoever asks, an outsider becomes such a member), and gets the job's token and secrets past what the Read role gives; who is a member, and with what role, is not in the workflow.
notes.cause: the rule evaluates the if with the attacker's author_association (NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR), for which it is false, so no attacker's event runs the job.
notes.attack_run_behavior: for an issue whose author_association is MEMBER, echo writes the lines body=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs body and PWNED; for an issue of NONE, FIRST_TIMER, FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR or CONTRIBUTOR the job's if is false and the job is skipped.

# situation: on issues opened, a step has the env key T=X with the issue's

jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          T=X: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: echo "title=$T" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: make

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step has the env key T=X with the issue's title, and writes $T to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): the runner sets the variable T to X= and the title, and a title with a line break writes a line of its own to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.cause: the rule reads a variable of env by a key equal to its name, and no key is T.
notes.attack_run_behavior: T is X=x, a line break and the rest of the title, and echo writes the lines title=X=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the step has the output PWNED.

undetected_forms.text: the summary of a wiki page (github.event.pages[*].summary) in a job that runs on gollum: the rule reads the summary as a value that nobody writes. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time: for pages made and edited on the web interface of GitHub and pushed by git, an edit message on the web interface and a commit message of git did not go into the summary. The authors saw only pages that the owner of a public repository made and edited, and did not try an edit by an account with no role in the repository

examples.name: wiki-summary.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on gollum, a step writes the summary of the wiki page to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page
#   when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the
#   linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on
#   the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role
#   in the repository was not tried.
# cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody
#   writes.
# attack-value: github.event.pages[0].summary = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the
#   wiki writes in the payload, a line break in the summary would set
#   another output of the step.
on: gollum
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          SUMMARY: ${{ github.event.pages[0].summary }}
        run: echo "summary=$SUMMARY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on gollum, a step writes the summary of the wiki page to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: a limitation (run time): GitHub decides the summary of a wiki page when the event happens. The gollum payloads that the authors of the linter saw had a null summary each time, for pages made and edited on the web interface and pushed by git; an edit by an account with no role in the repository was not tried.
notes.cause: the rule reads the summary of a wiki page as a value that nobody writes.
notes.attack_run_behavior: if GitHub ever put a summary that the editor of the wiki writes in the payload, a line break in the summary would set another output of the step.

undetected_forms.text: a value an attacker controls that a step prints to its log, with ##[set-output name=…;] anywhere in a line: the runner reads the line as set-output, which needs no ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS, and sets an output of the step; the rule reads what the step writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT

examples.name: log-command.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, a step prints the issue's title, and the
#   next step reads the output tag of the step.
# reason: a todo (the same file): the runner reads ##[set-output name=…;]
#   anywhere in a line of the log, without ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS,
#   so a title with ##[set-output name=tag;]PWNED sets the output tag that
#   the next step writes into its script.
# cause: the rule reads what a step writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, not the
#   workflow commands of its log.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x ##[set-output name=tag;]PWNED"
# attack-run-behavior: the runner reads the line of the log as set-output,
#   and the output tag of the step is PWNED.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: title
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          echo "title: $TITLE"
      - run: echo "tag ${{ steps.title.outputs.tag }}"

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step prints the issue's title, and the next step reads the output tag of the step.
notes.reason: a todo (the same file): the runner reads ##[set-output name=…;] anywhere in a line of the log, without ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS, so a title with ##[set-output name=tag;]PWNED sets the output tag that the next step writes into its script.
notes.cause: the rule reads what a step writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, not the workflow commands of its log.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the runner reads the line of the log as set-output, and the output tag of the step is PWNED.

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.name: remote-callee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/output-clobbering-unanswered, whose content
#   is the workflow of the true positive controlled
#   (controlled.default-assignment.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call
#   in place of the on of controlled.default-assignment.yml. The linter has
#   no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
#   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
#   the reusable workflow.
# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
#   the answer of workflow.definition.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/output-clobbering-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

notes.situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of the repository example-org/output-clobbering-unanswered, whose content is the workflow of the true positive controlled (controlled.default-assignment.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of controlled.default-assignment.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read the reusable workflow.
notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

inconclusive_kinds.text: the output of a step that runs a script (steps.<id>.outputs), which the script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT

examples.name: step-output-run.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the next step writes steps.s.outputs.o to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
# reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an
#   attacker controls it is not known.
# cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# attack-value: steps.s.outputs.o = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when o holds an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }}
#   puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the
#   lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v
#   and PWNED. As the step s is written here, o is x.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: echo "v=${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: the step s runs a script that writes the output o to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the next step writes steps.s.outputs.o to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
notes.reason: the output is what the script writes at run time, so whether an attacker controls it is not known.
notes.cause: the rule does not yet follow what a script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when o holds an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED. As the step s is written here, o is x.

inconclusive_kinds.text: the output of another job of the workflow (needs.<id>.outputs)

examples.name: job-output.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the job a sets its output o from the output of its step s,
#   which a script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the job b writes
#   needs.a.outputs.o to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
# reason: the value is what another job computes at run time, so whether an
#   attacker controls it is not known.
# cause: the rule does not yet follow the output of a job back to what sets
#   it.
# attack-value: needs.a.outputs.o = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when o holds an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }}
#   puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the
#   lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v
#   and PWNED. As the step s is written here, o is x.
on: issues
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      o: ${{ steps.s.outputs.o }}
    steps:
      - id: s
        run: echo "o=x" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  b:
    needs: a
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=${{ needs.a.outputs.o }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: the job a sets its output o from the output of its step s, which a script writes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the job b writes needs.a.outputs.o to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
notes.reason: the value is what another job computes at run time, so whether an attacker controls it is not known.
notes.cause: the rule does not yet follow the output of a job back to what sets it.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when o holds an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED. As the step s is written here, o is x.

inconclusive_kinds.text: an input of workflow_dispatch (inputs, github.event.inputs): whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value of the input. A credential whose only write access is to the permission Actions can dispatch the workflow, and the credential premise keeps the holder of such a credential as a possible attacker; the linter does not know whether such a credential exists or who holds it. The rule reports the value in a job with an environment that has required reviewers too, where a required reviewer of the environment can stop the run

examples.name: input-dispatch.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the workflow runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and a
#   step writes inputs.x and github.event.inputs.x to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{
#   }}.
# reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value, and the
#   workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls it
#   is not known; nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.
# attack-value: inputs.x = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches gives x an attacker's text
#   such as this, ${{ }} puts it in both places, so the echo writes the lines
#   v=x, PWNED=1 x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the
#   outputs v and PWNED (the last, 1).
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      x: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=${{ inputs.x }} ${{ github.event.inputs.x }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: the workflow runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and a step writes inputs.x and github.event.inputs.x to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
notes.reason: whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the value, and the workflow does not tell who that is, so whether an attacker controls it is not known; nothing the rule could read is expected to tell it.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when the one who dispatches gives x an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }} puts it in both places, so the echo writes the lines v=x, PWNED=1 x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED (the last, 1).

inconclusive_kinds.text: an input of a reusable workflow or a composite action (inputs), which the caller gives

examples.name: input-call.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the workflow is a reusable workflow (workflow_call) with the
#   input x, and a step writes inputs.x to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
# reason: the value of inputs.x is what the caller gives, and no file read
#   here calls this workflow, so whether an attacker controls it is not
#   known.
# cause: the rule reads what each caller among the files read gives
#   inputs.x, and decides only when those are every caller: the files read
#   are the whole repository and every call to this workflow is resolved.
#   Here no file read calls it; a caller in another repository is never
#   read.
# attack-value: inputs.x = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when a caller gives x an attacker's text such as this,
#   ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which
#   writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets
#   the outputs v and PWNED.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      x:
        type: string
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=${{ inputs.x }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: the workflow is a reusable workflow (workflow_call) with the input x, and a step writes inputs.x to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
notes.reason: the value of inputs.x is what the caller gives, and no file read here calls this workflow, so whether an attacker controls it is not known.
notes.cause: the rule reads what each caller among the files read gives inputs.x, and decides only when those are every caller: the files read are the whole repository and every call to this workflow is resolved. Here no file read calls it; a caller in another repository is never read.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when a caller gives x an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a value of a matrix that is not written out in the workflow

examples.name: matrix.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the matrix value v is ${{ vars.V }}, not written out in the
#   workflow, and a step writes matrix.v to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
# reason: what the value holds is not known from the workflow, so whether an

#   }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes

#   outputs v and PWNED.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:

    steps:

notes.reason: what the value holds is not known from the workflow, so whether an attacker controls it is not known.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when vars.V holds an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED.

      - run: echo "v=${{ env.NOWHERE }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: a step writes env.NOWHERE to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}, an env the workflow does not set.
notes.reason: a step before may set it at run time through $GITHUB_ENV, so what it holds, and whether an attacker controls it, is not known.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when a step before sets NOWHERE to an attacker's text such as this through $GITHUB_ENV, ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a variable of the env of the workflow, a job or a step, where the whole env of the workflow, the job or the step is one ${{ }}

examples.name: env-dynamic.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the env of the job is the whole ${{ fromJSON(vars.E) }}, and a
#   step writes env.X to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
# reason: which names that env sets, and their values, are known only at run
#   time, so whether an attacker controls env.X is not known.
# attack-value: env.X = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when vars.E sets X to an attacker's text such as this,
#   ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which
#   writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets
#   the outputs v and PWNED.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env: ${{ fromJSON(vars.E) }}
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=${{ env.X }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: the env of the job is the whole ${{ fromJSON(vars.E) }}, and a step writes env.X to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}.
notes.reason: which names that env sets, and their values, are known only at run time, so whether an attacker controls env.X is not known.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when vars.E sets X to an attacker's text such as this, ${{ }} puts its two lines inside the double quotes of the echo, which writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED.

inconclusive_kinds.text: the whole env (toJSON(env)), or an env whose name is not known, which has what steps set at run time

examples.name: env-whole.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step writes toJSON(env) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}, the
#   whole env.
# reason: the whole env has what steps set at run time, so whether an
#   attacker controls a part of it is not known.
# attack-value: toJSON(env) = "{\n  \"B\": \"$(echo PWNED=1 >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT)\"\n}"
# attack-run-behavior: the value is what toJSON returns when a step before set
#   the env B to the text $(echo PWNED=1 >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT) through
#   $GITHUB_ENV. toJSON writes a line break of a value as a backslash and n,
#   so no value of the env starts a line of its own; but the quotes of the
#   JSON close the double quotes of the echo, and the $( ) outside them runs
#   and appends the line PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The echo then writes v={,
#   a line "  B: " and }, and the runner sets the output PWNED, reads v, and
#   fails the step at the line "  B: ", which has neither = nor <<.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=${{ toJSON(env) }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: a step writes toJSON(env) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by ${{ }}, the whole env.
notes.reason: the whole env has what steps set at run time, so whether an attacker controls a part of it is not known.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value is what toJSON returns when a step before set the env B to the text $(echo PWNED=1 >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT) through $GITHUB_ENV. toJSON writes a line break of a value as a backslash and n, so no value of the env starts a line of its own; but the quotes of the JSON close the double quotes of the echo, and the $( ) outside them runs and appends the line PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. The echo then writes v={, a line "  B: " and }, and the runner sets the output PWNED, reads v, and fails the step at the line "  B: ", which has neither = nor <<.

inconclusive_kinds.text: what a command other than echo, printf and cat writes to the environment file, with what an attacker may control in the arguments of the command or in what a pipe gives the command; and also what the echo of dash writes of a value, what printf writes of a value split into more arguments, a write inside a case statement of the shell, and a write to the environment file that the script names in a way the rule does not read

examples.name: writer-unknown.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, and jq writes
#   what it reads from "$B" to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: the rule reads what echo, printf and cat write to the file; what
#   another command such as jq writes from a value an attacker may control
#   is not analyzed.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "\"a=x\\nPWNED=1\""
# attack-run-behavior: when the body is a JSON string whose text has an
#   escaped line break, as this one, jq -r prints the text with the line
#   break, so the lines a=x and PWNED=1 go to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner
#   sets the outputs a and PWNED. A body that is not JSON makes jq fail, and
#   the step fails.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: jq -r . <<< "$B" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, and jq writes what it reads from "$B" to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: the rule reads what echo, printf and cat write to the file; what another command such as jq writes from a value an attacker may control is not analyzed.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when the body is a JSON string whose text has an escaped line break, as this one, jq -r prints the text with the line break, so the lines a=x and PWNED=1 go to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs a and PWNED. A body that is not JSON makes jq fail, and the step fails.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a $( ), ` ` or $(( )), or ${ } with an operator, written to the environment file with what an attacker may control in it, whose line breaks are not known to be taken out

examples.name: subst-value.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B and writes
#   "b=$(echo "$B" | sed 's/^ *//')" to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: the value written is the output of a $( ) with what an attacker
#   may control in it, and whether its line breaks are taken out is not
#   known to the rule.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: when the command in $( ) keeps line breaks, as sed
#   here does, echo writes b=x and then the line PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT,
#   and the runner sets the output b to x and an output PWNED to 1; a command
#   that keeps the first line only (head -1) would write the one line b=x.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "b=$(echo "$B" | sed 's/^ *//')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B and writes "b=$(echo "$B" | sed 's/^ *//')" to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: the value written is the output of a $( ) with what an attacker may control in it, and whether its line breaks are taken out is not known to the rule.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when the command in $( ) keeps line breaks, as sed here does, echo writes b=x and then the line PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the output b to x and an output PWNED to 1; a command that keeps the first line only (head -1) would write the one line b=x.

inconclusive_kinds.text: what the script writes after exec sends its output to the environment file

examples.name: exec-redirect.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, sends the
#   output of its script to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by exec, and then runs echo
#   "b=$B".
# reason: after exec, what each later command writes goes to the file; the
#   rule does not analyze what the script writes after the exec.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: after the exec, the echo writes the lines b=x and
#   PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs b and PWNED.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          exec >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "b=$B"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B, sends the output of its script to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by exec, and then runs echo "b=$B".
notes.reason: after exec, what each later command writes goes to the file; the rule does not analyze what the script writes after the exec.
notes.attack_run_behavior: after the exec, the echo writes the lines b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs b and PWNED.

inconclusive_kinds.text: what the script writes to the environment file after the point where the rule stops following the script

examples.name: after-stop.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B; its script
#   first runs an echo with a case inside $( ), and then writes "b=$B" to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: the rule stops following the script where it cannot read it (the
#   case), so what the script writes to the file after that is not analyzed.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the case in $( ) matches nothing, so the first echo
#   prints a=; the second writes the lines b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT,
#   and the runner sets the outputs b and PWNED.
on: issues
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          echo "a=$(case x in a) b;; esac)"
          echo "b=$B" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: a step puts the body of the issue in the env B; its script first runs an echo with a case inside $( ), and then writes "b=$B" to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: the rule stops following the script where it cannot read it (the case), so what the script writes to the file after that is not analyzed.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the case in $( ) matches nothing, so the first echo prints a=; the second writes the lines b=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs b and PWNED.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a call of a function after the rule has read the bodies of the functions at 4,096 calls in the script, such as a call after a chain of functions in which each function calls the next function twice (f1() { f0; f0; }; ... f13() { f12; f12; }; f13; w): the rule does not read the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls, so the rule does not decide the assignments, the writes, the prints and the requests in the bodies of the functions at the calls past the 4,096 calls

examples.name: call-body-unknown.yml

notes.situation: on issues opened, a step defines a function w that sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, runs a chain of functions f0 to f13 in which each function calls the function before it twice (16,383 calls), calls w, and writes v=$V to "$out".
notes.reason: the call of w comes after the 4,096 calls of functions that the rule follows, so the rule does not read the body of w, and does not decide whether v=$V goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

inconclusive_kinds.text: a job that calls a reusable workflow of another repository, when the linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer (the token that the linter uses cannot read the file, the file is larger than the limit, or the linter has used up the requests it may send to the GitHub API), or when the call is deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact: the rule does not read the jobs and the steps of the reusable workflow

examples.name: remote-callee-unknown.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/output-clobbering-unknown, whose content is
#   the workflow of the true positive controlled

#   in place of the on of controlled.default-assignment.yml. The linter

# attack-run-behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/output-clobbering-unknown/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

facts.reason: the example does not answer it

The linter asked the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow and got no answer.
notes.reason: what the jobs of the reusable workflow do is in the file that the linter could not read; whoever changes the uses, such as the author of a pull request, can name a reusable workflow that the token that the linter uses cannot read.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the value goes to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

false_positive_forms.text: gollum in a repository whose wiki is off or that only collaborators may edit

examples.name: wiki-closed.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the job runs on gollum and reads the title of a wiki page.
# reason: the wiki is off, or only collaborators may edit it (GitHub's
#   default), so no outsider writes the title of a page.
# cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that not anyone may edit the
#   wiki (repo.wiki-open false), the rule reports the finding. When no source
#   answers repo.wiki-open, the finding is conditional.
# attack-value: github.event.pages[0].title = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: with the title in V, echo writes the lines v=x and
#   PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED.
on: gollum
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.pages[0].title }}
        run: echo "v=$V" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

facts.reason: the example does not answer it

notes.situation: the job runs on gollum and reads the title of a wiki page.
notes.reason: the wiki is off, or only collaborators may edit it (GitHub's default), so no outsider writes the title of a page.
notes.cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that not anyone may edit the wiki (repo.wiki-open false), the rule reports the finding. When no source answers repo.wiki-open, the finding is conditional.
notes.attack_run_behavior: with the title in V, echo writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED.

false_positive_forms.text: a string only those who can write to the repository, or moderate or administer its organization, set, which the webhook schema leaves free and the table reads as arbitrary, such as the name of a label (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/using-labels-and-milestones-to-track-work/managing-labels), the reason a comment is hidden (https://docs.github.com/en/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/managing-disruptive-comments), the name of an issue field or of its option (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/managing-issue-fields-in-your-organization)

examples.name: writer-string.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues labeled, a run writes the label's name to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: only those who can write to the repository create a label, so its
#   name is no attacker's.
# cause: the webhook schema gives the name no enum, and the table reads a
#   free string as arbitrary.
# attack-value: github.event.label.name = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: no attacker can name a label; were the name the
#   value, the script would append label=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT,
#   and the step would have an output PWNED.
on: {issues: {types: [labeled]}}
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        run: echo "label=${{ github.event.label.name }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on issues labeled, a run writes the label's name to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: only those who can write to the repository create a label, so its name is no attacker's.
notes.cause: the webhook schema gives the name no enum, and the table reads a free string as arbitrary.
notes.attack_run_behavior: no attacker can name a label; were the name the value, the script would append label=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the step would have an output PWNED.

false_positive_forms.text: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('[...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, _, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space, where the rule reports the value although the if limits the value to those strings, because the rule does not read the if in one of three forms. (1) A reusable workflow or a composite action gets the value through an input, and the if of the calling job or the calling step compares the value. The rule reports the value in the file of the reusable workflow or the composite action. The value is harmless when the if of every caller of that file, inside and outside the repository, compares the value. (2) The if compares the value under one name, and the script writes the value under another name: for example, the if compares env.BODY, which the env of the step sets to ${{ github.event.comment.body }}, and the script writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; or the if compares ${{ github.head_ref }}, and the script writes ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}. The value is harmless when the two names hold the same value in the step; the rule does not check that the two names hold the same value. (3) The if of a step that uses an action compares a value that the with or the env of the same step holds. At the start of the job, the runner runs the pre step of each action from another repository whose action.yml has runs.pre, under the condition runs.pre-if of that action.yml and not under the if of the step. For the pre step, the runner evaluates the with and the env of the step, and the code of the pre step may read the inputs. The runner runs no pre step of a local action (./). The value is harmless when the action has no pre step, or when the code of the pre step does not read the value. In each form, the value is harmless only where the case of the letters does not change what the value names (the undetected form if-compared)

examples.name: if-unnarrowed.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issue_comment created, a step that has the comment's body in
#   env.BODY runs only when env.BODY is deploy, and the step writes
#   ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the value, the part of a line of
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT after the =; the step has an id, so the runner keeps
#   the outputs of the step.
# reason: the step's if compares env.BODY, which holds the comment's body,
#   with deploy, so in the step the body is deploy, ignoring the case of its
#   letters: the body has no character that the shell reads as code, no
#   line break, no word that starts with - and no workflow command.
# cause: the rule limits a value by an if only under the name that the if
#   compares: the if compares env.BODY, and the script writes
#   ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; the rule does not check that env.BODY
#   holds the comment's body.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: on GitHub, the step's if is false for such a body,
#   and the runner skips the step.
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        if: env.BODY == 'deploy'
        env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: echo "v=${{ github.event.comment.body }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on issue_comment created, a step that has the comment's body in env.BODY runs only when env.BODY is deploy, and the step writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }} as the value, the part of a line of $GITHUB_OUTPUT after the =; the step has an id, so the runner keeps the outputs of the step.
notes.reason: the step's if compares env.BODY, which holds the comment's body, with deploy, so in the step the body is deploy, ignoring the case of its letters: the body has no character that the shell reads as code, no line break, no word that starts with - and no workflow command.
notes.cause: the rule limits a value by an if only under the name that the if compares: the if compares env.BODY, and the script writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; the rule does not check that env.BODY holds the comment's body.
notes.attack_run_behavior: on GitHub, the step's if is false for such a body, and the runner skips the step.

false_positive_forms.text: a job on pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment whose if: condition lets the job run only when the head repository of the pull request is a fork, such as a job whose if: condition is github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork: on a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. The run of a review of a pull request from a fork has the secrets of the repository or a token that writes only where a private repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the undetected form fork-review). The rule does not read whether the repository that runs the workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and reports the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a branch of the repository

examples.name: fork-flag-review.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, in a job that runs only when the head repository of
#   the pull request is a fork.
# reason: the job runs only when the head repository of the pull request
#   is a fork. On a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head
#   repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a
#   fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. In
#   a public repository, the run of such a review has no secrets and a
#   token that only reads; in a private repository, the run has neither
#   secrets nor a token that writes unless the repository gives secrets or
#   a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the
#   undetected form fork-review).
# cause: the rule does not read whether the repository that runs the
#   workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and
#   reads the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a
#   branch of the repository.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "x\nversion=PWNED"
# attack-run-behavior: in a public repository that is not a fork, a review
#   of a pull request from a branch of the repository does not start the
#   job, as the head repository of such a pull request is the repository
#   itself; a review of a pull request from a fork starts the job with no
#   secrets and a token that only reads, so the value reaches no secret
#   and no token that writes.
on: pull_request_review_comment
jobs:
  a:
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          B: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: echo "body=$B" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on comments on the diff, a step writes the comment's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, in a job that runs only when the head repository of the pull request is a fork.
notes.reason: the job runs only when the head repository of the pull request is a fork. On a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. In a public repository, the run of such a review has no secrets and a token that only reads; in a private repository, the run has neither secrets nor a token that writes unless the repository gives secrets or a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the undetected form fork-review).
notes.cause: the rule does not read whether the repository that runs the workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and reads the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a branch of the repository.
notes.attack_run_behavior: in a public repository that is not a fork, a review of a pull request from a branch of the repository does not start the job, as the head repository of such a pull request is the repository itself; a review of a pull request from a fork starts the job with no secrets and a token that only reads, so the value reaches no secret and no token that writes.

false_positive_forms.text: a ${{ }} written in a $( ) whose tr takes out the line breaks: the whole substitution is read as the attacker's value

examples.name: tr-in-substitution.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the step writes the body of an issue to an environment file through
#   a $( ) in which tr takes out the line breaks of the body.
# reason: tr takes out the line breaks of the body before it is written.
# cause: the ${{ }} is written in the $( ) itself, which the rule reads as
#   the attacker's value whole (code-injection reports the ${{ }}).
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: ${{ }} puts the two lines inside the double quotes of
#   the echo in $( ), whose output tr -d '\n' joins, so the step writes the
#   one line v=xPWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the output v to
#   xPWNED=1 and no PWNED.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "v=$(echo "${{ github.event.issue.body }}" | tr -d '\n')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: the step writes the body of an issue to an environment file through a $( ) in which tr takes out the line breaks of the body.
notes.reason: tr takes out the line breaks of the body before it is written.
notes.cause: the ${{ }} is written in the $( ) itself, which the rule reads as the attacker's value whole (code-injection reports the ${{ }}).
notes.attack_run_behavior: ${{ }} puts the two lines inside the double quotes of the echo in $( ), whose output tr -d '\n' joins, so the step writes the one line v=xPWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the output v to xPWNED=1 and no PWNED.

false_positive_forms.text: a heredoc delimiter the author made random, such as D=$(uuidgen): the rule reads only its own fix's form as random

examples.name: own-random-delimiter.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the step writes the body to an environment file in a heredoc
#   whose delimiter the author made random.
# reason: the delimiter of the heredoc is random, which no one can guess.
# cause: the rule reads a delimiter as random only when the delimiter is a
#   variable that the assignment of the fix of the rule sets (ghadelimiter_
#   and 16 bytes of /dev/urandom in hex); a delimiter from uuidgen is not read
#   as random.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\n00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: the step writes v<<$D, the three lines of the body and
#   $D, where $D is the UUID uuidgen made in the run; the line
#   00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 is not $D, so the runner reads all
#   three lines as the value of v, closes it at $D, and sets no PWNED.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          D=$(uuidgen)
          echo "v<<$D" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "$V" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "$D" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: the step writes the body to an environment file in a heredoc whose delimiter the author made random.
notes.reason: the delimiter of the heredoc is random, which no one can guess.
notes.cause: the rule reads a delimiter as random only when the delimiter is a variable that the assignment of the fix of the rule sets (ghadelimiter_ and 16 bytes of /dev/urandom in hex); a delimiter from uuidgen is not read as random.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the step writes v<<$D, the three lines of the body and $D, where $D is the UUID uuidgen made in the run; the line 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 is not $D, so the runner reads all three lines as the value of v, closes it at $D, and sets no PWNED.

false_positive_forms.text: an assignment in a branch of if, after && or ||, in the body of a loop, or in the body of a function called there, that bash does not run (if false; then s=$KEY; fi): the rule does not read the value of a condition, so the rule reads the assignment as one that may run, and reads the variable as one that may hold the value of the assignment

examples.name: branch-not-run.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, the step s sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT in an
#   if whose condition is false, writes v= and the issue's body to "$out",
#   and goes on when the write fails (|| true); the next step reads the
#   output v.
# reason: bash does not run the branch, so out is empty when echo runs, and
#   the body does not go to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# cause: the rule does not read the value of the condition of an if, and
#   reads the assignment in the branch as one that may run.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\npwned=1"
# attack-run-behavior: bash cannot open the file of the empty name and
#   writes nothing, || true keeps the step going, and the runner sets no
#   output of the step s.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          if false; then out=$GITHUB_OUTPUT; fi
          echo "v=$V" >> "$out" || true
      - env:
          W: ${{ steps.s.outputs.v }}
        run: echo "$W"

notes.situation: on issues opened, the step s sets out to $GITHUB_OUTPUT in an if whose condition is false, writes v= and the issue's body to "$out", and goes on when the write fails (|| true); the next step reads the output v.
notes.reason: bash does not run the branch, so out is empty when echo runs, and the body does not go to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.cause: the rule does not read the value of the condition of an if, and reads the assignment in the branch as one that may run.
notes.attack_run_behavior: bash cannot open the file of the empty name and writes nothing, || true keeps the step going, and the runner sets no output of the step s.

false_positive_forms.text: a variable of env that the script sets again, before the script writes the variable to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, by an assignment that bash runs each time the script reaches the write, in the same shell as the write (not in a subshell, a $( ) or a command of a pipeline, not before a command name, and not as local in a shell function), and whose value holds nothing of the variable of env (X=safe; echo "a=$X" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"): at the write the variable holds the value of the assignment, and the rule still reads the variable as holding the value of env

examples.name: reassigned-variable.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, the step's env sets V to the issue's body,
#   and the script sets V to safe before the script writes v= and "$V" to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: the script writes v=safe, the value that the script sets, not the
#   issue's body.
# cause: the rule reads $V as the value of env, and does not read the
#   assignment in the script before the write.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\napproved=true"
# attack-run-behavior: V is safe when echo runs, so the runner sets the
#   output v to safe and sets no output approved.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          V=safe
          echo "v=$V" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: on issues opened, the step's env sets V to the issue's body, and the script sets V to safe before the script writes v= and "$V" to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: the script writes v=safe, the value that the script sets, not the issue's body.
notes.cause: the rule reads $V as the value of env, and does not read the assignment in the script before the write.
notes.attack_run_behavior: V is safe when echo runs, so the runner sets the output v to safe and sets no output approved.

false_positive_forms.text: a write to $GITHUB_OUTPUT by a command that the script runs in the background (&) with no wait for the command, where the command writes after the shell of the script ends (for example: (sleep 5; echo "a=$X" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT") &): a write that the command makes after the shell of the script ends does not reach the steps after the step; the rule reads the write as a write that reaches $GITHUB_OUTPUT, because whether the command writes before the shell of the script ends depends on how long the commands take when the step runs

examples.name: background-write.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues opened, the step s runs in the background (&), with
#   no wait, a subshell that sleeps 5 seconds and then writes v= and the
#   issue's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the shell of the script ends before the
#   write; the next step reads the output v.
# reason: a write that the background command makes after the shell of the
#   script ends does not reach the steps after the step (seen on the runner
#   on 2026-11-17), so the body sets no output.
# cause: the rule reads the write in the background as a write that reaches
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and does not read when the background command writes.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\napproved=true"
# attack-run-behavior: the step s has neither the output v nor the output
#   approved.
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: s
        env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          (sleep 5; echo "v=$V" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT") &
      - env:
          W: ${{ steps.s.outputs.v }}
        run: echo "$W"

notes.situation: on issues opened, the step s runs in the background (&), with no wait, a subshell that sleeps 5 seconds and then writes v= and the issue's body to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the shell of the script ends before the write; the next step reads the output v.
notes.reason: a write that the background command makes after the shell of the script ends does not reach the steps after the step (seen on the runner on 2026-11-17), so the body sets no output.
notes.cause: the rule reads the write in the background as a write that reaches $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and does not read when the background command writes.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the step s has neither the output v nor the output approved.

false_positive_forms.text: a step whose outputs are not read: no step after the step, no output of the job and no output of the action has a reference to an output of the step (steps.<id>.outputs.NAME), or a reference that reads every output name (toJSON(steps.<id>.outputs), toJSON(steps), steps[...]). The harm comes from what the steps that read the outputs do with the outputs, and the outputs alone run nothing. output-clobbering also reports a step with no id, and the runner sets no output of such a step, so such a step is of this form

examples.name: unread-outputs.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a step with no id writes the body of the issue
#   to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: the runner keeps the outputs of a step only when the step has
#   an id, so no step reads an output the body sets.
# cause: the rule does not read what reads the outputs of the step.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\ntag=$(id)"
# attack-run-behavior: the echo writes the lines b=x and tag=$(id) to
#   $GITHUB_OUTPUT, the runner reads the two lines, and no step reads the
#   outputs of the step.
on: issues
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "b=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: echo done

notes.situation: on issues, a step with no id writes the body of the issue to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
notes.reason: the runner keeps the outputs of a step only when the step has an id, so no step reads an output the body sets.
notes.cause: the rule does not read what reads the outputs of the step.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the echo writes the lines b=x and tag=$(id) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, the runner reads the two lines, and no step reads the outputs of the step.

false_positive_forms.text: a reusable workflow or a composite action when all of the following are true: the rule does not know all of the callers of the reusable workflow or the composite action; every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action (directly, or through another reusable workflow or composite action) is a workflow in the same repository; and the rule would report no finding of the finding kind if the rule read the reusable workflow or the composite action only on the events on which the workflows in the same repository run the reusable workflow or the composite action (for example, every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action runs only on push). When the rule does not know all of the callers, the rule can read the reusable workflow or the composite action on every event (the worst case). For example, the rule does not know all of the callers when no caller is among the inputs; when the inputs are not the whole repository; for a composite action, when an input is excluded or cannot be read; when a caller names the reusable workflow or the composite action by a name of the form owner/repo/path@ref instead of by a ./ path, in which owner/repo is the repository that the --repo flag names, or is any repository when no --repo flag is given; when a step names the composite action by a ./ path, and either no checkout step runs before that step or the last checkout step before that step is not a plain checkout step (a plain checkout step has no ref input, no repository input and no path input); when a step inside a composite action names another composite action by a ./ path; or when the rule does not know all of the callers of a caller

examples.name: callee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a reusable workflow that reads the title of an issue, and that
#   only the repository's own workflows call, all of them on push.
# reason: the issue it reads is never an outsider's.
# cause: a callee is read in the worst case, as if a caller ran on issues.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: with the title in V, echo writes the lines v=x and
#   PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED. In
#   a run of the callers, all on push, the event has no issue: V is empty and
#   the step writes the one line v=.
on: workflow_call
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          V: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: echo "v=$V" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

notes.situation: a reusable workflow that reads the title of an issue, and that only the repository's own workflows call, all of them on push.
notes.reason: the issue it reads is never an outsider's.
notes.cause: a callee is read in the worst case, as if a caller ran on issues.
notes.attack_run_behavior: with the title in V, echo writes the lines v=x and PWNED=1 to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and the runner sets the outputs v and PWNED. In a run of the callers, all on push, the event has no issue: V is empty and the step writes the one line v=.

examples.name: .github/workflows/called.yml
examples.text:
# situation: ci.yml of the repository o/r calls this reusable workflow on
#   push only, by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main, not by the
#   path ./.github/workflows/called.yml.
# reason: when the run of the linter names the repository (--repo o/r), the
#   call by the name is a call of this file, and the only caller runs on
#   push, which no attacker of the finding kind triggers. A run without
#   --repo reads the call by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main
#   as a call that may name a file of the repository, because the run does
#   not know which repository the inputs are; the rule does not resolve the
#   call to this file, so the rule reads this file on every event and reports
#   the same finding.
# cause: the rule does not resolve a call by the name of the repository to
#   the file, so the rule reads this workflow on every event.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.body = "x\nPWNED=1"
# attack-run-behavior: only a push to the repository runs ci.yml, which
#   calls this workflow on push; the run of the push reads no value of the
#   attacker's issue, pull request or comment.
on:
  workflow_call:
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: echo "body=$BODY" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

others.name: .github/workflows/ci.yml
others.text:
on: push
jobs:
  call:
    uses: o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main
    secrets: inherit

notes.situation: ci.yml of the repository o/r calls this reusable workflow on push only, by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main, not by the path ./.github/workflows/called.yml.
notes.reason: when the run of the linter names the repository (--repo o/r), the call by the name is a call of this file, and the only caller runs on push, which no attacker of the finding kind triggers. A run without --repo reads the call by the name o/r/.github/workflows/called.yml@main as a call that may name a file of the repository, because the run does not know which repository the inputs are; the rule does not resolve the call to this file, so the rule reads this file on every event and reports the same finding.
notes.cause: the rule does not resolve a call by the name of the repository to the file, so the rule reads this workflow on every event.
notes.attack_run_behavior: only a push to the repository runs ci.yml, which calls this workflow on push; the run of the push reads no value of the attacker's issue, pull request or comment.

false_positive_forms.text: a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and no other event (no workflow_call event either), in a repository whose Actions policies block the runs of the workflow on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false): an event policy that an administrator sets without pull_request_target among the allowed events, or the default policy that GitHub adds to a public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error. The documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails; the rule assumes that no job of such a run starts

examples.name: pull-request-target-blocked.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on pull_request_target opened, a step writes body= and the body
#   of the pull request to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
# reason: the Actions policies of the repository block the runs of the
#   workflow on pull_request_target: the default policy that GitHub adds to a
#   public repository without an applicable event policy, from the time when
#   GitHub enforces the default policy on the repository, or an event policy
#   whose list of allowed events does not have pull_request_target. GitHub's
#   documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a run, and that a
#   run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the documents do not
#   say whether a job of such a run starts before the run fails, and the rule
#   assumes that no job starts.
# cause: unless a file of facts or --fact says that the Actions policies block
#   runs on pull_request_target (repo.pull-request-target-allowed false), the
