undetected_forms.text: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds

examples.name: pull-request.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on pull_request, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to
#   true, and a step prints the title of the pull request.
# reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the
#   author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the
#   run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets;
#   when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on
#   the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the
#   workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own
#   pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case
#   holds.
# cause: the rule does not count pull_request as an event of an attacker. The
#   rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the workflow.
# attack: the author of a pull request from a fork titles the pull request
#   ##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]$(id).
# attack-run-behavior: the runner sets BASH_ENV, and the next step runs id
#   with what the run of the pull request has. When a ruleset of the
#   organization runs the workflow on a pull request of another repository, the
#   same steps run in the run of the ruleset; what the run of the ruleset has
#   was not observed, so whether the steps do harm in the run of the ruleset is
#   not known.
on: pull_request
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
      - run: echo next

notes.situation: on pull_request, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true, and a step prints the title of the pull request.
notes.reason: when only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow, the author of the pull request can change the workflow itself and gets what the run has without the flaw, so the flaw adds nothing to what the author gets; when a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories, the author cannot change the workflow, and what the run of the ruleset has beyond the author's own pull_request workflow is not known. The workflow does not say which case holds.
notes.cause: the rule does not count pull_request as an event of an attacker. The rule does not read whether a ruleset runs the workflow.
notes.attack: the author of a pull request from a fork titles the pull request ##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]$(id).
notes.attack_run_behavior: the runner sets BASH_ENV, and the next step runs id with what the run of the pull request has. When a ruleset of the organization runs the workflow on a pull request of another repository, the same steps run in the run of the ruleset; what the run of the ruleset has was not observed, so whether the steps do harm in the run of the ruleset is not known.

undetected_forms.text: a value of the event of workflow_dispatch other than its inputs, in a job that runs only on workflow_dispatch: the event has the ref, which is a branch or a tag that the repository already has, and values that GitHub fills, such as the login of the account that dispatches the workflow; the event has no text of an issue, a comment or a pull request. Whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and nothing else of the event. A token that cannot change the files of the repository can dispatch the workflow, such as a fine-grained token that has the permission Actions with write access and no permission Contents. The rule reports an input of the dispatch with the inconclusive kind input-dispatch

examples.name: dispatch.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job sets
#   ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true, and a step prints the title of
#   the issue. If the workflow also ran on issues, the rule would report the
#   same steps.
# reason: no added gain: on workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object,
#   so the expression of the title gives an empty string; whoever dispatches
#   the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and the steps
#   read no input.
# cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not
#   have workflow_dispatch; the rule reports an input of a dispatch with the
#   inconclusive kind input-dispatch.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]$(id)"
# attack-run-behavior: with the value put in, the runner sets BASH_ENV, and
#   the next step runs id. On workflow_dispatch the event has no issue
#   object, though: the expression gives an empty string, and the step
#   prints an empty line.
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
      - run: echo next

notes.situation: on workflow_dispatch, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true, and a step prints the title of the issue. If the workflow also ran on issues, the rule would report the same steps.
notes.reason: no added gain: on workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object, so the expression of the title gives an empty string; whoever dispatches the workflow chooses the ref and the inputs of the dispatch, and the steps read no input.
notes.cause: the table of the attacker's events that the rule reads does not have workflow_dispatch; the rule reports an input of a dispatch with the inconclusive kind input-dispatch.
notes.attack_run_behavior: with the value put in, the runner sets BASH_ENV, and the next step runs id. On workflow_dispatch the event has no issue object, though: the expression gives an empty string, and the step prints an empty line.

undetected_forms.text: a value of the client_payload of repository_dispatch (github.event.client_payload): only a credential with write access to the permission Contents of the repository can send repository_dispatch, and the credential premise assumes that no attacker holds such a credential; the sender chooses the whole client_payload

examples.name: repository-dispatch.yml
examples.text:

on: repository_dispatch
permissions: {}

undetected_forms.text: a value that an app outside GitHub Actions writes into a field of a commit status or a check run (the fields context, description and target_url of status; the fields name, output, details_url and external_id of check_run): the app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the field, such as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives to an outside CI; the rule reads the field as a field whose value the app chooses

examples.name: app-written.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on check_run, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when
#   the app makes a check run for a commit, the job writes the name of the
#   check run (github.event.check_run.name) where the rule reads it.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the app writes the name of the check run, and an
#   app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the name, such
#   as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives
#   to an outside CI.
# cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads the values that the
#   app writes into a commit status or a check run as the values that the
#   app chooses.
# attack-value: github.event.check_run.name = "::set-env name=BASH_ENV::/tmp/x.sh"
# attack-run-behavior: an outside CI copies the name of a job from the
#   configuration file of the pull request from a fork into the name of the
#   check run; the run of check_run starts on the default branch, and the

#   on status.
on: check_run
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - run: echo next

notes.situation: on check_run, which an app outside GitHub Actions starts when the app makes a check run for a commit, the job writes the name of the check run (github.event.check_run.name) where the rule reads it.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the app writes the name of the check run, and an app may copy a value of a pull request from a fork into the name, such as the name of a job that a configuration file of the pull request gives to an outside CI.
notes.cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads the values that the app writes into a commit status or a check run as the values that the app chooses.

undetected_forms.text: a workflow on an event of an attacker that puts a value the attacker writes into the client_payload of a repository_dispatch that the workflow sends (gh api with client_payload to the endpoint dispatches, peter-evans/repository-dispatch), and a workflow on repository_dispatch that uses the value: the flaw is in the workflow that sends the repository_dispatch, and the rule does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow

examples.name: .github/workflows/receiver.yml
examples.text:
# situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN
#   sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the
#   title of the issue as the value title; receiver.yml runs on that
#   repository_dispatch, and a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to
#   true, and a step prints the value title of the client_payload.
# reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays
#   the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the
#   repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow
#   run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception
#   to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no
#   workflow run.
# cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read
#   what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a
#   repository_dispatch.
# attack-value: github.event.issue.title = "##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]$(id)"
# attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title is the value;
#   sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml the runner sets
#   BASH_ENV, and the next step runs id.
on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [relay]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.client_payload.title }}"
      - run: echo next

others.name: .github/workflows/sender.yml
others.text:
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  relay:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VALUE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/dispatches" -f event_type=relay -f "client_payload[title]=$VALUE"

notes.situation: sender.yml runs on issues opened, and with the GITHUB_TOKEN sends a repository_dispatch of the type relay whose client_payload has the title of the issue as the value title; receiver.yml runs on that repository_dispatch, and a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true, and a step prints the value title of the client_payload.
notes.reason: the author of the issue writes the value, and sender.yml relays the value to receiver.yml in a repository_dispatch that a run of the repository sends with a token of the repository; GitHub creates a workflow run for a repository_dispatch sent with the GITHUB_TOKEN, as an exception to the rule that an event that the GITHUB_TOKEN triggers creates no workflow run.
notes.cause: the rule reads the events of each workflow alone, and does not read what a workflow sends to another workflow as the client_payload of a repository_dispatch.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the attacker opens an issue whose title is the value; sender.yml sends the value, and in the run of receiver.yml the runner sets BASH_ENV, and the next step runs id.

undetected_forms.text: an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller of the same repository passes, as an input of the call (under the key with: of the calling job or step), to a reusable workflow or a composite action, which uses the input as a value: the one who dispatches the caller chooses the value, and the rule reads the events of a called workflow or action from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that the caller gives

examples.name: .github/workflows/called.yml
examples.text:
# situation: caller.yml runs on workflow_dispatch with the input x, and
#   calls called.yml with the input x of the dispatch as the input x of
#   called.yml; called.yml sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true in its
#   job, and prints the input x in a step.
# reason: the one who dispatches caller.yml chooses the value:
#   input-dispatch reports such a value where a workflow on workflow_dispatch
#   refers to its input directly, but through the call the value is the input
#   x of called.yml.
# cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of
#   the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of
#   workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
# attack-value: inputs.x = "##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]$(id)"
# attack-run-behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the
#   value as x, the runner sets BASH_ENV, and the next step runs id.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      x: {type: string}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ inputs.x }}"
      - run: echo next

    inputs:
      x: {type: string}

notes.cause: the rule reads the events of a called workflow from the table of the callers, and does not follow the value of an input of workflow_dispatch that a caller gives in with.
notes.attack_run_behavior: when the one who dispatches caller.yml gives the value as x, the runner sets BASH_ENV, and the next step runs id.

undetected_forms.text: secrets, vars, runner, the outcome of a step, the result of a job. A run of the linter that adds the attacker variables-writer reports a reference of vars where the rule reads the value as written by the attacker, and a run of the linter that adds the attacker secrets-writer reports such a reference of secrets except secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (--add-attacker); no run reports runner, the outcome of a step or the result of a job

examples.name: not-attacker.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true.
#   A step prints the variable RELEASE_TAG and the secret RELEASE_NOTE,
#   which reach the step through env, and prints runner.os.
# reason: no added gain in a run that adds no attacker: no attacker writes
#   vars, secrets or runner.os, and one who may change the repository's
#   settings sets the variable and the secret. A run of the linter that adds
#   variables-writer (--add-attacker) reports the variable, a run that adds
#   secrets-writer reports the secret, and no run reports runner.os.
# cause: the rule does not count vars, secrets and runner as values of an
#   attacker.
# attack: one who may change the repository's settings sets RELEASE_TAG to
#   a line that starts with ::set-env; in a run that adds no attacker, no
#   attacker can set the variable.
# attack-run-behavior: the step prints the values; no attacker sets an
#   environment variable.
on: issues
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - env:
          TAG: ${{ vars.RELEASE_TAG }}
          NOTE: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_NOTE }}
        run: |
          echo "tag: $TAG"
          echo "note: $NOTE"
          echo "${{ runner.os }}"
      - run: echo next

notes.situation: on issues, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true. A step prints the variable RELEASE_TAG and the secret RELEASE_NOTE, which reach the step through env, and prints runner.os.
notes.reason: no added gain in a run that adds no attacker: no attacker writes vars, secrets or runner.os, and one who may change the repository's settings sets the variable and the secret. A run of the linter that adds variables-writer (--add-attacker) reports the variable, a run that adds secrets-writer reports the secret, and no run reports runner.os.
notes.cause: the rule does not count vars, secrets and runner as values of an attacker.
notes.attack: one who may change the repository's settings sets RELEASE_TAG to a line that starts with ::set-env; in a run that adds no attacker, no attacker can set the variable.
notes.attack_run_behavior: the step prints the values; no attacker sets an environment variable.

undetected_forms.text: a value that the author of a pull request writes in the profile of the account of the author (the profile name, the public email of the profile), in github.event.pull_request.merged_by of a merged pull request, or in github.event.pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue: the rule reads merged_by and the pusher as the account that merged or pushed, and the account that merged or pushed holds a credential that can merge or push; whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request, or the pusher of the push that GitHub makes when GitHub merges a pull request by a rebase, by auto-merge or from a merge queue, to the account of the author of the merged pull request was not checked

examples.name: merged-pusher.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on a pull request that is closed, a job sets
#   ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true, and a step prints the name of the
#   account that merged the pull request.
# reason: whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request to the
#   account of the author of the pull request was not checked: no payload with
#   merged_by was seen on GitHub. Were merged_by the author, the author would
#   write the name of merged_by, which is the profile name of the account of
#   the author.
# cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads merged_by as the
#   account that merged the pull request, and the account that merged the pull
#   request holds a credential that can merge.
# attack: the author of a pull request writes ##[set-env
#   name=BASH_ENV;]$(id) in the profile name of the account of the author, and
#   the pull request is merged.
# attack-run-behavior: were merged_by the author of the pull request, the
#   runner would set BASH_ENV, and the bash of the next step would run id.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [closed]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - env:
          MERGER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.merged_by.name }}
        run: echo "merged by $MERGER"
      - run: echo next

notes.situation: on a pull request that is closed, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true, and a step prints the name of the account that merged the pull request.
notes.reason: whether GitHub sets merged_by of a merged pull request to the account of the author of the pull request was not checked: no payload with merged_by was seen on GitHub. Were merged_by the author, the author would write the name of merged_by, which is the profile name of the account of the author.
notes.cause: the table of what an attacker controls reads merged_by as the account that merged the pull request, and the account that merged the pull request holds a credential that can merge.
notes.attack: the author of a pull request writes ##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]$(id) in the profile name of the account of the author, and the pull request is merged.
notes.attack_run_behavior: were merged_by the author of the pull request, the runner would set BASH_ENV, and the bash of the next step would run id.

examples.name: decoded-escape.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on gollum, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true,
#   and a step prints the title of a wiki page with printf, which reads the

false_positive_forms.text: a variable of the env of the step that the script sets again in the last command of a pipeline after a shopt -s lastpipe whose option name the script does not write as a literal word (shopt -s "$o"): bash runs the last command of the pipeline in the shell that runs the pipeline, so after the pipeline the variable holds the value that the script sets, and the rule reads the variable as holding the value of the env

examples.name: lastpipe-not-literal.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issues, a job sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true
#   in its env; a step passes the title of the issue in the environment
#   variable T, turns lastpipe on with shopt -s and the option name in a
#   variable, sets T to a fixed word with read in the last command of a
#   pipeline, and prints T; a step comes after.
# reason: with lastpipe, bash runs the last command of the pipeline in the
#   shell that runs the pipeline, so T holds the fixed word when echo runs,
#   and the step does not print the title.
# cause: the rule follows lastpipe only after shopt -s lastpipe written as
#   literal words, so the rule reads T as holding the value of the env.
# attack: the attacker titles the issue ##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]$(id).
# attack-run-behavior: the step prints "issue: safe"; nothing is set.
on: issues
permissions: {}
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - env:
          T: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          o=lastpipe
          shopt -s "$o"
          echo safe | read -r T
          echo "issue: $T"

# situation: on comments on the diff, a step with
#   ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS prints the comment's body, in a job
#   that runs only when the head repository of the pull request is a fork.

#   is a fork. On a pull request from a branch of the repository, the head
#   repository is the repository itself, so in a repository that is not a
#   fork the job runs only for a review of a pull request from a fork. In
#   a public repository, the run of such a review has no secrets and a
#   token that only reads; in a private repository, the run has neither
#   secrets nor a token that writes unless the repository gives secrets or
#   a token that writes to the runs of pull requests from forks (the
#   undetected form fork-review).
# cause: the rule does not read whether the repository that runs the
#   workflow (not the head repository of the pull request) is a fork, and
#   reads the job as if the job ran for a review of a pull request from a
#   branch of the repository.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "::set-env name=NODE_OPTIONS::--require=/tmp/PWNED.js"
# attack-run-behavior: in a public repository that is not a fork, a review
#   of a pull request from a branch of the repository does not start the
#   job, as the head repository of such a pull request is the repository
#   itself; a review of a pull request from a fork starts the job with no
#   secrets and a token that only reads, so the value reaches no secret
#   and no token that writes.

jobs:
  a:
    if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
          B: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: echo "c=$B"
      - run: echo next

false_positive_forms.text: a value that an if compares with strings that the workflow writes in the if (strings compared by == with the value and joined by ||, or the strings of contains(fromJSON('[...]'), value)), where each string has only ASCII letters, digits, spaces, -, _, . and /, does not start with -, and has no - right after a space, where the rule reports the value although the if limits the value to those strings, because the rule does not read the if in one of three forms. (1) A reusable workflow or a composite action gets the value through an input, and the if of the calling job or the calling step compares the value. The rule reports the value in the file of the reusable workflow or the composite action. The value is harmless when the if of every caller of that file, inside and outside the repository, compares the value. (2) The if compares the value under one name, and the script writes the value under another name: for example, the if compares env.BODY, which the env of the step sets to ${{ github.event.comment.body }}, and the script writes ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; or the if compares ${{ github.head_ref }}, and the script writes ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}. The value is harmless when the two names hold the same value in the step; the rule does not check that the two names hold the same value. (3) The if of a step that uses an action compares a value that the with or the env of the same step holds. At the start of the job, the runner runs the pre step of each action from another repository whose action.yml has runs.pre, under the condition runs.pre-if of that action.yml and not under the if of the step. For the pre step, the runner evaluates the with and the env of the step, and the code of the pre step may read the inputs. The runner runs no pre step of a local action (./). The value is harmless when the action has no pre step, or when the code of the pre step does not read the value. In each form, the value is harmless only where the case of the letters does not change what the value names (the undetected form if-compared)

examples.text:
# situation: on issue_comment created, a step that has the comment's body in
#   env.BODY runs only when env.BODY is deploy, and the step
#   prints ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; the job sets
#   ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true, and another step of the job
#   runs after the step, as the rule requires.
# reason: the step's if compares env.BODY, which holds the comment's body,
#   with deploy, so in the step the body is deploy, ignoring the case of its
#   letters: the body has no character that the shell reads as code, no
#   line break, no word that starts with - and no workflow command.
# cause: the rule limits a value by an if only under the name that the if
#   compares: the if compares env.BODY, and the script writes
#   ${{ github.event.comment.body }}; the rule does not check that env.BODY
#   holds the comment's body.
# attack-value: github.event.comment.body = "##[set-env name=BASH_ENV;]./x.sh"
# attack-run-behavior: on GitHub, the step's if is false for such a body,
#   and the runner skips the step.
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
jobs:
  j:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS: true
    steps:
      - if: env.BODY == 'deploy'
        env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}"
      - run: echo next

false_positive_forms.text: a reusable workflow or a composite action when all of the following are true: the rule does not know all of the callers of the reusable workflow or the composite action; every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action (directly, or through another reusable workflow or composite action) is a workflow in the same repository; and the rule would report no finding of the finding kind if the rule read the reusable workflow or the composite action only on the events on which the workflows in the same repository run the reusable workflow or the composite action (for example, every workflow that runs the reusable workflow or the composite action runs only on push). When the rule does not know all of the callers, the rule can read the reusable workflow or the composite action on every event (the worst case). For example, the rule does not know all of the callers when no caller is among the inputs; when the inputs are not the whole repository; for a composite action, when an input is excluded or cannot be read; when a caller names the reusable workflow or the composite action by a name of the form owner/repo/path@ref instead of by a ./ path, in which owner/repo is the repository that the --repo flag names, or is any repository when no --repo flag is given; when a step names the composite action by a ./ path, and either no checkout step runs before that step or the last checkout step before that step is not a plain checkout step (a plain checkout step has no ref input, no repository input and no path input); when a step inside a composite action names another composite action by a ./ path; or when the rule does not know all of the callers of a caller

false_positive_forms.text: a run of status, check_suite or check_run in a repository where no app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for a commit that the attacker of the finding writes: the facts that the finding kind asks are false (repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository). In two cases, the rule does not ask these facts, and reports the finding whatever the values of the facts are. First, a workflow whose on has an event other than status, check_suite and check_run: the rule decides whether to ask the facts from the events of on alone, and does not read the if of the job, so the rule does not ask the facts even when the if of the job lets the job run only on status, check_suite or check_run. Second, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action (an action has no on) that only workflows on status, check_suite or check_run call: the rule asks the facts only of a workflow whose on has only events among these three, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so the rule reports a finding in the reusable workflow or the action whatever the values of the facts are

examples.name: app-checks-unasked.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on status and push, the job runs only on status (its if), and
#   writes the message of the commit of the status
#   (github.event.commit.commit.message) where the rule reads it.
# reason: no app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run
#   for a commit whose message an attacker writes in the repository: no app
#   makes one for a commit of a pull request from a fork
#   (repo.fork-pr-app-checks false), and no app makes one for a commit that
#   the merge of a pull request puts in a branch
#   (repo.merge-commit-app-checks false), so no run of status has such a
#   commit, and the job does not run on push.
# cause: the rule asks repo.fork-pr-app-checks and
#   repo.merge-commit-app-checks only of a workflow whose on has no event

# attack-value: github.event.commit.commit.message = "::set-env name=BASH_ENV::/tmp/x.sh"

permissions: {}
jobs:

      - run: echo "${{ github.event.commit.commit.message }}"
      - run: echo next

false_positive_forms.text: a job that runs only for a pull request from a fork (pull_request, pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment, with an if that compares github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork with true, or github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name with github.repository), in a repository that is not a fork, in a run of the linter that adds variables-writer or secrets-writer: the rule reads each value of vars and secrets as a value that the attacker writes in every workflow run of the event; the workflow run for a pull request from a fork has no secret except GITHUB_TOKEN and a GITHUB_TOKEN that only reads, unless the settings of a private repository send secrets or a GITHUB_TOKEN that writes to such workflow runs (the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens), and the attacker who writes a variable or a secret gets nothing from the job that the author of the pull request does not get from the code of the pull request. A job with no such if, in a repository where every pull request comes from a fork, is a false positive in the same way. The linter does not tell a workflow run for a pull request from a fork from a workflow run for a pull request from a branch of the repository. A fix: the linter splits the workflow runs of the three events into the runs for a pull request from a fork and the runs for a pull request from a branch of the repository, reads the comparisons of the if with the fork in each, and counts a run for a pull request from a fork only when the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets or repo.fork-pr-write-tokens say that the run gets secrets or a GITHUB_TOKEN that writes. A job with no such if keeps the runs for a pull request from a branch of the repository, and the finding stays. A fact of the rulesets of the repository (a ruleset with the rule Restrict creations on every branch and no actor that may bypass the ruleset) could say that no new branch, and so no pull request from a new branch, can be made, and remove a part of the false positives of a job with no such if; the actors that may bypass a ruleset, the branches made before the ruleset and the names of branches outside the patterns of the ruleset remain. The fix is not observed on GitHub

#   of the pull request is a fork writes values of vars and secrets where
#   the rule reads a value that the attacker writes.
# reason: in a run of the linter that adds variables-writer or
#   secrets-writer, the rule reads each value of vars and secrets as a
#   value that the attacker writes. In a repository that is not a fork,
#   the job runs only for a pull request from a fork, and such a workflow
#   run has no secret except GITHUB_TOKEN and a GITHUB_TOKEN that only
#   reads, unless the settings of a private repository send secrets or a
#   GITHUB_TOKEN that writes to the workflow runs for pull requests from
#   forks (the facts repo.fork-pr-secrets and repo.fork-pr-write-tokens).
#   The attacker who writes a variable or a secret gets nothing from the
#   job that the author of the pull request does not get from the code of
#   the pull request.
# cause: the rule counts every workflow run of the event pull_request, and
#   does not tell a workflow run for a pull request from a fork from a
#   workflow run for a pull request from a branch of the repository.
# attack-value: vars.RELEASE_TAG = "::add-path::/tmp/PWNED"

permissions: {}

      - env:

          NOTE: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_NOTE }}
        run: |
          echo "tag: $TAG"
          echo "note: $NOTE"
          echo "${{ runner.os }}"
      - run: echo next

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:

    if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm ci

undetected_forms.text: a job that runs only on pull_request, in one of two cases. In the first case, only the pull requests of the repository run the workflow: the author of a pull request can change the workflow itself, so the run of the job gives the author what the run has (read-only from a fork, or what a private repository sends to the runs of pull requests from forks: secrets, a token that writes) without the flaw of the rule, and the flaw of the rule adds nothing to what the author gets. In the second case, a ruleset of the organization or the enterprise runs the workflow on the pull requests of its other repositories (Require workflows to pass before merging, of GitHub Enterprise): the author of such a pull request cannot change the workflow, and whether the run has more than the pull_request workflow of the author would get (the token, secrets) is known from GitHub's documentation only, as no such run was observed; making a required check pass is outside the threat model of the rule. The workflow does not say which case holds, and the rule does not read which case holds

#   workflow that runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal
#   access token and adds the label test to a pull request that changes a file
#   under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when
#   contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) is true, and the job
#   checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.
# reason: the workflow that runs actions/labeler adds the label to the pull
#   request of the attacker, so no person approves the run before the label
#   starts the run.
# cause: the run of the linter reads only the files that it names, so the rule
#   does not read the workflow that runs actions/labeler.
# attack-value: the file package.json in the pull request's head = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
# attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
#   changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler
#   adds the label test, which starts labeled.yml, and
#   contains('safe-to-test', 'test') is true, the checkout fetches the head of
#   the pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull
#   request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]
jobs:
  build:
    if: contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4.2.2
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm ci

notes.situation: the linter is given labeled.yml alone; the repository also has a workflow that runs actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal access token and adds the label test to a pull request that changes a file under site/; labeled.yml runs on pull_request_target on labeled when contains('safe-to-test', github.event.label.name) is true, and the job checks out the head of the pull request and runs npm ci.

attack_value.carrier: the file package.json in the pull request's head

notes.attack_run_behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that changes a file under site/ and the files of the attack; actions/labeler adds the label test, which starts labeled.yml, and contains('safe-to-test', 'test') is true, the checkout fetches the head of the pull request, and npm ci runs the preinstall script of the pull request, which prints PWNED, with the secrets of the repository.

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

false_positive_forms.text: a run that the Actions policies of the repository block, in four cases where the rule does not take the policies into account. First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. Second, an actor rule that does not allow the account of the attacker (for example, an actor rule that allows only the repository roles with write access): repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of a workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run by the account that starts the run, so the fact cannot tell what an actor rule blocks. Third, a workflow whose on has pull_request_target and another event: the rule does not ask repo.pull-request-target-allowed for such a workflow, because a run on the other event can reach the job. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive. Fourth, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action that only workflows on pull_request_target call: the rule asks repo.pull-request-target-allowed only of a workflow whose on has pull_request_target, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so a finding in the reusable workflow or the action is still reported when the policies block the runs of every caller

preconditions.text: an app outside GitHub Actions, such as an outside CI, makes a commit status or a check run for a commit whose message an attacker writes (a commit of a pull request from a fork, or a commit that merges a pull request; the message of a commit that merges a pull request can have the title of the pull request), and the commit status or the check run starts a run of status, check_suite or check_run, which runs the workflow of the default branch, whatever branch the commit is on. The payload of a run of any of the three events has the SHA of the commit, and the payload of a run of status or check_suite also has the message, the author name and the committer name of the commit. A finding of a workflow whose on has only events among status, check_suite and check_run (one, two or all three) holds only when the fact of the commit is true: repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, and repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository or that a merge queue of the repository makes. A finding kind asks the fact of each kind of commit that its attackers write; the finding of a finding kind that asks both facts holds when at least one of the two facts is true. The rule does not ask these facts of a workflow whose on has another event too, and reports the finding of such a workflow whatever the values of the facts are. The finding is conditional when no file of facts and no --fact answers the facts

name: Build Docs Artefacts

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  build-and-greet:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'documentation'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout PR code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.number }}/merge
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: 'pages/package-lock.json'

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: pages
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build Docusaurus artifacts
        working-directory: pages
        run: npm run build

      - name: Post Welcome Comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const gifUrl = "https://media.giphy.com/media/KJ1f5iTl4Oo7u/giphy.gif";

            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: `👋 **Thanks for contributing to our documentation!**\n\nThe artifacts have been successfully built for this pull request.\n\n![Thank You GIF](${gifUrl})`
            })

# situation: the workflows of fooagen/zellij
#   (https://github.com/fooagen/zellij/tree/039c8d5962dd341bb58dd7dcd09eb2cf7389ac7a/.github).
#   For the example, build-artefacts.yaml is named labeled.yml and the
#   directory docs is named pages. In the workflows, labeler.yaml runs
#   actions/labeler on pull_request_target with a personal access token; the
#   configuration .github/labeler.yaml adds the label documentation to a pull
#   request that changes a Markdown file under pages/ (under one
#   changed-files, the configuration has two conditions, and actions/labeler
#   adds the label when either condition holds); labeled.yml runs on
#   pull_request_target on labeled when the label is documentation, checks out
#   the merge commit of the pull request with actions/checkout@v4, and runs
#   npm ci and npm run build in pages. On 2026-04-25 a pull request from a
#   fork that changed a .mdx file and pages/package.json got the label, and
#   the labeled run succeeded, before actions/checkout refused the code of a
#   fork on pull_request_target.
# reason: actions/checkout@v4 refuses refs/pull/<n>/merge of a pull request
#   from a fork on pull_request_target, so the checkout fails and no code of
#   the pull request runs.
# attack-value: the file pages/package.json in the pull request's merge commit = "{\"scripts\":{\"preinstall\":\"echo PWNED\"}}"
# attack-run-behavior: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork that
#   changes a .mdx file under pages/ and pages/package.json; actions/labeler
#   adds the label documentation, which starts labeled.yml, and the checkout
#   fails, so npm ci does not run.
name: Build Docs Artefacts

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [labeled]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  build-and-greet:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'documentation'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout PR code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.number }}/merge

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: 'pages/package-lock.json'

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: pages
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build Docusaurus artifacts
        working-directory: pages
        run: npm run build

      - name: Post Welcome Comment
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const gifUrl = "https://media.giphy.com/media/KJ1f5iTl4Oo7u/giphy.gif";

            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: `👋 **Thanks for contributing to our documentation!**\n\nThe artifacts have been successfully built for this pull request.\n\n![Thank You GIF](${gifUrl})`
            })

examples.text:
# situation: on workflow_run, the artifact of the run workflow_run follows
#   is downloaded into the workspace, and ./build.sh runs.
# reason: another rule's: the pull request's code comes in an artifact,
#   which artifact-poisoning reports.
# cause: the rule reads checkouts by actions/checkout, not downloads.
# attack-value: the file build.sh in the artifact of the pull request's ci run = "#!/bin/sh\necho PWNED\n"
# attack-run-behavior: the fork's pull request changes ci so its run uploads
#   build.sh; when that run completes, the download takes its artifact by
#   workflow_run.id with the token into the workspace, and ./build.sh runs
#   it, with this run's token and the base repository's secrets.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ci]
    types: [completed]
permissions: {actions: read}
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4

examples.name: checkout-ref-unknown.ghsl-2025-082.yml
examples.text:
# situation: on issue_comment, when the comment is /benchmarks, a run step
#   writes the name of the head branch of the pull request (gh pr view --json
#   headRefName) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, actions/checkout@v4 checks out that name
#   with the input repository not set, and a later step uses the local action
#   ./.github/actions/setup-nx. This is performance.yml of ag-grid/ag-grid
#   (commit 7d969b0a0374d1e0ce690ae1159ceb7b6091f325, the commit of the
#   advisory's links; performance.yml at that commit is the same blob as at
#   6b5582325b9eb843e2d566aff8b530eaee5996ad; lines 3-5, 43-52, 72-95 and
#   115-119). The triggers workflow_dispatch and schedule, the env of the
#   workflow except PR_ID, the step Notify start and the test of its output in
#   the script (lines 56-70 and 80), the two echo lines of the script (lines
#   78-79), the branches of the script for the other events (lines 83-89), and
#   the steps between the step Checkout and the step Setup and after the step
#   Setup are left out; the if of the job keeps only its part for issue_comment,
#   and PR_ID keeps only github.event.issue.number.
# reason: the rule does not read what the run step writes to the output, so
#   the ref is not known. The advisory says that the code of the pull request
#   runs; the source of actions/checkout does not fetch the code of a pull
#   request from a fork in this form. With the input repository not set,
#   actions/checkout fetches from the repository of the run (src/input-helper.ts
#   of v4.4.0, 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262, lines 22-24), and for a
#   ref that is not a SHA and does not start with refs/, actions/checkout
#   fetches only +refs/heads/<ref>* and +refs/tags/<ref>* (src/ref-helper.ts,
#   lines 106-111). The base repository has no branch of a fork: the base
#   repository has refs/pull/<number>/head and refs/pull/<number>/merge only
#   (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs on 2026-11-07). A run of the
#   same form on 2026-11-07 (actions/checkout@v4 resolved to 11d5960a) showed
#   two results: for a pull request from a fork whose branch name the base
#   repository does not have, the fetch failed (git exited with code 1) and the
#   later step found no file of the fork; for a pull request from a fork whose
#   branch has the name of a branch of the base repository, the checkout took
#   the branch of the base repository, not the commit of the fork. Two kinds of
#   names would reach the code of the fork, as actions/checkout takes a ref that
#   starts with refs/ as a full name of a ref and a ref of 40 hexadecimal digits
#   as a commit, but GitHub refused a push of a branch named refs/pull/32/head
#   ("Invalid branch or tag name") and of a branch named by the 40 hexadecimal
#   digits of a commit ("branch or tag names consisting of 40 or 64 hex
#   characters are not allowed"), on 2026-11-07. gh pr view --json headRefName
#   gives the name of the branch without its owner (cli/cli v2.76.1,
#   api/queries_pr.go line 37). So the checkout brings the code of a branch of
#   the base repository, to which only an account with write access to the
#   repository can push; if the rule read what the run step writes, the form
#   would be the one of the declaration branch-name-ref (a checkout of a name of
#   a branch, which brings no code of a fork). The timeline of the advisory says
#   how ag-grid fixed the workflow, by approval of the runs of pull requests
#   from forks: "2025-08-05: Issue fixed by requiring approval for external
#   forked PR"; in the form of this example, a pull request from a fork brings
#   no code, and a pull request from a branch of the base repository brings the
#   code of the branch.
# attack: the author of a pull request from a fork writes
#   .github/actions/setup-nx/action.yml in the head branch and comments
#   /benchmarks on the pull request.
# attack-run-behavior: gh pr view gives the name of the head branch, which is
#   in the fork; actions/checkout fetches +refs/heads/<name>* and
#   +refs/tags/<name>* from the base repository, which has no ref of the name,
#   and the fetch fails (git exits with code 1), so the step Setup does not run
#   the action.yml of the author.
# advisory: https://securitylab.github.com/advisories/GHSL-2025-082_ag-grid_ag-grid/
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
env:
  PR_ID: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  benchmark:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    if: github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.comment.body == '/benchmarks'
    steps:
      - name: Assign correct Branch name
        id: get-branch
        env:
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          echo "branch=$(gh pr view $PR_ID --repo $REPO --json headRefName --jq '.headRefName')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          ref: ${{ steps.get-branch.outputs.branch }}
      - name: Setup
        id: setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-nx
        with:
          cache_mode: rw

notes.situation: on issue_comment, when the comment is /benchmarks, a run step writes the name of the head branch of the pull request (gh pr view --json headRefName) to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, actions/checkout@v4 checks out that name with the input repository not set, and a later step uses the local action ./.github/actions/setup-nx. This is performance.yml of ag-grid/ag-grid (commit 7d969b0a0374d1e0ce690ae1159ceb7b6091f325, the commit of the advisory's links; performance.yml at that commit is the same blob as at 6b5582325b9eb843e2d566aff8b530eaee5996ad; lines 3-5, 43-52, 72-95 and 115-119). The triggers workflow_dispatch and schedule, the env of the workflow except PR_ID, the step Notify start and the test of its output in the script (lines 56-70 and 80), the two echo lines of the script (lines 78-79), the branches of the script for the other events (lines 83-89), and the steps between the step Checkout and the step Setup and after the step Setup are left out; the if of the job keeps only its part for issue_comment, and PR_ID keeps only github.event.issue.number.
notes.reason: the rule does not read what the run step writes to the output, so the ref is not known. The advisory says that the code of the pull request runs; the source of actions/checkout does not fetch the code of a pull request from a fork in this form. With the input repository not set, actions/checkout fetches from the repository of the run (src/input-helper.ts of v4.4.0, 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262, lines 22-24), and for a ref that is not a SHA and does not start with refs/, actions/checkout fetches only +refs/heads/<ref>* and +refs/tags/<ref>* (src/ref-helper.ts, lines 106-111). The base repository has no branch of a fork: the base repository has refs/pull/<number>/head and refs/pull/<number>/merge only (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs on 2026-11-07). A run of the same form on 2026-11-07 (actions/checkout@v4 resolved to 11d5960a) showed two results: for a pull request from a fork whose branch name the base repository does not have, the fetch failed (git exited with code 1) and the later step found no file of the fork; for a pull request from a fork whose branch has the name of a branch of the base repository, the checkout took the branch of the base repository, not the commit of the fork. Two kinds of names would reach the code of the fork, as actions/checkout takes a ref that starts with refs/ as a full name of a ref and a ref of 40 hexadecimal digits as a commit, but GitHub refused a push of a branch named refs/pull/32/head ("Invalid branch or tag name") and of a branch named by the 40 hexadecimal digits of a commit ("branch or tag names consisting of 40 or 64 hex characters are not allowed"), on 2026-11-07. gh pr view --json headRefName gives the name of the branch without its owner (cli/cli v2.76.1, api/queries_pr.go line 37). So the checkout brings the code of a branch of the base repository, to which only an account with write access to the repository can push; if the rule read what the run step writes, the form would be the one of the declaration branch-name-ref (a checkout of a name of a branch, which brings no code of a fork). The timeline of the advisory says how ag-grid fixed the workflow, by approval of the runs of pull requests from forks: "2025-08-05: Issue fixed by requiring approval for external forked PR"; in the form of this example, a pull request from a fork brings no code, and a pull request from a branch of the base repository brings the code of the branch.
notes.attack: the author of a pull request from a fork writes .github/actions/setup-nx/action.yml in the head branch and comments /benchmarks on the pull request.
notes.attack_run_behavior: gh pr view gives the name of the head branch, which is in the fork; actions/checkout fetches +refs/heads/<name>* and +refs/tags/<name>* from the base repository, which has no ref of the name, and the fetch fails (git exits with code 1), so the step Setup does not run the action.yml of the author.

#   request into pr, with the guard of actions/checkout taken away, and then
#   runs npm --prefix pr ci.
# reason: an actor rule of the Actions policies of the repository allows
#   only the repository roles with write access to trigger the workflow, so a
#   run that a pull request from an account without write access triggers
#   fails. GitHub's documents say that GitHub evaluates the policies before a
#   run, and that a run that a policy does not allow fails with an error; the
#   documents do not say whether a job of such a run starts before the run
#   fails, and the rule assumes that no job starts.
# cause: the rule does not take the actor rules of the Actions policies into
#   account: repo.pull-request-target-allowed is one value for all the runs of
#   the workflow file on pull_request_target, and an actor rule blocks a run
#   by the account that starts the run.
# attack-value: the file package.json in the head of the pull request = "{\"scripts\": {\"preinstall\": \"echo PWNED\"}}"
# attack-run-behavior: the account of the attacker is not an allowed actor,
#   so the run on pull_request_target fails with an error, and no job of the
#   run starts (the assumption of the reason), so npm never runs the
#   preinstall script.
name: policy
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
          path: pr
      - run: npm --prefix pr ci

false_positive_forms.text: a run of status, check_suite or check_run in a repository where no app outside GitHub Actions makes a commit status or a check run for a commit that the attacker of the finding writes: the facts that the finding kind asks are false (repo.fork-pr-app-checks for a commit of a pull request from a fork, repo.merge-commit-app-checks for a commit that the merge of a pull request puts in a branch of the repository). In two cases, the rule does not ask these facts, and reports the finding whatever the values of the facts are. First, a workflow whose on has an event other than status, check_suite and check_run: the rule decides whether to ask the facts from the events of on alone, and does not read the if of the job, so the rule does not ask the facts even when the if of the job lets the job run only on status, check_suite or check_run. Second, a reusable workflow (on workflow_call) or an action (an action has no on) that only workflows on status, check_suite or check_run call: the rule asks the facts only of a workflow whose on has only events among these three, not of the reusable workflow or the action, so the rule reports a finding in the reusable workflow or the action whatever the values of the facts are

rules.problem: a privileged job that a person approves checks out the code of a pull request by what its author can move, so a push after the approval runs code no one approved
rules.expected: a job that a person approves checks out the commit the approval saw (github.event.pull_request.head.sha)

actors.via: pushes to the pull request's branch after a maintainer approves it

preconditions.text: a reusable workflow or a composite action that is among the inputs runs on the events of the callers of the workflow or the action, whoever the callers are; when the inputs are the whole repository and hold every caller of the workflow or the action, the rule reads the workflow or the action on the events of the callers, with the values that the callers give under with

the job runs on pull_request_target, workflow_run or issue_comment, which a pull request from a fork or a comment triggers, with the repository's secrets and a token that may write; not pull_request, pull_request_review or pull_request_review_comment: from a fork they run the pull request's own workflow, which its author can change, read-only unless a private repository sends them secrets or a token that writes; from a branch of the repository, the code checked out is of one who can write

observed.what: a pull request from a fork ran pull_request_target, workflow_run after its pull_request, and issue_comment on a comment, each with the repository's secret and a token that created a ref

preconditions.text: the checkout brings the pull request's code: its head or merge commit, refs/pull/<n>/head or merge, or the fork as the repository; a branch's name with the base repository brings the base's branch of that name, if any

observed.what: a checkout of the fork's head SHA, refs/pull/<n>/head and refs/pull/<n>/merge from the base repository brought the fork's commit and the merge commit; one of head.ref with the base repository failed, as the base had no such branch

preconditions.text: on pull_request_target and workflow_run, the release of actions/checkout does not refuse a fork's code: v1, a release before the guard (v2.8.0, v3.7.0, v4.4.0, v5.1.0, v6.1.0, v7.0.0), a commit pinned before it, or allow-unsafe-pr-checkout set; issue_comment is not guarded

observed.what: v7.0.1 and the major tag v4 refused the fork's head SHA and refs/pull/<n>/head on pull_request_target and workflow_run, and allowed them with allow-unsafe-pr-checkout; v4.2.2 pinned by its SHA fetched them; on issue_comment v7.0.1 fetched refs/pull/<n>/head

preconditions.text: a person approves the run: a job that runs only on pull_request_target with the activity type labeled, whose label needs a credential with write access to the permission Issues or Pull requests, which the credential premise assumes no attacker holds, and no workflow of the same repository runs actions/labeler that adds the label to the pull request of an attacker with a token other than the GITHUB_TOKEN; or a job whose environment has required reviewers (repo.environment-protected)
the checkout fetches what the author moves: refs/pull/<n>/head or merge, or a branch of the fork; github.event.pull_request.head.sha is the head when the label was added

observed.what: a commit pushed after the label, while the labeled run waited, was fetched by refs/pull/<n>/head; github.event.pull_request.head.sha fetched the head of the time of the label; the push ran no labeled run

finding_kinds.detected: {uses} checks out {checkout_ref} on {pr_code_on} after {approval}, and {checkout_ref} can move
finding_kinds.consequence: the author pushes after the approval, and the job runs code no one approved with its secrets and its token
finding_kinds.remedy: check out the commit the approval saw: github.event.pull_request.head.sha

metrics.reason: the attacker opens a pull request from a fork, or comments on one, over the network
a change of a script, a build file or a package manifest of the pull request is all it takes

the push must come after the approval and before a checkout fetches the ref: in the run itself (the time from the label to the step, seconds to minutes), or before a re-run of the run, which a credential with write access to the permission Actions may start within 30 days, such as the credential of an attacker whose only write access is to the permission Actions, and which runs with the payload of the approval, so that a label taken off since still lets the job run (observed on 2026-09-28)
nothing of the repository is needed
a maintainer adds the label, or approves the environment, after looking at the pull request
the code reads the job's secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN
with the job's token the code can push, and write releases and packages
the code can fail or stop the job
the secrets open what is past the job: clouds, registries, other repositories
what the job publishes reaches those who use it; in the tj-actions incident a stolen token of this kind led to moved tags
nothing past the job is made unavailable by this as such

# situation: a composite action with no caller among the files that the
#   linter reads; when the event is pull_request_target labeled with the label
#   safe, a step checks out refs/pull/<n>/head and the next step runs npm ci.
# reason: with no caller among the files that the linter reads, the rule
#   reads the action on every event an attacker triggers, pull_request_target
#   labeled among the events. The label is the approval, but
#   refs/pull/<n>/head names the head of the pull request when the checkout
#   fetches the head, not the commit that was labelled, so a push between the
#   label and the fetch is what npm ci runs.
# attack: after a maintainer reads the pull request and adds the label safe,
#   the author of the pull request pushes to the branch of the fork a commit
#   whose package.json has a preinstall that prints PWNED, before the checkout
#   fetches.
# attack-run-behavior: the labeled run checks out refs/pull/<n>/head, which
#   GitHub has moved to the pushed commit, and npm ci runs the preinstall,
#   with the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repository in .git/config and the
#   secrets that the job of a workflow that calls the action gives the steps.
name: test
description: test the labelled pull request
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'safe'
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head
        allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true
    - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'safe'
      run: npm ci
      shell: bash

First, an event policy that blocks an event of the attackers other than pull_request_target (such as issue_comment) in a workflow whose on has that event: the rules ask a fact only for pull_request_target. When the if of the job is false on the other event, so that the job runs only on pull_request_target, and a policy blocks pull_request_target, the finding is a false positive.   build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - run: echo built
  disabled:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/cache@v4

          path: ~/.cache
          key: cache-${{ github.sha }}

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache
          key: cache-${{ github.sha }}

notes.reason: if GitHub checks the image of a Docker container action with the setting, GitHub fails the job that uses the action.

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.name: remote-callee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/allowed-actions-unanswered, whose content is
#   the workflow of the true positive unstarted-run (unstarted-run.yml) of
#   the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
#   unstarted-run.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact
#   workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
#   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
#   the reusable workflow.
# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
#   the answer of workflow.definition.
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/allowed-actions-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

notes.situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of the repository example-org/allowed-actions-unanswered, whose content is the workflow of the true positive unstarted-run (unstarted-run.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of unstarted-run.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read the reusable workflow.
notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.

examples.name: lockfile-sha.yml
examples.text:

#   and locks actions/cache@v4 to the commit 0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830, and the setting of

#   actions/cache@v4.
# reason: GitHub compares a locked uses by the commit SHA of the lockfile,
#   so the pattern allows the uses, and GitHub starts the run.
# cause: the rule does not read the lockfile, and compares the uses as
#   written.

permissions: {}

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache
          key: cache-${{ github.sha }}

quality_rules.problem: a uses names an action or a reusable workflow of a repository that is archived
quality_rules.expected: every uses that names an action or a reusable workflow of another repository names one of a repository that is not archived

finding_kinds.detected: {uses} names {repo}, a repository that is archived
finding_kinds.consequence: an archived repository is read-only and is no longer maintained: when an error or a vulnerability is found in the action or the reusable workflow, the repository gets no fixed version, and the runner still runs the version that the uses names (the rule known-vulnerable-actions of this linter reports an advisory of the GitHub Advisory Database about the action)
finding_kinds.remedy: replace the action or the reusable workflow with one that is maintained, or fork the repository, maintain the fork, and point the uses to the fork

quality_rules.problem: a step saves under a new key the content of a cache that restore-keys restored from another key, so the content of the older caches stays in each new cache
quality_rules.expected: a cache is saved only by a run in which restore-keys restored no older cache

finding_kinds.detected: the step may save under a new key the content of an older cache that restore-keys restored; the events on which the step may save: {saves_on}
finding_kinds.consequence: the content of the older caches stays in each new cache, so the new cache grows and takes longer to restore and to save; when the caches of the repository pass the cache limit, GitHub deletes the caches used least recently
finding_kinds.remedy: save the cache only in runs in which restore-keys restores no older cache (for example, a push run that builds without a restore), or remove restore-keys from the step

# situation: the example "Always save cache" of the README of
#   actions/cache/save: restore by an exact key, and save under the key that

        id: cache-prime-numbers-restore
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v5
        with:
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-prime-numbers
          path: |
            path/to/dependencies
            some/other/dependencies

        id: cache-prime-numbers-save
        if: always() && steps.cache-prime-numbers-restore.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v5
        with:
          key: ${{ steps.cache-prime-numbers-restore.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
          path: |
            path/to/dependencies
            some/other/dependencies

quality_rules.problem: an if has text outside its ${{ }} (white space counts as text in an action.yml, not in a workflow), or more than one ${{ }}, and GitHub reads such an if as a string, which is true whatever the expressions in the if give
quality_rules.expected: every if of a job or a step is one ${{ }}, with at most white space around the ${{ }} in a workflow and nothing around the ${{ }} in an action.yml, or a condition written without ${{ }}, in a workflow and in an action.yml

finding_kinds.detected: the if {condition} has text outside its ${{ }} (in an action.yml, a space or a line break counts as text too), or more than one ${{ }}, so GitHub reads the if as a string
finding_kinds.consequence: GitHub joins the text and the values of the expressions into one string; the string is not empty, so the string is true whatever the expressions give. When no ${{ }} of the if calls a status function (always(), cancelled(), failure() or success()), GitHub adds success() && before the string, and the job or the step runs only when the jobs or the steps before the job or the step succeeded. When a ${{ }} calls a status function, even success(), GitHub adds nothing, the if is the string alone, and the job or the step runs after a failure too. When the if is written to keep an attacker from running the job or the step, the if does not stop the attacker: the rules of this linter that evaluate the if in the runs of an attacker read the if as true, as GitHub does, and read the job or the step as when the job or the step has no if: for example, dangerous-triggers reports a job that runs on an event of the attacker with secrets or a token that writes. What the attacker gets comes from what the job or the step does, not from the if alone
finding_kinds.remedy: write the whole condition in one ${{ }}, such as ${{ a && b }}, or write the condition without ${{ }}, such as a && b; both forms work in a workflow and in an action.yml. In an action.yml, write nothing around the ${{ }}: no space, and no block scalar (if: |), which keeps a line break after the ${{ }}
