true_positives.name: mixed-text.yml
true_positives.text:
# situation: the job deploy has an if of two ${{ }} joined by && outside
#   them, meant to run the job only for a push to main.
# reason: GitHub reads the if as the string "true && false" or "false &&
#   false", which is not empty and so true: the job runs for every push and
#   every pull request of every branch.
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }} && ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh

notes.situation: the job deploy has an if of two ${{ }} joined by && outside them, meant to run the job only for a push to main.
notes.reason: GitHub reads the if as the string "true && false" or "false && false", which is not empty and so true: the job runs for every push and every pull request of every branch.

true_negatives.name: mixed-text.block.yml
true_negatives.text:
# situation: a step of a workflow has an if written as a block scalar
#   (if: |), which keeps a line break after the ${{ }}.
# reason: GitHub drops the white space around the one ${{ }} of an if of a
#   workflow and reads the if as the expression: the step runs only for a
#   push.
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - if: |
          ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
        run: make release

notes.situation: a step of a workflow has an if written as a block scalar (if: |), which keeps a line break after the ${{ }}.
notes.reason: GitHub drops the white space around the one ${{ }} of an if of a workflow and reads the if as the expression: the step runs only for a push.

true_negatives.name: mixed-text.yml
true_negatives.text:
# situation: the job deploy has its whole condition in one ${{ }}, and the
#   step has its condition without ${{ }}.
# reason: GitHub reads both ifs as expressions: the job runs only for a push
#   to main, and the step only when the event is not pull_request.
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push' }}
    steps:
      - if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: ./deploy.sh

notes.situation: the job deploy has its whole condition in one ${{ }}, and the step has its condition without ${{ }}.
notes.reason: GitHub reads both ifs as expressions: the job runs only for a push to main, and the step only when the event is not pull_request.

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.name: remote-callee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/cond-unanswered, whose content is the
#   workflow of the true positive mixed-text (mixed-text.yml) of the rule,
#   with on: workflow_call in place of the on of mixed-text.yml. The linter
#   has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
#   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
#   the reusable workflow.
# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
#   the answer of workflow.definition.
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/cond-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

notes.situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of the repository example-org/cond-unanswered, whose content is the workflow of the true positive mixed-text (mixed-text.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of mixed-text.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read the reusable workflow.
notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.

quality_rules.problem: no update tool keeps the uses of a workflow or an action metadata file current: no entry of Dependabot version updates reads the file, and Renovate does not update the uses (the rule keeps the name of the rule of sisakulint, and reads the configuration of Renovate too)
quality_rules.expected: every file whose uses name an action of another repository or a reusable workflow of another repository by a commit SHA or a version is a file that an entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions makes Dependabot read, or a file whose every such uses Renovate updates

finding_kinds.detected: no update tool updates {uses} and every other such uses of the same file, if there are any: no entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions lists {directory}, the directory that an entry would have to list for Dependabot to read the file, with version updates enabled (an entry whose open-pull-requests-limit is 0 does not count), and no Renovate configuration in the repository updates the file
finding_kinds.consequence: when a new version of an action or a reusable workflow is released, no pull request updates the uses; a uses pinned to a commit SHA never gets a Dependabot alert or a security update, whatever the configuration, so version updates are the only updates of such a uses, and without them the workflow keeps running the old commit until a person changes the uses
finding_kinds.remedy: create .github/dependabot.yml with version: 2 if the repository has none, and add to the updates of .github/dependabot.yml an entry with package-ecosystem: github-actions whose key directory: or key directories: lists the directory named in the finding; or configure Renovate to update the file

true_positives.name: no-update-tool.yml
true_positives.text:
# situation: a workflow pins actions/checkout to a commit SHA and uses
#   actions/setup-node by a tag, and the repository has no
#   .github/dependabot.yml and no configuration file of Renovate.
# reason: no update tool opens a pull request when a new version of either
#   action is released; the action pinned to a SHA gets no Dependabot alert
#   either, so the workflow keeps running the old commit.
on: push
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

notes.situation: a workflow pins actions/checkout to a commit SHA and uses actions/setup-node by a tag, and the repository has no .github/dependabot.yml and no configuration file of Renovate.
notes.reason: no update tool opens a pull request when a new version of either action is released; the action pinned to a SHA gets no Dependabot alert either, so the workflow keeps running the old commit.

true_negatives.name: no-update-tool.dependabot.yml
true_negatives.text:
# situation: the form of on-keyday/brgen (pull request 359,
#   https://github.com/on-keyday/brgen/pull/359, whose base commit
#   ef4654f7de65e8b44326906e27fc658be996b246 has a .github/dependabot.yml
#   with package-ecosystem github-actions and directory /): a workflow pins
#   actions/setup-node to a commit SHA with no comment on the line.
# reason: Dependabot version updates read the workflows under
#   .github/workflows for that entry, and Dependabot opened the pull request
#   that moved this SHA to the commit of v6.4.0, though the line had no
#   comment.
on: push
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@53b83947a5a98c8d113130e565377fae1a50d02f
        with:
          node-version: "23.11"

notes.situation: the form of on-keyday/brgen (pull request 359, https://github.com/on-keyday/brgen/pull/359, whose base commit ef4654f7de65e8b44326906e27fc658be996b246 has a .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions and directory /): a workflow pins actions/setup-node to a commit SHA with no comment on the line.
notes.reason: Dependabot version updates read the workflows under .github/workflows for that entry, and Dependabot opened the pull request that moved this SHA to the commit of v6.4.0, though the line had no comment.

finding_kinds.detected: Renovate updates the file, but does not update {uses} and every other uses of the same file that is pinned to a commit SHA without a version comment, if there are any; and no entry of .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions lists {directory}, the directory that an entry would have to list for Dependabot to read the file, with version updates enabled (an entry whose open-pull-requests-limit is 0 does not count)
finding_kinds.consequence: Renovate skips a uses pinned to a commit SHA when the line of the uses has no comment that names a version; a uses pinned to a commit SHA never gets a Dependabot alert or a security update, whatever the configuration, so when a new version is released, no pull request updates the uses, and the workflow keeps running the old commit until a person changes the uses
finding_kinds.remedy: write the version of the commit as a comment at the end of the line of each such uses, such as # v4.1.0, so that Renovate updates the uses; or create .github/dependabot.yml with version: 2 if the repository has none, and add to the updates of .github/dependabot.yml an entry with package-ecosystem: github-actions whose key directory: or key directories: lists the directory named in the finding

true_positives.name: unversioned-sha.yml
true_positives.text:
# situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate and no
#   .github/dependabot.yml, and a workflow pins actions/checkout to a commit
#   SHA with no comment on the line.
# reason: Renovate does not update a uses pinned to a SHA without a comment
#   that names the version (unversioned-reference), and Dependabot does not
#   read the file, so no pull request moves the SHA.

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

notes.situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate and no .github/dependabot.yml, and a workflow pins actions/checkout to a commit SHA with no comment on the line.
notes.reason: Renovate does not update a uses pinned to a SHA without a comment that names the version (unversioned-reference), and Dependabot does not read the file, so no pull request moves the SHA.

true_negatives.name: unversioned-sha.yml
true_negatives.text:
# situation: the repository has a configuration file of Renovate and no

undetected_forms.text: a uses whose ref is a tag that is neither a commit SHA nor a version (v and digits such as v4, digits with dots such as 1.2, or a date such as 20240101), such as stable: the rule does not report the uses, also in a repository with no update tool, since whether Dependabot or Renovate updates such a tag is not known

undetected_forms.text: a file of a fork: Dependabot version updates do not run on a fork that has .github/dependabot.yml until Dependabot version updates are enabled under Code security and analysis in the settings of the fork, and the rule does not read the settings

examples.name: fork.yml
examples.text:

#   the original repository) has an entry of package-ecosystem
#   github-actions, and the fork has not turned version updates on.
# reason: Dependabot version updates do not run on the fork, so no pull

undetected_forms.text: a repository where the update tool does not run: Dependabot paused for a repository without activity, Dependabot turned off by an administrator or a policy of GitHub Enterprise Server, or a configuration file of Renovate in a repository where Renovate is not installed: the rule does not read whether the update tool runs

examples.text:

undetected_forms.text: a uses that Renovate does not read in the form the uses is written in, such as a uses in a flow mapping or in a scalar of several lines: Renovate reads the line of uses:, and the rule reads the uses as updated

examples.name: renovate-line-form.yml
examples.text:

undetected_forms.text: a uses written as ${{ }} around a string literal, such as ${{ 'actions/setup-node@v4' }} (not a folded scalar of YAML): the rule does not know whether the update tools read such a uses, and does not report the uses, also in a repository with no update tool

undetected_forms.text: a uses pinned to 8 to 39 hexadecimal digits, such as abcdef12, in a file that Renovate updates: Dependabot reads the ref as a commit SHA, Renovate does not (Renovate reads 40 or 64 digits, or 6 or 7), and whether Renovate updates such a ref is not known: the rule reads the uses as updated by Renovate

examples.name: hex-ref.yml
examples.text:

# reason: Renovate does not read eight digits as a commit SHA, so whether

undetected_forms.text: a uses of an action that the key ignore: of .github/dependabot.yml or a package rule of Renovate names: the update tool does not update the action, and the rule reads the file as updated

examples.name: ignored-dependency.yml
examples.text:

undetected_forms.text: a run on a branch that is not the default branch, whose .github/dependabot.yml is not on the default branch yet: Dependabot reads .github/dependabot.yml of the default branch, and the rule reads .github/dependabot.yml under --root

examples.name: default-branch.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a pull request adds .github/dependabot.yml with an entry of
#   package-ecosystem github-actions, and the linter runs on the branch of
#   the pull request.
# reason: until the pull request is merged, the default branch has no
#   .github/dependabot.yml, so Dependabot updates nothing.
# cause: the rule reads .github/dependabot.yml under --root, the files of

on: push

notes.situation: a pull request adds .github/dependabot.yml with an entry of package-ecosystem github-actions, and the linter runs on the branch of the pull request.
notes.reason: until the pull request is merged, the default branch has no .github/dependabot.yml, so Dependabot updates nothing.
notes.cause: the rule reads .github/dependabot.yml under --root, the files of the branch, not those of the default branch.

quality_rules.problem: a step of actions/dependency-review-action turns off a check of the action, or asks for a pull request comment that the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job cannot write
quality_rules.expected: the step checks vulnerabilities and the license policy written for the step, fails when a check finds a problem, and asks for a comment only when the job has pull-requests: write

finding_kinds.detected: the step asks to write the summary of the dependency review as a comment on the pull request, but the GITHUB_TOKEN of the job is not given pull-requests: write
finding_kinds.consequence: the comment is not written: the step warns and succeeds
finding_kinds.remedy: give the job pull-requests: write, or set comment-summary-in-pr to never

true_positives.text:
# situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with

#   writes permissions; the repository's default token is read-only

  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
        with:
          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure

notes.situation: a pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action with comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure, and neither the workflow nor the job writes permissions; the repository's default token is read-only (repo.default-token-write is false).

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.name: remote-callee.yml
examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/dependency-review-settings-unanswered, whose
#   content is the workflow of the true positive comment-without-permission
#   (comment-without-permission.default-token.yml) of the rule, with on:
#   workflow_call in place of the on of
#   comment-without-permission.default-token.yml. The linter has no answer
#   of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
#   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
#   the reusable workflow.
# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
#   the answer of workflow.definition.
on: pull_request
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/dependency-review-settings-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

notes.situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of the repository example-org/dependency-review-settings-unanswered, whose content is the workflow of the true positive comment-without-permission (comment-without-permission.default-token.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of comment-without-permission.default-token.yml. The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read the reusable workflow.
notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.

quality_rules.problem: the run script of a step prints to the log of the step, as ::name at the head of a line or ##[name anywhere in a line (such as ##[set-output name=x;]v), a workflow command that GitHub deprecated (set-output, save-state) or disabled (set-env, add-path)
quality_rules.expected: every run script that sets an output, state, an environment variable or the PATH writes to the environment files ($GITHUB_OUTPUT, $GITHUB_STATE, $GITHUB_ENV, $GITHUB_PATH) instead of printing a workflow command

finding_kinds.detected: the run script of the step prints the workflow command {command}, which GitHub deprecated
finding_kinds.consequence: the runner adds a warning to each run of the workflow that runs the step. GitHub planned to disable both commands on 2023-05-31, and the notice of 2023-07-24 postponed the date without a new date. For set-output: once GitHub disables set-output, the step sets no output. For save-state: only the post step of the same action reads the state, and a run script has no post step, so no step reads the state that a run script saves
finding_kinds.remedy: for set-output, write name=value to the file $GITHUB_OUTPUT; for a value of many lines, write the line name<<DELIM, the lines of the value and the line DELIM, where DELIM is a random text that the value does not contain. For save-state, remove the command, because no step reads the state that a run script saves

quality_rules.problem: an action.yml of the repository, or an action of another repository that a step uses, declares an older Node.js version than node24; an env sets a setting of the Node.js version of actions; or actions/setup-node sets up a Node.js version whose support ended
quality_rules.expected: every JavaScript action (an action whose runs.using names a Node.js version) declares runs.using: node24 or later; no env sets ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION or FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE20; and the node-version of actions/setup-node names a Node.js version that is still supported

finding_kinds.remedy: change runs.using to node24, and test the action on Node.js 24

examples.name: outside-other-path.yml

# situation: the first step uses actions/cache/restore at the tag v3; the
#   second step names actions/cache/restore by a full SHA, but its path goes
#   with .. above the root of the repository, into the directory where the
#   runner puts actions/cache at v3, and names the path save there.
# reason: the second step runs actions/cache/save at v3, whose runs.using
#   decides the Node.js version that the step asks for.
# cause: for the second step, the rule reads the action of the first step
#   (restore), not the action at the path of the second step (save).
on: push
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@v3
        with:
          path: build
          key: build
      - uses: actions/cache/restore/../../v3/save@0123456789012345678901234567890123456789
        with:
          path: build
          key: build

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

quality_rules.problem: a key of env has = in it, or names a variable that the runner writes in each step after the env of the step is set, with a value other than the value that the runner writes, so no step gets the variable with the name and the value as written
quality_rules.expected: every key of env is a name without =, and is a name that the runner does not write in each step, or is written with the value that the runner writes

finding_kinds.detected: the env key {name} has =, which no name of an environment variable can have, and the runner sets the variable {variable} instead, to a value made from the rest of the key and the value written
finding_kinds.consequence: no step gets a variable whose name is the key: the runner sets the variable named by the part of the key before its first = instead. For the key A=B with the value x, the value of A depends on where the key is written and where the step runs. For a key in the env of the workflow, a job or a step: a step on the runner gets A with the value B=x, and a step in the job's container gets A with the value B. For a key in container.env (the job's container) or in the env of a service container (services): the container gets A with the value B=x. For a key in runs.env of a Docker container action: the container of the action gets A with the value B
finding_kinds.remedy: rename the key to a name without =, the name that the step reads

quality_rules.problem: a ${{ }} that GitHub accepts in the file does not work when the workflow runs: the value of the ${{ }} has a type that the key of the ${{ }} does not take, a call of format(), case() or fromJSON() in the ${{ }} fails, the value of a ${{ }} in a text is an object or an array (the text of an if is the rule cond's, not this rule's), or the ${{ }} reads a configuration variable by a name that no level of GitHub can define
quality_rules.expected: every expression that is the whole value of a key (${{ x }} alone) gives a type that the key takes, every call of format(), case() and fromJSON() gets arguments that the function can use, and every expression written in a text (with other text, or with another ${{ }}, in the same value) gives a string, a number, a boolean or null; the whole text is a string, so the key of such a text takes a string; and every name read from vars is a name that GitHub lets a level define

finding_kinds.detected: the expression {expression} is written in a text, with other text or another expression in the same value, and the expression gives an object or an array
finding_kinds.consequence: GitHub writes the text Object in place of an object and the text Array in place of an array, not the content of the value, so the text does not hold the value
finding_kinds.remedy: write the property of the object that holds the value, such as github.event.pull_request.number in place of github.event.pull_request; or toJSON(...) of the value, which gives the value as JSON; or join(...) of an array, such as join(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, ', '). In a run script, put such an expression in env of the step and read the variable in the script, since a value that ${{ }} writes into a script becomes part of the code of the script (the rule code-injection reports a value of an attacker there)

finding_kinds.detected: the expression {expression} of {key} {error}
finding_kinds.consequence: the jobs that need a failed job do not run, and the run fails. For env of the workflow, every job of the workflow fails before the first step of the job runs. For env, the container, the services and defaults.run of a job, that job fails before the first step of that job runs. For the secrets that a job gives a called workflow, the jobs of the called workflow fail before their first steps run. For the outputs and environment.url of a job, that job fails after the steps of that job ran. For the value of an output of workflow_call, the jobs of the called workflow succeed, and the jobs that need the job that calls the workflow do not run
finding_kinds.remedy: write the expression so that the expression gives a value of a type that the place of the expression takes, and so that each function gets arguments that the function can use: fromJSON(...) turns a string such as 'true' or '5' into a boolean or a number; a property of an object whose value is a string, or toJSON(...) of the object, gives a string; format() needs an argument for each placeholder of its format string; each predicate of case() needs to be a boolean, such as a comparison; fromJSON() needs a string, not an object or an array

# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of
#   the repository example-org/missing-timeout-minutes-remote, which the
#   fact workflow.definition answers with the workflow of the true positive
#   job (job.yml) of the rule, with on: workflow_call in place of the on of
#   job.yml. The job passes its secrets with secrets: inherit. In the true
#   positive, a job builds on push and writes no timeout-minutes.
# reason: the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the
#   run of the calling job, so the reason of the true positive holds: GitHub
#   cancels a job after 360 minutes when timeout-minutes is not written, so
#   a build that stops making progress holds the runner for 360 minutes.
on: push
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/missing-timeout-minutes-remote/.github/workflows/w.yml@v1
    secrets: inherit

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of

# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from

permissions: {}
jobs:

The linter has no answer of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.

notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.

quality_rules.problem: a ${{ }} of a workflow reads a configuration variable (vars.<name>) as a value, or gives the configuration variable to fromJSON(), and no level (repository, organization, environment) defines the name: GitHub gives the empty string for the name and reports no error, so a misspelled name shows only in what the workflow run does
quality_rules.expected: every name that a ${{ }} reads from vars as a value, or gives to fromJSON(), is the name of a configuration variable defined at the repository level or the organization level (repo.configuration-variables), or defined at the environment level (repo.environment-configuration-variables) of an environment whose configuration variables the place of the ${{ }} reads

finding_kinds.detected: the expression {expression} reads the configuration variable {name} as a value, and no list of defined names that this run of the linter has (repo.configuration-variables, and repo.environment-configuration-variables of each environment whose configuration variables the place of the expression reads) has the name {name}
finding_kinds.consequence: GitHub gives the empty string for a configuration variable that no level (repository, organization, environment) defines, and GitHub reports no error, so the expression gives the empty string where the workflow expects the value of the configuration variable. A misspelled name shows only in what the workflow run does, such as an empty argument of a step
finding_kinds.remedy: define the configuration variable at the repository, organization or environment level, or correct the name in the expression; when the workflow reads a missing configuration variable on purpose as meaning that the setting is not given, write the default value after ||, such as vars.NAME || 'default'

finding_kinds.detected: the expression {expression} gives the configuration variable {name} to fromJSON(), and no list of defined names that this run of the linter has (repo.configuration-variables, and repo.environment-configuration-variables of each environment whose configuration variables the place of the expression reads) has the name {name}
finding_kinds.consequence: GitHub gives the empty string for a configuration variable that no level defines, and fromJSON() of the empty string fails, so the evaluation of the expression fails: when the expression is in a key of a step, the step fails; when the expression is in a key of a job, the job fails or does not start

undetected_forms.text: a reference whose place reads the configuration variables of an environment, when repo.environment-configuration-variables has no answer, or the answer absent, for the environment: in a key of a job, the environment of the job; in env, concurrency and on.workflow_call of the workflow, the environment of every job of the workflow (in a workflow run on GitHub, env of the workflow had the value of a name that only the environment level of the environment of the job defined; concurrency and on.workflow_call were not tried, and the rule takes the names of the environment of every job as defined for them, which can only miss a name). run-name of the workflow and the if and the name of a job read no environment. undetected_forms.text: a reference that the ${{ }} reads only as a boolean condition or in a comparison: an operand of || or && that is not the last, an operand of ! or of a comparison, an argument of contains(), startsWith() or endsWith(), a predicate of case(), or the whole of an if, such as if: vars.DEPOLY == 'true', where DEPOLY is a misspelling of the defined name DEPLOY. A workflow can leave a name undefined on purpose to turn a setting off, and the rule does not tell such a name from a misspelled one

examples.name: compared.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the step runs when the configuration variable DEPOLY is true,
#   and the repository level defines DEPLOY, not DEPOLY.
# reason: a todo: DEPOLY is likely a misspelling of DEPLOY, and the step
#   never runs; but a workflow can also leave a name undefined on purpose,
#   so that the step does not run.
# cause: the rule reports no reference that the expression reads only as a
#   truth or in a comparison.
on: push
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - if: vars.DEPOLY == 'true'
        run: ./deploy.sh

notes.situation: the step runs when the configuration variable DEPOLY is true, and the repository level defines DEPLOY, not DEPOLY.
notes.reason: a todo: DEPOLY is likely a misspelling of DEPLOY, and the step never runs; but a workflow can also leave a name undefined on purpose, so that the step does not run.
notes.cause: the rule reports no reference that the expression reads only as a truth or in a comparison.

undetected_forms.text: a reference whose name is not a literal, such as vars[matrix.name]: the rule does not compute the name

examples.name: dynamic-name.yml
examples.text:

#   EU_ENDPOINT and US_ENDPOINT, and the step reads vars[matrix.endpoint];
#   the repository level defines US_ENDPOINT only.

undetected_forms.text: a reference to a name that only the environment level defines, in a key that was not tried on GitHub: in runs-on, concurrency, strategy, timeout-minutes, continue-on-error, environment, container, services, defaults and outputs of a job, and in with and secrets of a job that calls a workflow, a name of the environment level of the environment of the job; in concurrency and on.workflow_call of the workflow, a name of the environment level of the environment of any job of the workflow. In a workflow run on GitHub, such a name was the empty string in run-name of the workflow and in the if and the name of the job, and had its value in env of the workflow and of the job and in the keys of the steps; in run-name and in the if and the name of a job, the rule does not take the names of the environment level as defined. In the keys that were not tried, the rule takes the names of the environment level as defined and reports nothing for the reference, though the name may be the empty string there

examples.name: environment-before-start.yml
examples.text:
# situation: runs-on reads the configuration variable RUNNER_LABEL, which
#   only the environment level of the environment production defines; the
#   job names production.
# reason: a todo (a fact): if GitHub reads runs-on before the names of the
#   environment level are seen, as it does for the if and the name of a
#   job, runs-on is empty and the job does not start; the authors of the
#   rule did not try runs-on.
# cause: the rule reads the environment level as defined in the keys of a
#   job that were not tried.
on: push
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ${{ vars.RUNNER_LABEL }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    environment: production
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh

notes.situation: runs-on reads the configuration variable RUNNER_LABEL, which only the environment level of the environment production defines; the job names production.
notes.reason: a todo (a fact): if GitHub reads runs-on before the names of the environment level are seen, as it does for the if and the name of a job, runs-on is empty and the job does not start; the authors of the rule did not try runs-on.
notes.cause: the rule reads the environment level as defined in the keys of a job that were not tried.

undetected_forms.text: a reference in a workflow that runs on workflow_call only, when none of the files given to the linter calls the workflow with ./ or $/ (a path in the repository of the workflow): GitHub uses the configuration variables of the repository of the caller, and only workflows of other repositories call the workflow

examples.name: remote-caller-only.yml
examples.text:
# situation: the workflow runs on workflow_call only, no workflow of the
#   repository calls it, and its step reads vars.PUBLISH_TARGET, which the
#   repository does not define.
# reason: a limitation: GitHub uses the configuration variables of the
#   repository of the caller, which another repository decides.
# cause: the rule compares only the names of the repository that the
#   linter checks.
on:
  workflow_call:
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - run: ./publish.sh "${{ vars.PUBLISH_TARGET }}"

notes.situation: the workflow runs on workflow_call only, no workflow of the repository calls it, and its step reads vars.PUBLISH_TARGET, which the repository does not define.
notes.reason: a limitation: GitHub uses the configuration variables of the repository of the caller, which another repository decides.
notes.cause: the rule compares only the names of the repository that the linter checks.

undetected_forms.text: a reference in a key that the rule does not read: a variable of strategy.matrix whose whole value is one ${{ }}, such as os: ${{ fromJSON(vars.OSES) }}, include or exclude of strategy.matrix whose whole value is one ${{ }}, a key of strategy.matrix written with a ${{ }}, the values of exclude of strategy.matrix, the options, ports and volumes of a container or a service, snapshot of a job, deployment of environment, group of a mapping of runs-on, and queue of concurrency. The rule reports nothing for such a reference. The rule reads the other values of strategy.matrix, such as the items of a list of a variable and the values of include

# situation: the matrix of the job reads its operating systems from the
#   configuration variable OSES with fromJSON(), and no level defines OSES.
# reason: a todo: fromJSON() of the empty string fails, so GitHub does not
#   start the job.
# cause: the rule does not read a variable of strategy.matrix whose value
#   is one ${{ }}.
on: push
permissions: {contents: read}
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

undetected_forms.text: a job or a step inside a reusable workflow of another repository (uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>) whose content the fact workflow.definition does not give. For every rule: a run that does not ask the fact (a run without --online and without the answer in --facts). For a quality rule, also: a run where the linter asked the fact and got no answer (an answer of unknown: the GitHub API did not give the file), and a call deeper than the 3 levels of reusable workflows that the linter reads, for which the linter does not ask the fact. The rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition. For a rule that is not a quality rule (a rule with a threat), the last two forms are the inconclusive kind remote-callee-unknown, not this form

examples.text:
# situation: a job calls the reusable workflow .github/workflows/w.yml of

#   place of the on of empty-value.misspelled.yml. The linter has no answer
#   of the fact workflow.definition for the reusable workflow.
# reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event
#   that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read
#   the reusable workflow.
# cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from
#   the answer of workflow.definition.
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  c:
    uses: example-org/unset-configuration-variable-unanswered/.github/workflows/w.yml@eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee

notes.reason: a todo (a fact): the jobs of a reusable workflow run on the event that started the run of the calling job, and the linter does not read the reusable workflow.
notes.cause: the rule reads a reusable workflow of another repository only from the answer of workflow.definition.

false_positive_forms.text: a name that the workflow reads on purpose as an optional setting, whose empty value the script of a run step puts a default value in place of, such as env: {X: '${{ vars.X }}'} and ${X:-default} in the script: the empty string is what the workflow expects for a missing setting, and the rule does not read the script

false_positive_forms.text: a name that the workflow reads on purpose as an optional setting and gives to an input of an action under with, when the code of the action reads an empty input as an input not given and uses a default value: the runner gives the empty string to the action, since the key is under with, and the code of the action decides what the empty string means

quality_rules.problem: a step's uses writes its owner, repository or path with parts that GitHub drops or resolves (empty parts such as // or a / before @, a part that is . or .., or, in a uses of another repository, a backslash, which GitHub reads as /), or with .. that goes above the root of the repository or of the workspace, so that the uses as written does not name the action that runs
quality_rules.expected: every uses names the action that runs as GitHub reads the uses: no empty part, no part that is . or .. (the ./ at the start of a local action stays), and / between the parts

finding_kinds.detected: the path of the uses {uses} goes with .. above the root of the repository that the uses names
finding_kinds.consequence: the runner puts each action that the job downloads in _actions/<owner>/<repo>/<ref> on the runner, and runs the action of the directory that the path names, outside the repository that the uses names. When another uses of the job, or of a composite action that the job uses, downloads an action into that directory, the step runs that action; when no uses does, the job fails before the steps of the job run. The ref after @ does not decide the code that runs. For a uses of another repository whose path stays in _actions, commit-sha reports, on this step, the ref of the action that runs when that ref is not a full commit SHA
finding_kinds.remedy: write a uses of the action that is meant to run, as owner/repo/path@ref of that action (/path only when the action is in a directory of the repository), without ..
